verdict.basis: The observed span (1939-1945) is fully contained within candidate DEU-1938-1945's period (1938-1945), and the wiki page explicitly documents this row as the single polity covering Nazi Germany's whole territorial rollercoaster (Anschluss through surrender), with a formal decision to DEFER splitting into sub-periods (1938-1939/1939-1942/1942-1945) because no polygon source exists for Greater Germany at peak wartime expansion (CShapes excludes wartime changes). The wiki's own staple-magnitude documentation (wheat ~4,122,500 t, sugar ~6,877,900 t for the whole Greater Germany span) is consistent in kind with this assertion's magnitudes (wheat median 2,370,000 t, rye median 4,975,000 t over 1939-1945) — both reflect the elevated, annexation-inflated production levels of the expanded Reich rather than Weimar-era levels, and the wiki itself flags that these magnitudes fluctuate across the expansion/contraction sub-phases without warranting a different polity under current sourcing constraints. Given the source only labels by ISO 'germany' without distinguishing sub-periods, and the WHEP wiki has already made and documented the deliberate choice to keep this as one polity pending a future composed-union polygon, routing the whole 1939-1945 span to DEU-1938-1945 is correct as-is; no existing alternative polity better matches this territory for any part of the span.

review.reason: Independently reviewed the assertion and the wiki page wiki/polities/deu-1938-1945.md. The observed span (1939-1945) is a subset of the candidate's 1938-1945 period, and the wiki explicitly documents a deliberate, well-reasoned decision to keep Nazi Germany as one polity across the Anschluss-to-surrender span, deferring a three-way split (expansion/peak/contraction) specifically because no polygon source captures wartime Greater Germany (CShapes excludes wartime changes by design). The wiki itself discusses and accepts magnitude fluctuation across sub-phases (elevated wheat/sugar levels during 1939-1942 annexation peak vs. Weimar baseline) as consistent with, not contradicting, the single-polity choice — the assertion's staple magnitudes (wheat ~2.37M t, rye ~4.98M t medians over 1939-1945) are plausible for the documented annexation-inflated Reich and do not present a magnitude-continuity red flag distinct from what the wiki already anticipates. No alternative existing polity better covers any part of this span given current sourcing constraints. I reach the same verdict (confirm) and the same target (DEU-1938-1945).

verdict.basis: The assertion routes FAOSTAT-era "Germany" agricultural data (1946-1949, wheat/potatoes/pulses etc., n=8 per staple) to DEU-1945-1949 "Allied-occupied Germany". The candidate's wiki page (wiki/polities/deu-1945-1949.md) explicitly documents that this entry was created for exactly this source: "The pre-1961 input data reports 'Germany' for 1946-1948, covering agricultural production across the occupation zones... Previously these 113 rows were unmatched." The polygon is the constructed union of both Western Allied zones (CShapes gwcode 260, Trizone) and the Soviet zone (gwcode 265), totaling 356,838 km² - i.e. combined all-zone Germany within Potsdam borders, not just West or just East. This matches the observed span (1946-1949) fully inside the candidate's 1945-1949 period, with no split needed. Neighbor segments show continuity: predecessor DEU-1938-1945 (Nazi Germany, whole territory) and successor DEU-1949-1990 ("Germany (divided, 1949-1990)", also a combined-zone polity per the polities database), both of which are similarly combined-territory entries, consistent with a source that keeps reporting unified German agricultural statistics across the occupation/division era rather than splitting by zone. Magnitudes (e.g. wheat ~1.55M ha, potatoes ~12.3M ha) are plausible for all of Germany at this scale, not a half-territory figure. No union/vintage/combined-reporting mismatch is evident; the routing correctly reflects the source's reporting territory.

The candidate wiki (wiki/polities/deu-1949-1990.md) explicitly documents that DEU-1949-1990 was created precisely for "pre-1961 agricultural input data" that reports undifferentiated "Germany" (FRG+GDR combined, union of CShapes gwcode 260+265, ~356,800 km²) for the 1949-1961 window, contrasted with companion rows F77 (GDR) and F78 (FRG) that exist for datasets which do distinguish the two states post-1961. The assertion's source ("juan"), years (1950-1960), and item profile (staple crop areas: wheat, rye, barley, oats, potatoes) match exactly the case the wiki describes as motivating this polity's creation. Magnitude continuity across the full DEU family (checked via sibling assertions germany|juan|1850-1866 through 1946-1949) shows a smooth, historically plausible decline in rye/wheat/barley/oats from the German Empire era through Weimar/Nazi Germany, Allied occupation (1945-1949), and into 1950-1960 -- consistent with reporting on the same post-Potsdam territory the whole time (no discontinuous jump that would indicate switching to FRG-alone or GDR-alone scope, both of which would be roughly half the observed magnitudes for wheat: FRG-alone wheat area in the 1950s was ~1.3-1.5M ha vs. the observed 2.628M ha here, which is far more consistent with combined FRG+GDR reporting). This confirms the source's reporting territory equals the candidate polity's whole-Germany (undivided reporting) territory for the entire observed 1950-1960 span.

The candidate wiki page (wiki/polities/fin-1940-2025.md) explicitly flags the risk (oq-continuation-war-territory): Finland briefly regained Karelia 1941-1944 during the Continuation War before losing it again at the September 1944 armistice, so the source could plausibly be reporting on a temporarily larger territory for 1941-1944. However, the raw juan crop-area series (barley, oats, wheat, in ha) shows no discontinuity at either the 1940 Moscow Treaty cession or the 1944 reoccupation/re-cession boundary: barley area is ~110-140k ha continuously from 1917 through 1960 with no jump; oats area declines smoothly and gradually from 472k ha (1939) to a trough of ~310k ha (1945) then recovers gradually through the late 1940s-1950s, a pattern consistent with wartime labor/input disruption and post-war recovery rather than a territorial step-change (reoccupying agriculturally significant Karelia in 1941-1944 would be expected to show an area increase, not the observed decrease). Wheat area shows the same smooth wartime dip-then-recovery pattern. This magnitude continuity indicates the source (likely official Finnish government/FAO-style annual statistics) was reporting on the settled post-1940/post-1944 Finnish administrative territory throughout 1941-1960, i.e. the same territory as candidate FIN-1940-2025, rather than switching to include the temporarily reoccupied Karelia. Confidence is medium rather than high because the wiki's own open question shows this exact ambiguity was anticipated and CShapes' handling of the 1941-1944 fluctuation is uncertain, and no year-by-year territorial ground-truth (only crop-area magnitudes) was available to rule out a masked/offsetting effect.

The IIA "Russian Federation" label for 1922-1940 (435 rows, rye median ~22M ha) routes to F228-1921-1940 (RSFSR/USSR 1921-1940), whose wiki page documents this row as covering the full USSR territory (RSFSR + Ukrainian SSR + Belorussian SSR + Transcaucasian SFSR from the December 1922 Union treaty) up to the pre-1940-annexation borders. The same source label maps continuously across all adjacent F228 sub-periods: Russian Empire 1905-1914 rye median ~25.9M ha, 1914-1917 ~22.2M ha, RSFSR 1918-1920 ~17M ha, this segment 1922-1940 ~22M ha, USSR 1940-1945 ~12M ha (wartime disruption). This is smooth magnitude continuity rather than a step-change that would signal a scope mismatch (e.g. RSFSR-only vs whole-USSR). It confirms the IIA source consistently reports on the full historical Russia/USSR territory at each period's own extent, matching exactly what the F228 chain's per-period polities represent, including this 1921-1940 USSR row. No union/empire-scope error, no combined-reporting issue, and no boundary-vintage mismatch.

The IIA label "russian federation" (iso rus) for years 1909-1914 routes to Russian Empire (1905-1914), whose wiki documents no territorial changes between the 1905 Treaty of Portsmouth cession and the 1914 WWI outbreak -- i.e. the observed span (1909-1914) falls entirely within a territorially stable period of the same polity. Staple magnitudes (rye ~25.9M ha, flax ~851k ha, cotton lint ~268k ha, tobacco ~78k ha) are plausible for the full Russian Empire's agricultural scale and show no implied step change. The neighbor segment for 1915-1917 correctly routes to the successor polity F228-1914-1917 (WWI-era Russian Empire), confirming the period boundary aligns with the source's own reporting basis rather than splitting the observed span. No union/combined-reporting or boundary-vintage issue is evident.

verdict.basis: The IIA label 'south korea' for years 1909-1945 is a retrospective/anachronistic naming artifact — Korea was not partitioned into North/South until after liberation on 15 August 1945, so any IIA data dated within 1909-1944 (and up through mid-1945) necessarily covers the whole peninsula under Japanese Chōsen administration (or the tail of the Korean Empire), matching KOR-1800-1945's documented territory (union of CShapes gwcode 731+732, ~219,400 km², stable peninsula outline). The candidate's wiki page explicitly documents this exact source/label/routing combination (IIA 'south korea' ISO KOR rows, pipelines/pre1961-matching rule: country='Korea' + year<1945 -> KOR-1800-1945), confirming this is the intended and previously-vetted match, not an artifact of blind ISO routing. Staple magnitudes (cotton lint ~49,400 ha, cotton seed ~95,650 ha, tobacco ~16,138 ha, silk cocoons ~7,630 t) are consistent with whole-peninsula colonial-era agricultural output and show no discontinuity suggesting a partial-territory (south-only) reporting scope. No neighbor_segments data was available to test cross-period continuity, but since the entire observed span (1909-1945) lies within the single-polity period and no partition existed yet, there is no risk of a north/south split misattribution.

The candidate KOR-1800-1945 wiki documents the peninsula as a single unchanging territorial unit (~219,400 km2) spanning Joseon/Korean Empire/Japanese Chōsen through liberation on 15 Aug 1945, with the successor split (KOR-1945-1948 occupation zones) beginning only in 1946. Mitchell's "Korea" label for 1909-1945 falls entirely within the Japanese colonial period and the whole span sits before the 1945 territorial break documented in the wiki and reflected in neighbor_segments (1946-1948 routes elsewhere). Staple magnitudes (rice ~1.68M t, wheat ~261k t, barley ~866k ha) are plausible for the full peninsula and show no internal step suggesting a partial-territory reporting basis. No union/empire-scope, boundary-vintage, or combined-reporting issue applies since Mitchell's Korea data pre-dates the division entirely.

The candidate PAK-1949-1971 explicitly covers united Pakistan (West Pakistan + East Pakistan/future Bangladesh) per its wiki page, ending only in 1971 with the secession of Bangladesh. Mitchell's "Pakistan" label for 1950-1960 reports a rice paddy median of ~10,038,000 ha, a magnitude only explicable by inclusion of East Pakistan (Bengal), which was the dominant rice-growing region; West Pakistan alone grows negligible rice. Wheat (~4,016,000 ha) and other staples are consistent with a combined national territory of this size. This matches the standard convention in historical compilations (e.g. Mitchell's International Historical Statistics) of reporting undivided Pakistan through 1971. No magnitude discontinuity is evident within the observed 1950-1960 span, and it aligns with the polity's full 1949-1971 territorial scope, so no split is needed.

The assertion's observed span (1938-1947) sits entirely inside candidate IND-1937-1947's official span (1 Apr 1937 - 14 Aug 1947, British India post-Burma-separation, pre-Partition). The wiki documents this precisely as the polity between Burma's 1937 separation and independence/partition in Aug 1947, with CShapes-2.0 polygon (4,227,508 km²) correctly excluding Burma. Staple magnitudes (rice paddy median 34.6M tonnes, wheat 11.2M tonnes, sorghum/millet several million tonnes) are consistent with undivided British India's known scale as one of the world's largest grain producers of that era, not a partitioned or reduced territory. Mitchell's International Historical Statistics conventionally reports "India" for this era as undivided British India (matching the pre-1947 borders), which aligns with this polity's territorial definition. No magnitude discontinuity or scope-change red flags; single reporting territory for the whole span.

verdict.basis: The observed span 1896-1944 is fully contained within the candidate polity's period 1895-1945 (Japanese colonial Taiwan/Formosa). The wiki explicitly documents this exact label ("China, Taiwan Province of", ISO TWN, years 1896-1944) as the reason the row was created, to correctly separate pre-1945 agricultural data from the post-WWII ROC state (TWN-1945-2025, which starts only in 1945 per the neighbor_segments entry). Taiwan's territorial extent (island + Pescadores, ~36,000 km²) was fixed at the 1895 Treaty of Shimonoseki and did not change during the colonial period, so there is no boundary-vintage or scope concern; the sub-territory rule also confirms Taiwan data should not be absorbed into the Japanese Empire aggregate. Staple magnitudes (rice paddy ~658,000 ha, sugar cane ~122,000 t, tea ~12,000 t) are plausible for this island's known intensive agriculture and show no scope-change discontinuity across the observed years, consistent with a single stable reporting territory.

The assertion's observed span (1887-1948) sits entirely within FID-1887-1954's period (1887-1954), and the candidate's wiki page explicitly documents that "agricultural data for 'Indochina' in the pre-1961 dataset refers to the federation as a whole" (Cochinchina, Annam, Tonkin, Cambodia, Laos, Kwangchow Wan), matching Mitchell's "indochina" label exactly — a national-level aggregate label, not a member territory. The neighbor segment shows 1866-1886 routed to FCC-1862-1887 (French Cochinchina, pre-federation), a clean predecessor transition right at the 1887 federation date, which is consistent with no boundary-vintage mismatch. Staple magnitudes (rice paddy median 5.4M ha, rubber 7,400 t, maize 210,000 t) are plausible for a large Southeast Asian federation and no internal jump is indicated across the observed years. No combined-reporting risk (this is one federation, not two merged polities) and no evidence our period splits misalign with the source's reporting basis.

The FAO 1952 "Burma" series (1937-1951, 109 rows, 6 distinct years) falls entirely within MMR-1885-2025's 1885-2025 span, which per the candidate's wiki is intentionally NOT split at the 1937 (crown colony) or 1948 (independence) transitions in our DB — those are documented as open future-split recommendations, not actual splits. Since WHEP currently tracks a single Burma polity across this entire observed window, there is no alternative existing polity to reroute to and no split boundary within our DB to tile against. The staple magnitudes (rice paddy median 5,050 thousand ha) are consistent with full British/independent Burma including the Irrawaddy delta rice bowl (the wiki explicitly notes ~5,050 vs ~834 for the truncated pre-1885 Konbaung rump), not the reduced Ministerial-Burma-only scope (~77% of area). No neighbor_segments evidence was available to check for a magnitude step at 1948, but since our polity period itself doesn't split there, this is moot for correctness of this match. The reporting territory (Burma as a whole, including Shan States/Frontier Areas by FAO convention) matches the candidate's documented territory for the full 1937-1951 span.

The assertion routes FAO 1952 yearbook "Yugoslavia" rows (n=4 years: 1937, 1938, 1946, 1947, gap for WWII) to F248-1920-1947 (Kingdom/early postwar Yugoslavia, CShapes cowcode=345, 1920 polygon vintage, 255,000 km2). Initial concern about the staple_magnitudes population figure (median 5,083 thousand, which looked far too small for Yugoslavia's ~15M population) was resolved by inspecting the underlying layer_b rows directly: the "r_fao_population_1952_10_18" item bundles five demographic sub-series under one item code (population total=15,722k; population agricultural=10,629k; population agricultural occupied=5,083k; female/male agricultural occupied=1,864k/3,219k for 1937), and the pipeline's magnitude summary happened to sample a subcategory rather than the total. The true "population total" series (15,722k in 1937 -> 16,340k in 1951) shows smooth continuity with no territorial discontinuity, consistent across the whole observed span and into the neighboring 1948-1951 segment. The candidate's wiki page documents that CShapes 2.0 uses the identical 1920 polygon geometry from 1920 through 1991 without an update at the 1947 Paris Peace Treaty border change (~4,165 km2 Istria/Zadar transfer, ~1.6% of total area, below CShapes' 10,000 km2 update threshold), so both F248-1920-1947 and its neighbor share the same territory definition — there is no union/empire-scope ambiguity (unlike Sweden-Norway or Cisleithania), no combined-reporting issue, and no meaningful boundary-vintage mismatch given the sub-2% territorial change straddling 1947 that our own DB explicitly treats as immaterial. Other staple magnitudes (poultry, horses/mules/asses, dry beans, cottonseed) are plausible in scale for interwar/early-postwar Yugoslavia. This confirms the source's reporting territory equals the candidate's territory for the whole 1937-1947 span.

The wiki (wiki/polities/grl-1800-2025.md) documents Greenland as a single stable territorial unit from 1800-2025 with no boundary changes (island with no land borders, only administrative status changes from colony to county to home-rule to self-governing). The fao1952 "Greenland" label for 1937-1951 reports population ~20,000 and total area ~217,600 thousand hectares (~2,176,000 km²), consistent with Greenland's known total area (~2.1 million km²) and its historically small population (well under CShapes' 250,000 threshold, matching the wiki's cited ~55,000 in 1994). No union/empire scope issue applies since Greenland is a non-adjacent territory reported separately from Denmark in FAO data, and there is no combined-reporting or boundary-vintage concern for this single-island polity across the observed span.

review.reason: Independently re-derived the same conclusion. The wiki (wiki/polities/grl-1800-2025.md) documents Greenland as territorially stable from 1800-2025, a single non-adjacent island unit with no land borders, administratively distinct from Denmark and reported separately in FAOSTAT/FT sources. The fao1952 magnitudes for 1937-1951 (population ~20,000; total area ~217,600 thousand ha = ~2,176,000 km²) match Greenland's known total area (~2.166M km² incl. ice) and its historically small population trajectory (well under the ~55,000 figure cited for 1994), consistent with smooth demographic growth rather than a scope break. No union/empire, combined-reporting, or boundary-vintage issue applies: Greenland is reported as its own label distinct from Denmark, is a single coastline-bounded island with no territorial changes in this window, and there is no second polity whose data could be commingled under this label. Confirm with same target GRL-1800-2025.

verdict.basis: The "juan" source reports a continuous 24-year annual series (1922-1945) for staple crops (rye, wheat, oats, barley, potatoes) with two units (ha, tonnes) per year, cleanly routed by ISO to POL-1921-1945. Per-year values are smooth and plausible for interwar Poland through 1938-1939 (e.g. rye ~5.6-7.3M ha/tonnes, wheat ~1.0-1.8M ha), consistent with the wiki's documented ~389,000 km2 territory stable from the 1921 Treaty of Riga to the September 1939 partition. From 1940-1944 all five crops show a fairly uniform ~20-30% plateau-level decline (e.g. wheat area 1.76M ha in 1939 to ~1.05-1.2M ha in 1940-44; oats 2.32M to ~1.75-1.85M; barley 1.18M to ~0.92-1.07M; potatoes essentially flat, only -9%), followed by a much sharper 1945 collapse (wheat -42% y/y, potatoes -31%, rye area -92%) before the successor POL-1945-2025 begins. A uniform, roughly parallel decline across crops with different regional/agronomic profiles, plateauing rather than progressively worsening, is the documented signature of wartime occupation-era production collapse (forced requisitioning, labor/input shortages, livestock and machinery losses under Nazi occupation) reported on a constant pre-war territorial basis, rather than a clean territorial redefinition (a hard boundary cut would not plausibly produce near-identical percentage declines across rye, wheat, oats, barley and potatoes, which have very different regional distributions within pre-war Poland). The severe 1945 figure reflects the front line crossing the entire country Jan-May 1945, a one-off wartime harvest catastrophe at the transition to the postwar polity, not evidence the reporting territory itself changed mid-row. Critically, the candidate's own wiki documents that POL-1921-1945 was deliberately designed as the sole container for the 1921-1939 stable-border period plus the 1939-1945 WWII disruption (COW gap 1939-09-27 to 1945-06-28, ending only when borders shifted dramatically westward in 1945) -- there is no alternative existing WHEP polity for an "occupied/reduced-territory wartime Poland," so even if the wartime dip partly reflects the loss of Soviet-annexed eastern regions and/or German-incorporated western regions rather than pure production collapse, no better-fitting existing polity is available to reroute or split to. Given the plausible wartime-collapse explanation for the magnitude pattern and the absence of any viable alternative candidate, the whole 1922-1945 span is best confirmed against POL-1921-1945 as currently routed.

Candidate F51-1938-1945's wiki page explicitly documents that this row covers the reduced wartime territory (Munich Agreement Sudetenland loss, First Vienna Award southern Slovakia loss, German occupation of rump Bohemia-Moravia with Slovakia as a puppet state), i.e. exactly the state of 'Czechoslovakia' as reportable 1939-1945 despite loss of sovereignty. The source ('juan', one of three consolidated printed-statistics feeds alongside mitchell/iia in mitchell_juan_iia.csv) labels this span 'czechoslovakia'/iso csk continuously across 1919-1960, with the matcher already correctly period-splitting it across F51-1918-1938 / F51-1938-1945 / F51-1945-1947 / F51-1947-1993 per neighbor_segments. Checking the one staple present in all four adjacent assertion bundles (sugar beet, reported in the same unusually large units throughout, likely a bundle-generation unit quirk rather than a real-world scale) shows no discontinuity coincident with the 1938/39 territorial break: 1,610,450 (1919-1938) -> 1,761,500 (1939-1945) -> 2,258,000 (1946) -> 1,324,500 (1947-1960). If the source had kept reporting on full pre-Munich borders through the war (a boundary-vintage mismatch) or had switched to a much smaller Protectorate-only or Slovakia-only slice (a combined-reporting/split issue), a visible step-change at the 1938/39 boundary would be expected; instead the value stays in the same order of magnitude and is not obviously lower than the surrounding periods, consistent with Bohemia (which remained within the Protectorate) retaining most of the country's sugar-beet acreage. No alternative existing polity better matches this reduced-territory, occupation-era Czechoslovakia, and there is no evidence of a combined YAR+PDR-style merge of two separately-reported wartime entities into one label. Confidence is medium rather than high because the exact wartime data-collection convention of the 'juan' source (official Protectorate/Slovak wartime yearbooks reflecting the shrunk territory, versus a later harmonization back-cast to pre-war borders) could not be independently verified; the magnitude-continuity check is suggestive but not conclusive given only one comparable staple and non-standard units.

Candidate GRC-1919-1947 (wiki/polities/grc-1919-1947.md) documents metropolitan Greece post-Neuilly (1919) through the Dodecanese cession (effective Sept 1947), area 129,479 km2, explicitly excluding the Dodecanese Islands (~2,714 km2, ~2%) which remained under Italian sovereignty (ITAEG) for the entire 1920-1947 observed span. The FAO-style 'greece' label for 1920-1947 (rows=920, 28 distinct years, staple crops like wheat/maize/tobacco/cotton) is a standard national agricultural report that would not include a foreign-held island group still under Italian administration, so the source's reporting territory matches the candidate's documented territory for the whole span with no internal vintage break (the Dodecanese only becomes Greek from 1947 onward, which is exactly where this row ends and the successor begins per neighbor_segments). No combined-reporting or union-scope ambiguity applies to Greece in this period (unlike Sweden-Norway or Austria-Hungary cases); magnitudes (wheat ~551k t, maize ~204k t) are plausible for interwar Greece's agricultural output and area, with no anomalous step suggesting a different territorial scope.

ROU-1940-1947 is documented (wiki/polities/rou-1940-1947.md) as reduced Romania (~194,000 km²) after the three 1940 territorial losses (Bessarabia+N.Bukovina to USSR, N.Transylvania to Hungary, S.Dobruja to Bulgaria), lasting until the Feb 1947 Treaty of Paris formally restored N.Transylvania. Year-by-year wheat-area data extracted from matched_rows.parquet for 'juan'/Romania shows 1938-39 (Greater Romania, ROU-1920-1940) at ~3.8-4.1M ha, dropping to the 1.5-2.8M ha range for 1941-1947 (ROU-1940-1947) -- consistent with the ~66% territory ratio (194,000/295,000) plus wartime disruption -- and then only a modest rise to 2.4-2.8M ha in 1948-1950 (ROU-1947-2025, 238,000 km², ~81% of Greater Romania). Critically, there is no discontinuous jump at 1944-1945 (when Soviet forces de facto reoccupied N.Transylvania) -- 1945 area (1.85M ha) is actually lower than 1944 (2.82M ha) -- so the source does not appear to be folding Transylvania into 'Romania' ahead of the formal 1947 treaty; the whole 1941-1947 span reads as the reduced-Romania reporting territory matching the candidate. Noise from war/drought (1946-47 Romanian famine) makes the signal imperfect but no reroute or split is indicated across the observed span.

The 'juan' source gives a continuous 24-year annual series (1922-1945) for staple crops (rye, wheat, oats, barley, potatoes) routed by ISO to POL-1921-1945, whose wiki documents ~389,000 km2 stable from the March 1921 Treaty of Riga through the September 1939 partition, with a COW membership gap 1939-09-27 to 1945-06-28 and end-of-row marked by the dramatic 1945 westward border shift to POL-1945-2025. Magnitudes are smooth and plausible for interwar Poland through 1938-39 (rye ~5.6-7.3M ha/t, wheat ~1.0-1.8M ha). From 1940-1944 all five crops show a fairly uniform ~20-30% plateau-level decline (wheat 1.76M ha in 1939 to ~1.05-1.2M in 1940-44; oats 2.32M to ~1.75-1.85M; barley 1.18M to ~0.92-1.07M; potatoes nearly flat, only -9%), then a sharp 1945 collapse (rye area -92%, wheat -42%, potatoes -31%) at the transition to the successor polity. A roughly parallel percentage decline across crops with different regional/agronomic distributions is the signature of a wartime occupation-era production collapse (requisitioning, labor/machinery losses) reported on a broadly constant pre-war territorial basis, rather than a clean mid-row territorial redefinition -- a hard boundary cut (e.g. losing only the Soviet-annexed east or only the German-incorporated west) would not plausibly produce near-identical percentage drops across rye, wheat, oats, barley and potatoes. That said, WWII Poland was in fact partitioned between Nazi Germany and the USSR for the 1939-1945 years, so the source's true reporting basis for those wartime years cannot be pinned down with certainty from magnitudes alone; the wiki itself offers no documentation of wartime reporting convention. Critically, no alternative existing WHEP polity exists for an 'occupied/reduced-territory wartime Poland' -- the candidate's own wiki documents POL-1921-1945 as the deliberate sole container for both the 1921-1939 stable-border period and the 1939-1945 disruption -- so even allowing for some wartime territorial ambiguity, POL-1921-1945 remains the best-available match for the whole 1922-1945 span; there is nothing to split_reroute to.
verdict.wiki_note: The 'juan' agricultural series (rye/wheat/oats/barley/potatoes, ha & tonnes, 1922-1945) shows a smooth, roughly parallel ~20-30% decline across all five staples from 1939 through 1940-1944 (plateau-level wartime disruption, not a stepped territorial cut), followed by a sharp 1945 collapse (rye area -92% y/y) coinciding with the front line crossing the country Jan-May 1945 -- consistent with pre-war-territory reporting continuing through the occupation years rather than a documented switch to a reduced/zone-specific reporting basis, though the true wartime reporting convention (whole pre-war Poland vs. General-Government-only) could not be independently confirmed and remains an open question worth flagging on this page.

review.basis: The candidate POL-1921-1945 (Second Polish Republic, ~389,000 km², borders per Treaty of Riga 1921, stable 1921-1939) is the WHEP polity explicitly designed to span 1921-1945 as a single territorial unit, including the WWII occupation years (1939-1945) for which no sovereign Polish state existed in COW's system (COW gap 1939-09-27 to 1945-06-28) -- the wiki documents this as a deliberate choice, tracking the pre-war political definition of 'Poland' through the occupation rather than splitting further, with the post-war (dramatically shifted westward) territory only beginning at the 1945-06-28 successor POL-1945-2025. The 'juan' source's observed span (1922-1945, 24 consecutive years, no gap) reports continuously through the war years, consistent with an agrarian-statistics compilation convention of using the last stable political/administrative border definition (pre-war Poland) for a retrospective series even across a period when the state was partitioned/occupied -- a known practice in long-run agricultural production series (e.g., Mitchell-style International Historical Statistics or agrarian-history compilations) that do not track de facto wartime administrative fragmentation. The neighbor_segments show clean boundary-aligned handoffs on both sides: 1921 maps to POL-1920-1921 (pre-Riga) and 1946-1960 maps to POL-1945-2025 (post-war borders) -- i.e., the source's implicit territorial transitions line up exactly with our period-split boundaries at 1921 and 1945, strong circumstantial evidence the reporting territory for 1922-1945 is consistently interwar (1921-1939) Poland, matching the candidate. Staple magnitudes (rye ~5.77M ha, wheat ~1.59M ha, oats ~2.33M ha, barley ~1.23M ha, potatoes ~3.06M ha; combined ~14M ha of ~38.9M ha total area) are plausible for interwar Poland's agrarian economy and the summary shows no indication of a mid-series magnitude break that would flag a territorial discontinuity. Residual uncertainty: actual on-the-ground data collection during German/Soviet occupation (1939-1945) is historically dubious (Generalgouvernement/annexed-territory administration replaced the Polish statistical apparatus), so the 'Poland' label for 1939-1945 likely reflects retrospective/estimated data keyed to the pre-war territorial definition rather than territory that was ever administratively 'Poland' during those years -- this is the best available match given no dedicated occupation-era polity exists in our schema, hence confirm as best_available rather than verified_equal.

verdict.basis: Pulled the underlying juan-source rows (matched_rows.parquet) for Finland, item barley/oats/wheat, hectares harvested, 1941-1960. The area series is smooth and continuous straight through 1941-1944 (Continuation War, when Finland briefly recaptured Karelia) and 1944-1945 (armistice/re-cession) — e.g. barley ha: 117k(1941)→108k(1942)→120k(1943)→136k(1944)→139k(1945)→140k(1946), no discontinuity; oats and wheat show the same smooth trend. If the source's reporting territory had swelled to include recaptured Karelia during 1941-1944 and then contracted back, we would expect a visible step up then down in sown-area magnitudes; instead the series tracks a steady post-Winter-War (reduced) Finland throughout, consistent with FIN-1940-2025's documented territory (~338,000 km2, post-Moscow Peace Treaty borders, per wiki/polities/fin-1940-2025.md). This directly answers the candidate's own open question (oq-continuation-war-territory) for this particular source: juan's Finland series does NOT reflect the temporary Continuation-War Karelia recapture, it reports on the post-1940 reduced-territory basis the whole span. (Note: tonnes figures for barley show an odd unexplained jump 1941→1942, 117.7k→765.2k tonnes, but this looks like a unit/scale data artifact — ha figures for the same years are smooth — so it does not indicate a territorial change and I did not use it as evidence.)
verdict.wiki_note: Checked juan-source Finland sown-area series (barley/oats/wheat, ha) for 1941-1960: values are smooth and continuous across 1941-1944 (Continuation War) and the 1944 armistice, with no step corresponding to the temporary Karelia recapture -- this directly resolves open question oq-continuation-war-territory for at least this source: it reports consistently on the post-1940 reduced-territory basis, not on the briefly-expanded wartime borders.

review.basis: The candidate's wiki page (wiki/polities/fin-1940-2025.md) flags an open question (oq-continuation-war-territory) worrying that Finland's 1941-1944 Continuation War reoccupation of Karelia could mean 'juan' source data for those years reports a larger, pre-1940 territory rather than the reduced post-Winter-War Finland this polity represents. I resolved that question directly against the raw layer_b parquet (/home/usuario/Nextcloud/whep/layer_b/consolidated_layer_b.parquet): pulling the 'juan' source's Finland barley/oats/wheat hectares-sown series year-by-year (1938-1948) shows smooth, gradual continuity with no discontinuity across the 1940 cession or the 1941-1944 reoccupation/1944 re-cession (e.g. barley ha: 122k(1938)->114k(1940)->117k(1941)->108k(1942)->136k(1944)->140k(1946); oats ha: 463k(1938)->427k(1940)->399k(1941)->354k(1943)->310k(1945)->321k(1946); wheat ha similarly flat ~125-160k throughout). A territorial scope change of the magnitude implied by reannexing/re-losing the Karelian Isthmus (a substantial agricultural region) would produce a visible step in these area series; none appears. This indicates the 'juan' source reported Finnish agricultural statistics on a consistent (reduced, post-1940-borders) territorial basis throughout 1941-1960, matching FIN-1940-2025's documented territory (~338,000 km2 per Biger 1995, cited on the wiki page). The routing by ISO/name is therefore also correct on territorial-scope grounds, not just administrative continuity. Note: an initial exploratory query mixed 'ha' and 'tonnes' unit rows for the same item, producing an apparent 3.7x jump in 1942 barley -- that artifact evaporates once unit is held constant to 'ha' as the assertion's own staple_magnitudes already specify; it is not evidence of a territorial change.

verdict.basis: The IIA source label 'russian federation' for 1922-1940 is a legacy/simplified name for what is actually whole-USSR reporting, and the candidate F228-1921-1940 is explicitly documented on its wiki page as 'RSFSR/USSR (1921-1940)' — the single row covering the RSFSR-to-USSR transition of 30 Dec 1922, i.e. it already represents the whole Union's territory from 1922 onward (constituent republics: RSFSR, Ukrainian SSR, Belorussian SSR, Transcaucasian SFSR, plus Central Asian SSRs as they were carved out). The key tell is the cotton data: median cotton lint area of ~796,000 ha and cotton seed ~1,503,000 ha are far too large to be RSFSR-proper production (cotton in the USSR was grown almost entirely in the Central Asian republics — Uzbek, Turkmen, Tajik SSRs — which were NOT part of the RSFSR after their 1924-1929 delimitation), confirming the source's 'Russian Federation' figures actually aggregate the whole Union, matching this candidate's documented scope. Rye at ~22M ha is also consistent with USSR-wide (not RSFSR-only) grain reporting. Neighbor segments show smooth continuity: 1920 maps to F228-1918-1920 and 1941-1945 to F228-1940-1945, the same chain, with no magnitude discontinuity at the 1921/1922 boundary reported. No existing polity better represents this combined territory, so this is a verified match, not merely best-available.
verdict.wiki_note: IIA source data labeled 'Russian Federation'/'Russia' for 1922-1940 is confirmed (via implausibly large cotton lint/cotton seed area for RSFSR-proper) to actually report whole-USSR territory, consistent with this row's documented RSFSR-to-USSR scope; this is a useful confirmed source-labeling convention for IIA-era Soviet data.

review.basis: The label "Russian Federation" in this 1922-1940 IIA (International Institute of Agriculture, Rome — International Yearbook of Agricultural Statistics) series is informal interwar usage for the whole Soviet Union, not literal RSFSR borders, and matches candidate F228-1921-1940 ("RSFSR/USSR"), whose wiki page documents it as covering the entire USSR including the constituent republics (Ukrainian SSR, Belorussian SSR, Transcaucasian SFSR, and from 1924/1925 onward the Central Asian SSRs). The decisive evidence is the cotton lint/cotton seed staple data (median ~796,410 ha lint / ~1,503,400 ha seed across n=36 obs spanning 1922-1940): pre-1924 Central Asian cotton lands were administered as the Turkestan ASSR within the RSFSR, but from 1924-1925 national delimitation split them into separate Uzbek, Turkmen (later Tajik) union republics, formally outside the RSFSR proper. Substantial, continuous cotton-area reporting persisting through the late 1920s-1930s in this series shows the source is NOT restricting to literal RSFSR territory but is reporting whole-USSR agricultural statistics under the loose label "Russia"/"Russian Federation" — a common interwar convention before "USSR" terminology was universally adopted in Western statistical yearbooks. This is corroborated by the neighbor_segments showing the same source label mapped continuously across the entire F228 chain (Russian Empire through USSR, 1905-1945) via consistent period splits, i.e., one continuously-reporting entity that our F228 family already tracks as a single territorial lineage. Rye magnitude (median 22,034,000 ha) is also consistent with whole-USSR scale rye cultivation (USSR was the world's largest rye producer, concentrated in the Russian/Ukrainian/Belarusian core), not implausible for the full USSR territory. No step-discontinuity is evident at the 1922 USSR-formation boundary or elsewhere in this segment, supporting continuity of reporting territory = candidate's documented territory.
review.wiki_note: Verified via cotton lint/seed staple magnitudes (median ~796k ha lint, ~1.5M ha seed, 1922-1940) that this IIA "Russian Federation" label is whole-USSR scope, not literal RSFSR borders — cotton area this large could not derive from RSFSR alone post-1924 national delimitation (Uzbek/Turkmen SSRs split off from Turkestan ASSR), confirming the source uses "Russia" as informal shorthand for the whole Soviet Union throughout the interwar period.

verdict.basis: The source label is undifferentiated "germany" (iso3 deu) for 1950-1960, with no companion East/West German rows in this stream (603 rows spanning 11 years, single label). The candidate's own wiki page was created specifically for this exact failure family: it documents that pre-1961 agricultural data reports "Germany" as a single undifferentiated country from 1949-1961, and that routing such rows to F78 (West Germany alone) undercounts territory by ~30% (the GDR share). DEU-1949-1990 is the union of FRG (247,553 km2) + GDR (109,272 km2) = ~356,800 km2, i.e. the full post-Potsdam German territory, matching the combined-reporting scope implied by an undifferentiated "germany" label in this era. The observed span (1950-1960) falls entirely within the polity's 1949-1990 period and predates the era (post-1961) when FAOSTAT-style sources begin splitting FRG/GDR. Neighbor segment continuity (1946-1949 -> DEU-1945-1949, same territory) supports no boundary discontinuity. This is a verified_equal case: the wiki's stated purpose matches this exact source/label/year combination precisely.
verdict.wiki_note: Confirmed against source "juan" (rows=603, years 1950-1960, iso deu, single undifferentiated "germany" label, no FRG/GDR split) -- exactly the failure mode the wiki's "Why this entry exists" section describes; this is direct corroborating evidence the DEU-1949-1990 aggregate-Germany design is correct for this source.

review.basis: The candidate's own wiki page (wiki/polities/deu-1949-1990.md) was created specifically to document this exact case: the pre-1961 'juan' agricultural dataset (pipelines/pre1961-matching/match.R) reports undifferentiated iso3c=DEU 'Germany' for 1949-1961 with no separate FRG/GDR rows, and DEU-1949-1990 is the constructed union (CShapes gwcode 260 FRG + 265 GDR, ~356,800 km2) built to receive exactly that undifferentiated stream. The wiki explicitly states the old F78 (West-Germany-only) rewrite was removed because it undercounted coverage by ~30% (the East Germany share). The observed span (1950-1960) sits entirely inside the 1949-1961 window the wiki names, and the source label 'germany' with iso_in_data='deu' and no split reporting matches the documented combined-reporting pattern this polity was purpose-built to resolve. Territorial continuity also holds: predecessor DEU-1945-1949 (Allied-occupied) and successor share identical post-Potsdam borders, so no boundary-vintage discontinuity is expected.
review.wiki_note: Confirmed: the pre-1961 'juan' dataset row for label 'germany', years 1950-1960 (n=11 years, 603 rows) is the undifferentiated Germany stream the DEU-1949-1990 entry was created to absorb; no companion F77/F78 rows exist for this source in this window, consistent with the page's 'Why this entry exists' section.

verdict.basis: The bundle's observed span (1937-1947) matches the candidate row's own boundaries almost exactly (1920-1947, ending at the 1947-02-10 Paris Peace Treaty cession), and the neighbor_segment for 1948-1951 correctly routes to the successor F248-1920-1991, showing our period splits and the source's reporting cadence are aligned rather than mismatched. The candidate's wiki page documents area ~255,000 km2 (CShapes 2.0 cowcode=345, 1920 geometry) as stable through the whole interwar period, and explicitly documents a WWII occupation gap (1941-04-20 to 1944-10-20) that the row spans without further splitting -- i.e. the wiki already anticipates a source continuing to report under the 'Yugoslavia' label straight through the occupation years, which is exactly what this FAO 1952 series does (rows sampled 1937-1947 including war years). Staple magnitudes (poultry ~1.2M head, horses/mules/asses ~132k, dry beans ~33k t, cottonseed area ~2k ha) are plausible orders of magnitude for interwar Yugoslav agriculture and show no discontinuity suggesting a territorial-scope break. One anomaly: median population ('r_fao_population_1952_10_18') of ~5.08M is far below Yugoslavia's actual 1931/1948 census population (~14-16M); this looks like a distinct population subseries (e.g. agricultural/rural population) rather than total population, not a sign that the whole label covers a smaller territory -- other agricultural magnitudes are consistent with full-country scope and the area figure matches exactly. No existing sibling polity (F248-1920-1991, F248-1947-1991, F248-1918-1919/1919-1920) better fits a 1937-1947 span that must include the 1920-1947 monarchy borders, so F248-1920-1947 remains the correct match.
verdict.wiki_note: FAO 1952 yearbook 'Yugoslavia' series for population (r_fao_population_1952_10_18) reports a median ~5.08M for 1937-1947, roughly one-third of Yugoslavia's actual total population (~14-16M per 1931/1948 censuses); this FAO population figure likely reflects agricultural/rural population rather than total population and should not be read as evidence of a territorial mismatch -- other staple magnitudes (poultry, draft animals, crop areas) are consistent with full pre-1947 Kingdom of Yugoslavia territory.

review.basis: The bundle routes FAO's 1952 Production Yearbook "Yugoslavia" label (1937-1947, 66 rows of crop/livestock/fertilizer items) to F248-1920-1947 (Kingdom of Yugoslavia / early FPRY, pre-Paris-Treaty borders, ~255,000 km², wiki documents CShapes cowcode=345 geometry stable 1920-1991 per the <10,000km² transfer-exclusion rule). This is a single national label with no union/empire ambiguity (unlike Sweden-Norway or Cisleithania) and no combined-reporting pattern (unlike Yemen YAR+PDR) — Yugoslavia was one government (in exile/occupation notwithstanding) reporting one national statistical series both before and immediately after WWII. The 1947 cutoff (Paris Peace Treaty, Feb 10) transferring ~4,165 km² of Istria/Zadar from Italy postdates almost the entire observed span and is a <2% territorial delta, immaterial to the crop-item magnitudes. I cross-checked the one seemingly alarming figure — staple_magnitudes reports median population only 5,083 thousand, far below Yugoslavia's actual ~14-16M wartime-era population — against the same field for every other fao1952-routed country in the assertions file: USA shows 8,130k (actual ~132M), Germany 7,116k (actual ~68M), Japan 10,933k (actual ~72M), USSR 92,896k (actual ~170M). Since this "r_fao_population_1952_10_18" series is implausibly low by wildly varying, non-uniform ratios for every country in the source (not just Yugoslavia), it is clearly some other FAO series (e.g. agricultural/economically-active population, not total population) mislabeled in the pipeline, not a territorial signal — Yugoslavia's ratio (~5,083/~15,000 ≈ 34%, comparable in kind to Germany's ~10% and USSR's ~55%, all plausible as "population in agriculture" shares) is unremarkable once framed this way. Remaining crop/livestock magnitudes (poultry 1.2M head, horses/mules/asses 132k head, dry beans 33k tonnes) are unremarkable for a ~255,000 km², mid-sized agrarian European state. The neighbor_segments note routing 1948-1951 to the retired code F248-1920-1991 is stale pre-split bundle data (that code is marked "retired" in polities_database.csv, superseded by the 1920-1947/1947-1991 split) and not evidence of a territorial problem for the observed 1937-1947 span itself.
review.wiki_note: FAO 1952 Yearbook's "r_fao_population" series is not total national population — cross-checked against USA/Germany/Japan/USSR in the same source, it reads far below true totals by non-uniform ratios for every country, consistent with an agricultural/economically-active-population series; do not use it alone to flag territorial scope issues for Yugoslavia or other fao1952-routed polities.

verdict.basis: The observed span 1909-1945 falls entirely within the pre-liberation period (Korean Empire 1909-1910, then Japanese Chōsen colony 1910-1945), during which South Korea did not exist as a distinct polity - ROK/DPRK only emerged in 1948. The candidate KOR-1800-1945 wiki page explicitly documents this exact pattern: IIA source data labeled 'south korea' (iso3c=KOR) for the pre-1945 era is anachronistic labeling of the whole, then-unified Korean peninsula, and the page's own routing rule (country='Korea'+iso=KOR+year<1945 -> KOR-1800-1945) covers this. The candidate's territory (union of North+South Korea polygons, ~219,400 km2, unchanging Joseon/Korean Empire/Choson borders) is the correct reporting territory for the whole span; there is no distinct 'South Korea only' polity applicable before 1945. Staple magnitudes (cotton lint ~49,400 ha, cotton seed ~95,650 ha, tobacco ~16,138 ha, silk cocoons ~7,630 t) are consistent with whole-peninsula agricultural output scale, not a truncated southern subset, and no neighbor_segments data suggests a discontinuity.
verdict.wiki_note: Verified: 432 IIA rows labeled 'south korea' (iso=KOR) spanning years 1909-1945 route correctly to KOR-1800-1945 under the page's existing routing rule; this is a separate, larger, dated (non-null-year) batch from the 71 null-year rows already documented under iia-null-year-rows, and it independently corroborates that the IIA used 'south korea' as an anachronistic label for the whole peninsula prior to 1945.

review.basis: The candidate's own wiki page (wiki/polities/kor-1800-1945.md) already documents this exact phenomenon: the IIA dataset reports pre-1945 Korean agricultural data under the label "south korea" (iso3c=KOR) even though no South/North division existed before 1945 - the peninsula was a single Japanese colonial unit (Chosen) with stable borders inherited unchanged from the Joseon dynasty/Korean Empire. The wiki explicitly names the routing rule (country="Korea"/south korea + year<1945 -> KOR lookup -> KOR-1800-1945) as the correct resolution for this labeling quirk, distinguishing it from a separate known issue (71 null-year IIA rows also labeled "south korea"). The observed assertion (years 1909-1945, 432 rows, commodities: cotton lint, cotton seed, tobacco, hemp yarn, silk cocoons) are classic Choseon-era Korean agricultural exports/staples, and the magnitudes (e.g. cotton lint median 49,400 ha, cotton seed 95,650 ha across the full peninsula) are plausible for the whole ~219,400 km2 peninsula, not an artificially truncated southern rump (which did not exist as a reporting entity until after 1945). No combined-reporting or boundary-vintage red flag surfaces: IIA's "south korea" here is simply a retrospective/anachronistic modern-name label applied by the source to the historical unified Korea, and the candidate polity's territory (peninsula union, Joseon/Korean Empire/Choseon unchanged borders 1800-1945) equals the reporting territory implied by the data. This matches the wiki's own documented reasoning, so I confirm the routing as correct rather than a mismatch needing reroute or split.

verdict.basis: The assertion is one row of a recurring Mitchell series "China, Manchuria province of" that spans 1928-1952 in this bundle. Sibling segments show the same series routed to whichever polity held sovereignty over the Manchuria region in each span: CHN-1921-1932 (1928-1932), MAN-1932-1945 (Manchukuo, 1933-1945, when a dedicated regional polity existed), CHN-1945-1947 (1946-1947), and CHN-1950-2025 (1950-1952). For 1948 the only entity holding sovereignty over Manchuria was China itself (CHN-1947-1949, ROC/incipient PRC transitional period, per its wiki). Magnitudes across the whole series (wheat 300k-1.4M tonnes, maize 1.6-4.2M tonnes, soybeans 3.5-5M tonnes) are far below whole-China national totals for the same commodities in this era (China's national wheat output alone was ~18-20M tonnes), confirming this is a regional (Manchuria-only) reporting series, not a national one. No dedicated Manchuria-region polity exists in the database for 1945-1949 (Manchukuo's tenure ended 1945; no successor regional entity was created), so the label's territory is a genuine proper subset of CHN-1947-1949's territory, not equal to it. Absent a better-fitting existing polity, routing this regional series to the overarching sovereign national polity is the best available match, consistent with how the sibling non-Manchukuo segments of the same series are treated.
verdict.wiki_note: Mitchell's "China, Manchuria province of" series (recurring 1928-1952 in our data) reports the Manchuria region only, not all of China -- magnitudes (e.g. wheat ~300k-1.4M tonnes/yr) are far below whole-China national totals for the same era (~18-20M tonnes wheat). For 1945-1949, when no dedicated Manchuria-region polity exists (Manchukuo ended 1945), this series is routed here as best-available since China held sovereignty, but users should not read these values as national aggregates.

review.basis: The assertion routes Mitchell's "China, Manchuria province of" 1948 wheat figure (840,000 t) to CHN-1947-1949, the whole-mainland-China national polity for that period. Checking the full "manchuria" family across the assertions bank shows this is a consistent, long-running regional series: the same label is tracked continuously from 1928 through 1952, at similar regional-scale magnitudes throughout (wheat: 1928-32 median 1.36M t -> 1933-45 (Manchukuo) 903k t -> 1946-47 393k t -> 1948 840k t -> 1950-52 732k t). These are far too small to be whole-China wheat totals (which ran in the tens of millions of tonnes in this era), confirming the source really is reporting Manchuria as a distinct sub-national region, not all of China. Crucially, only the 1933-1945 span has a dedicated polity (MAN-1932-1945, Manchukuo); before and after that, no standalone Manchuria polity exists in the DB, so every other Manchuria-labeled row (1928-32, 1946-47, 1948, 1950-52) gets mapped to whichever national China polity is current, as the only available container. The candidate's wiki (wiki/polities/chn-1947-1949.md) describes CHN-1947-1949 as the whole mainland-China civil-war-era polity with no Manchuria-specific carve-out, and there is no documented alternative. Magnitude continuity across the neighbor segments is smooth (no discontinuous jump into national-China-scale numbers), which is the evidence that the source's reporting basis (regional Manchuria) hasn't silently shifted to national scope at this particular row — it's the same imperfect-but-consistent situation as all its sibling rows. Given no better-fitting existing polity is available for 1948 Manchuria specifically, and the mapping is applied uniformly across the whole time series rather than being an isolated routing error, this is a best-available match rather than a genuine territorial equivalence.
review.wiki_note: Mitchell's "China, Manchuria province of" series (and FAO1952's "China Manchuria") is a distinct sub-national regional series running continuously ~1928-1952 at regional-scale magnitudes (wheat ~300k-1.4M t range) -- far below whole-China national totals. Only 1933-1945 has a dedicated container polity (MAN-1932-1945/Manchukuo); all other years (1928-32, 1946-49, 1950-52) are routed to the current enclosing China national polity as best-available since no standalone post-1945 Manchuria polity exists. This CHN-1947-1949 row (and its siblings) should be understood as receiving Manchuria-scoped agricultural data nested inside a whole-China territorial label -- a known, systematic under-count/scope-mismatch worth flagging if a dedicated post-1945 Manchuria entity is ever added.

verdict.basis: The assertion routes FAO1952's "Ethiopia" 1937 population figure (15,000 thousand = 15M) to AOI-1936-1941 (Italian East Africa aggregate: Ethiopia+Eritrea+Somaliland, ~1.7M km2) via an applied alias. But the same source (fao1952) reports "Eritrea" (ERI-1889-1952) and "Somalia"/"Italian Somaliland" (ITS-1908-1960) as CONTINUOUSLY SEPARATE labels with their own agricultural production series spanning 1936-1951, i.e. straight through the AOI occupation period, with no interruption or merging into an "Ethiopia" umbrella. This is strong structural evidence that FAO1952's country-table convention keeps these as distinct reporting entities regardless of the AOI colonial administrative unification, so its "Ethiopia" label almost certainly means Ethiopia proper (~1,000,000 km2), matching ETH-1907-1952 — consistent with the neighbor segment 1948-1951, which already routes the same "ethiopia" label to ETH-1907-1952. The AOI-1936-1941 wiki's own audit protocol (oq-aoi-data-audit) calls for comparing magnitude vs adjacent pre/post ETH series (~1.5x threshold) before accepting an AOI reroute; here the single 15M population point is well within plausible range for Ethiopia-proper alone (historical estimates for Ethiopia in this era commonly range 10-20M) and is NOT the ~70% inflation the wiki's contradictions section says would indicate true AOI-aggregate reporting. The population source_convention (agricultural-population-not-total, ~1/3 ratio) does not materially change this conclusion since it would apply proportionally either way. Given the deterministic "applied_alias" mechanism appears to have generically mapped any "Ethiopia" 1936-1941 label to AOI without checking that this particular source keeps Eritrea/Somaliland disaggregated, the correct destination for this single 1937 row is ETH-1907-1952, not AOI-1936-1941.
verdict.wiki_note: Checked FAO1952 yearbook's own country-table structure: it reports "Eritrea" and "Somalia"/"Italian Somaliland" as separate labels with continuous agricultural-production series spanning the entire 1936-1941 AOI occupation period (and beyond), never merging them into an "Ethiopia" umbrella. This means FAO1952 is NOT a source that reports on the full AOI aggregate under the "Ethiopia" label — for this source, "Ethiopia" 1936-1941 rows should generally reroute to ETH-1907-1952 rather than AOI-1936-1941, unless a specific row shows the ~70% magnitude inflation the wiki's contradictions section flags as the AOI signature. Worth revisiting the fao1952-sourced alias rule that routes "Ethiopia" 1936-1941 to AOI-1936-1941, as it appears too broad for this particular source.

review.basis: Single FAO-1952 row: 'Ethiopia' population 1937, reported value 15,000 (thousand people = 15M). The candidate AOI-1936-1941 wiki explicitly documents this exact failure mode: sources labeling 1936-1941 Horn-of-Africa data 'Ethiopia' sometimes mean the full Italian East Africa aggregate (~1.7M km2: Ethiopia+Eritrea+Italian Somaliland), not occupied-Ethiopia-alone (~1M km2), and gives a magnitude test (>1.5x pre-1936 ETH series => route to AOI). No pre-1936 population series exists in this source/bundle to run that test directly, so I checked external population estimates: contemporary sources put Italian East Africa's total population at ~12.1M (1939) versus Ethiopia-alone (Ethiopia Governorate) at ~9.45M. FAO's reported 15M is closer in order of magnitude to the AOI aggregate (ratio 1.24x) than to Ethiopia alone (ratio 1.59x), though it overshoots both slightly, consistent with typical inflation in Italian-era colonial population estimates of this period. The bundle's own source_convention (this FAO population series reads ~1/3 of true total for industrialized economies like Yugoslavia/USA/Germany/Japan/USSR) likely does NOT transfer cleanly to Ethiopia, an overwhelmingly agrarian society where agricultural population approx. total population -- so I did not apply a 3x deflation, which would have implied an implausible ~45M total. Given (a) the deterministic route was an explicit, pre-vetted alias built for exactly this label+year pattern, (b) the wiki's own stated purpose is to catch 'Ethiopia' labels covering full AOI scope in 1936-1941, and (c) the external magnitude comparison favors AOI over ETH-alone, I confirm the AOI-1936-1941 routing, though as a best-available call given the single data point (n=1) and the inherent unreliability of 1930s Horn-of-Africa population statistics.
review.wiki_note: External corroboration for oq-aoi-data-audit: contemporary population estimates put Italian East Africa's total population at ~12.1M (1939) vs. Ethiopia-Governorate-alone at ~9.45M (Eritrea+Somalia governorates together ~2.65M). Use these as reference magnitudes when auditing 1936-1941 'Ethiopia'-labeled population rows for AOI vs ETH-alone scope; also note the source's general '1/3 of true total = agricultural population' convention (verified for Yugoslavia/USA/Germany/Japan/USSR) should not be blindly applied to Ethiopia, whose population was overwhelmingly agricultural at the time.

verdict.basis: The assertion's magnitude (coffee, green: 16,300 t, the 1934-35/1938-39 five-year average from the IIA yearbook) traces to an IIA table where 'Ethiopie' and 'Erythree' are reported as SEPARATE country lines throughout 1934-1945 (verified in the raw IIA 1939-vintage crops workbook, cafe table) -- IIA never merges them into a single 'Italian East Africa' figure, even after the 1936 annexation. Cross-checking the year-by-year coffee series (mitchell_juan_iia.csv) shows perfect continuity across the 1936 annexation and 1941 liberation with no ~70%+ step-up (1934: 22,400t; 1935: 19,800t; 1936: 14,500t; 1937: 13,000t; 1938: 11,800t; 1939: 6,500t; ...; 1945: 17,000t) -- a smooth decline/fluctuation, not the jump that would signal a switch to the full ~1.7M km2 AOI scope (vs ~1.0M km2 Ethiopia proper). This is exactly the magnitude test the AOI wiki page itself prescribes ('if 1936-1941 value is ~70% larger than pre-1936 ETH series, route to AOI; if comparable, flag as occupation_disruption'): the value is comparable, so it fails the AOI test. Additionally, the AOI wiki's own 'Constituent polities' table explicitly maps the Ethiopian portion of AOI territory to polity code ETH-1907-1936, confirming that code is the intended target for Ethiopia-scope (not full-AOI-scope) data observed during 1936-1941, even though its nominal end_year is 1936. No dedicated 'Ethiopia-proper, 1936-1941' polity exists in the DB (the split scheme only has ETH-1907-1936 / AOI-1936-1941 / ETH-1941-1952), so ETH-1907-1936 is the best existing match for this source's actual reporting territory.
verdict.wiki_note: Verified via the raw IIA yearbook (1939-vintage crops workbook, cafe table) and the mitchell_juan_iia.csv consolidated series: this source keeps 'Ethiopie' and 'Erythree' as separate country lines throughout 1934-1945 and never aggregates to full-AOI scope for coffee. The year-by-year coffee series shows smooth continuity across 1936 and 1941 (no ~70% step consistent with AOI's ~1.7M km2 vs Ethiopia's ~1.0M km2), so the magnitude test in oq-aoi-data-audit resolves as 'comparable' -> occupation_disruption, not AOI-scope, for this item/source. Recommend auditing other iia/mitchell 'ethiopia' rows for 1936-1941 with the same test; they likely also belong on ETH-1907-1936 (per the AOI page's own constituent-polities mapping) rather than AOI-1936-1941.

source_convention.convention: IIA (and the derived Mitchell/IIA consolidated series) report 'Ethiopie' as a country line distinct from 'Erythree' continuously through 1934-1945, including the 1936-1941 Italian occupation period -- it never switches to full Italian-East-Africa (AOI) aggregate scope for this label.
source_convention.evidence: Raw IIA 1939-vintage crops workbook (cafe/coffee table): Ethiopie and Erythree appear as separate rows in every year column 1934/38-avg through 1945-46. mitchell_juan_iia.csv coffee series for 'ethiopia' shows smooth continuity (no ~70% step) across both 1936 and 1941 transitions.

review.basis: The candidate AOI-1936-1941 (Italian East Africa) is a 1,700,000 km2 aggregate combining occupied Ethiopia (~1,000,000 km2) + Eritrea (~125,000 km2) + Italian Somaliland (~500,000 km2). The AOI wiki page itself specifies the exact test for this assertion family: "Magnitude comparison with adjacent years determines routing: if 1936-1941 value is ~70% larger than pre-1936 ETH series, route to AOI-1936-1941; if comparable, flag as occupation_disruption." Pulling the neighboring IIA assertions for the "ethiopia" label shows coffee, green production of 19,800 tonnes (1932, routed to ETH-1907-1936), 16,300 tonnes (1938, this assertion, routed to AOI-1936-1941), and 17,000 tonnes (1945, routed to ETH-1907-1952) — a smooth, essentially flat series with no ~70% step-up. Cross-checking against Eritrea's own IIA coffee series (median 34 tonnes) confirms Eritrea contributes negligibly to regional coffee output, and Italian Somaliland grows essentially none, so even a full-AOI-scope reading would barely move the number — the observed continuity is inconsistent with a genuine territorial expansion to full AOI scope. This is exactly the "comparable magnitude" case the wiki instructs to flag rather than route to AOI. However, the DB has no dedicated polity for "occupied Ethiopia proper, 1936-1941" — ETH-1907-1936 hard-ends in 1936 and its designated successor is ETH-1941-1952, with the 1936-1941 gap structurally reserved for AOI-1936-1941. Since the source's actual reporting territory (Ethiopian highlands coffee production) is demonstrably narrower than AOI's full 1.7M km2 territory, and no existing polity captures the narrower occupied-Ethiopia-proper scope for this exact span, I recommend a new dedicated polity rather than confirming or rerouting to a territorially wrong candidate.

new_polity_proposal.territory_description: Historic Ethiopian highlands/heartland only (~1,000,000 km2), excluding Eritrea and Italian Somaliland; distinct from the 1,700,000 km2 AOI aggregate which combines all three occupied territories administratively.

review.wiki_note: For oq-aoi-data-audit: the IIA "ethiopia" coffee, green series shows 19,800 t (1932) -> 16,300 t (1938) -> 17,000 t (1945), a smooth, essentially flat trajectory with no ~70% step-up expected from full-AOI territorial scope (per the wiki's own routing test). Eritrea's independent IIA coffee series is negligible (median 34 t), so this is not a case where the "comparable" reading is confounded by a large non-Ethiopian contribution masking a true jump. This specific label/item is best read as reporting occupied-Ethiopia-proper output, not full-AOI output, and should be flagged occupation_disruption rather than routed to AOI-1936-1941.
