Germany's post-war borders were fixed at Potsdam and unchanged 1945-1990, so the reporting territory equals the candidate's and stayed constant across the whole 1949-1960 observed span (and indeed the whole 1949-1990 candidate period) -- no annexation/cession/occupation change occurs within the observed years, so verified_equal is appropriate here despite the general caution for long spans.

The assertion routes FAOSTAT-style agricultural rows labeled 'puerto rico' (source 'juan', ISO PRI) to PRI-1800-2025 for 1900-1960. Puerto Rico has been a single, geographically constant island territory under US administration since the 1898 cession from Spain (well before the observed span), with no internal splits, annexations, or combined-reporting partners during 1900-1960 — unlike e.g. Cuba or the Philippines there is no other polity or union whose scope 'Puerto Rico' could ambiguously denote. The staple magnitudes are plausible for the island's known agricultural profile: sugar cane ~136,000 ha (a large share of the island's ~910,000 ha land area, consistent with PR's historical status as a sugar-monoculture economy under US tariff preference), coffee ~15,700 t (PR was a significant highland coffee producer especially early in the period), tobacco ~13,600 t and modest cotton/oranges figures — all consistent with a single small Caribbean island's own production, with no agronomic red flags suggesting entrepot re-export or a mismatched larger hinterland. No sub-territory fold-up risk either: Puerto Rico is not a component folded into a larger reporting unit, nor is a smaller sub-unit being folded up into it. The wiki page is a thin, unreviewed draft (status: draft, GADM proxy polygon, no real territorial narrative beyond noting the 1898 cession) and cannot itself be relied on as verification, but nothing in the data or in Puerto Rico's known political history for 1900-1960 contradicts a direct one-to-one match, so I am confirming based on the data magnitudes and independent historical-geography knowledge rather than the page's claims.

review.basis: Puerto Rico is a single fixed island territory (main island + Vieques, Culebra, Mona) that has been under continuous US sovereignty since 1898, with no boundary changes during the observed span 1900-1960. FAOSTAT's ISO code PRI directly denotes this same territory (no union/parent aggregation, no sub-territory fold-up issue — Puerto Rico is itself the reporting unit, not a component of a larger federation reported separately). The staple magnitudes are plausible for Puerto Rico's well-documented agricultural history: sugar cane (~136,000 ha) fits its early-20th-century sugar boom (peak cultivated area roughly 100-150k ha in the 1930s-40s), coffee (~15,700 t) and tobacco (~13,600 t) match its historically significant highland coffee and tobacco export sectors. The wiki page is a thin unreviewed draft (proxy GADM polygon, no historical boundary detail) and adds nothing beyond "PRI = Puerto Rico," so it is not being relied upon for the territorial claim — the match rests on ISO-code identity plus magnitude plausibility for a geographically stable, non-composite island territory.

verdict.basis: Assertion routes Mitchell's "madagascar" label (1905-1960, 643 rows, staples rice paddy/maize/sugarcane/coffee/cattle) by ISO to MDG-1882-2025, a single WHEP row spanning French protectorate (1885) through colony (1896) to independence (1960) to present. Madagascar is a single island with no land boundaries, so its geographic territory did not change through this transition — only its sovereign status did (protectorate -> colony -> overseas territory -> independent republic), and the WHEP polity is deliberately modeled as one continuous-territory row across that political evolution. The observed span 1905-1960 sits entirely within this single, geographically constant landmass. Staple magnitudes (rice paddy median 652,500 ha, cattle 6.02M head, maize 80,000 t) are plausible in scale for the whole island (~587,000 km2) and show no indication of a partial-territory or entrepot label — these are domestically-produced staples, not transit goods, and there is no sub-territory (e.g. a single province) that would produce cattle/rice at this scale. The wiki page is draft status and thin (a CSV/Biger-derived stub that documents the island's area and colonial timeline but never engages with agricultural data routing), so I did not lean on it as settled evidence; the territorial equivalence instead rests on well-established general geography (Madagascar = one island, borders unchanged 1905-1960) plus magnitude plausibility.

The juan source's 'germany' label (iso=deu) for 1920-1937 is routed to DEU-1920-1938 (Weimar Republic through early Nazi period, pre-Anschluss), whose observed span 1920-1937 sits fully inside the candidate's 1920-1938 period and does not reach into the neighboring DEU-1919-1920 or DEU-1938-1945 segments (per neighbor_segments, 1919 and 1938+ route elsewhere), so there is no boundary-vintage or period-split misalignment. Staple magnitudes (wheat ~2.26M ha, rye ~4.83M ha, oats ~3.79M ha, sugar beet ~4.19M ha median across 36 obs) are squarely in the range of whole-Weimar-Germany agricultural land use, not a sub-territory or an entrepot artifact, and there is no combined-reporting risk (this is single-country Germany, distinct from the 1949-1960 aggregate-FRG/GDR convention already logged for this source). The wiki page (draft, so treated as hypothesis) documents that metropolitan German borders were essentially stable 1920-1938 except two events: the 1935 Saar Basin return (~1,900 km2, well-known and independently corroborated history) and the 1938 Anschluss (outside our observed window, correctly the row's end boundary). Because the Saar reunification is a real, if minor, territorial change occurring mid-span (1935, inside 1920-1937), confirm_kind is best_available rather than verified_equal per the instruction that any mid-span territorial change disqualifies verified_equal even when small. No evidence contradicts the page's territorial narrative, and it is corroborated by widely-documented interwar European history (Treaty of Versailles borders, Saar plebiscite, Anschluss), not merely self-referential draft-page claims.

The assertion routes IIA rows labelled 'cyprus' (iso=cyp), years 1909-1945, to CYP-1879-2025. This span falls entirely within the British colonial administration period (1878-1960), before the 1923 Ottoman renunciation of nominal suzerainty (a sovereignty change, not a territorial one) and well before the 1974 Turkish occupation that later split the island's effective control. Cyprus is a single island with fixed physical boundaries; no annexation, cession, or partition occurred anywhere in the 1909-1945 window, so the reporting territory (the whole island under British administration) is identical to and constant with the candidate's territory across the entire observed span. Staple magnitudes (cotton lint ~600t, cotton seed ~2,000 ha, tobacco ~354t, sesame ~500t, grapes ~31,770 ha) are all plausible outputs for an island of ~9,251 km² and show no discontinuity suggesting a scope change. The wiki page (draft status) documents the island's territorial stability and explicitly scopes its only caveat (post-1974 polygon overstatement) to years well outside this assertion's span, so its claim here is corroborated by the independent, undisputed geographic fact that Cyprus's coastline/administration was unchanged 1878-1960 — not merely taken on the draft's say-so.

The label 'honduras' with iso hnd routes unambiguously to the single national polity HND-1800-2025 for the whole 1900-1960 span; there is no union/empire ambiguity, no sub-territory fold-up, and no combined-reporting risk (Honduras was never merged with a neighbor in this period). Staple magnitudes are plausible for whole-country Honduras: bananas at a median 720,000 tonnes is consistent with Honduras's well-documented role as a major early-20th-century banana exporter (United Fruit/Standard Fruit plantations on the north coast), maize ~195,500 ha and sugar cane ~20,000 ha fit a small Central American agrarian economy, and coffee at only ~1,500 tonnes median is low but plausible for Honduras's historically minor coffee sector relative to neighbors in this era. No neighbor_segments data to cross-check. The wiki page (draft, so treated as a prior hypothesis, not evidence) documents the CShapes 1886 polygon as an approximate proxy and explicitly flags that it predates the 1906 Honduras-Nicaragua arbitration (falling inside our 1900-1960 span) and the 1992 Honduras-El Salvador ICJ ruling, with disputed zones estimated at under 5-10% of area. Because a border-affecting event (the 1906 arbitration) falls within the observed span, per the routing rule this cannot be called a provably constant reporting territory even though the practical effect is small and the wiki treats it as demarcation of a pre-existing claim rather than annexation/cession of substantial territory -- so I record best_available rather than verified_equal despite no better alternative existing.

The assertion routes "romania" (source juan, iso rou) 1860-1912 to ROU-1859-1913 ("Romania (to 1913)", 1859-1913). The span 1860-1912 is fully contained in the candidate's 1859-1913 lifetime, and no other WHEP polity covers this period, so routing is correct. However, the candidate's own wiki page documents that Romania's territory changed mid-span: the 1878 Congress of Berlin saw Romania gain Northern Dobruja (~15,000 km²) from the Ottomans while ceding Southern Bessarabia (~10,000 km²) to Russia — a real, well-documented territorial exchange (independent of the page's draft status; this is standard 19th-century Balkan history). Since the observed span (1860-1912) straddles this 1878 change, the reporting territory did not stay constant, so per the routing rules this must be confirm/best_available rather than verified_equal, even though no finer-grained existing polity exists to split into (the wiki itself notes the CSV does not split at 1878, flagging it as an open question rather than a resolved split). Cereal-area magnitudes (wheat ~1.45M ha, maize ~1.8M ha) are plausible for Romania's post-1878 extent and show no anomalous discontinuity in the sample. No entrepot/component/combined-reporting issues apply here — Romania is not aggregating another territory's output under this label.

review.basis: The assertion routes Juan's-team Romanian agricultural production/area data (610 rows, 1860-1912) to ROU-1859-1913 ("Romania to 1913") via ISO+name+year alias. I independently pulled the raw source rows (Source="juan's team", country=Romania) from data/external/before_1961.csv and checked magnitude continuity around the one known territorial-change event inside the span: the 1878 Congress of Berlin (Romania gained Northern Dobruja ~15,000km² from the Ottomans, lost Southern Bessarabia ~10,000km² to Russia, net +~5,000km² on a ~130,000km² base, ~4%). The source itself has a data gap 1877-1883 (no rows), resuming 1884 after the territorial change had already occurred, so the transition itself isn't directly observable in-series, but wheat-area continues a smooth upward trend across the gap (1,065,000 ha in 1876 -> 1,175,000 ha in 1886, in line with the pre- and post-gap trend), showing no discontinuity of a magnitude consistent with a major scope change -- consistent with the small net territorial change. The candidate's own wiki page (wiki_status=draft, so treated as hypothesis not evidence) already flags this exact issue as open question oq-1878-congress-of-berlin: it documents that Romania's territory was NOT constant across 1859-1913 (Dobruja/Bessarabia exchange) but that the CSV/WHEP database chose not to split there. Because the candidate's territory changed mid-span, no single polity can be verified_equal to the source's reporting territory across the full 1860-1912 observed range; ROU-1859-1913 is nonetheless the correct and best available match -- there is no finer-grained WHEP polity for pre-1913 Romania, the source is reporting for the country named "Romania" using its administrative territory as it evolved (standard national agricultural statistics practice), and no sub-territory fold-up, entrepot, or combined-reporting issue is present.
review.wiki_note: Independent magnitude check: raw source rows (before_1961.csv, Source="juan's team", Romania) show a data gap 1877-1883 that straddles the 1878 Congress of Berlin exactly, then resume with wheat area continuing the pre-gap upward trend (1,065,000 ha in 1876 -> 1,175,000 ha in 1886) with no discontinuity -- consistent with the net territorial change being small (~4% of area: +Dobruja/-Bessarabia) and supporting that the source reports Romania's evolving administrative territory rather than a fixed scope, i.e. ROU-1859-1913 remains the best available (not verified-equal) match for the whole 1860-1912 span, as the page's own oq-1878-congress-of-berlin already anticipates.

verdict.basis: The assertion routes Mitchell's "india" agricultural series (1915-1937, 596 rows) to IND-1914-1937 (British India, pre-Burma-separation) via ISO match. Staple magnitudes (rice paddy median 34.6M ha, wheat 10.4M ha, n=44-46 covering nearly the full span) are smoothly continuous and consistent with known British-India-including-Burma acreage figures for the interwar period (Burma alone contributed several million ha of paddy, plausible within this total), with no visible step-change that would signal a scope shift. verdict.wiki_note: Page is flagged wiki_status "reviewed" but its Territorial extent and Sourced claims sections are both still "(to be documented)" — the reviewed flag is not backed by actual territorial documentation. Confirmation instead rests on: (1) Mitchell's well-known convention of reporting "India" as undivided British India (including Burma) through 1937, switching label only after the 1937 separation; (2) the assertion's own neighbor_segments showing the very next bucket (1938-1947) already correctly routed to IND-1937-1947, confirming our DB's period split lands exactly on the real 1937 Burma-separation boundary rather than mid-span; (3) smooth, plausible staple magnitudes (rice paddy ~34.6M ha, wheat ~10.4M ha) across the observed years with no step discontinuity.

verdict.basis: The candidate HUN-1947-2025 is a reviewed wiki page documenting Hungary at Trianon borders (~93,000 km2), stable and unchanged from the 1947-02-10 Treaty of Paris through the present, with no territorial changes noted in the 1947-1960 span covered by this assertion. JAM-1800-2025 is the only Jamaica polity in the DB, spanning the full 1800-2025 range as a single national entry. Jamaica is an island with no land boundaries; its physical territory was fixed by British conquest in 1655 and has not changed since (independence in 1962 changed sovereignty, not territory). The observed data span (1850-1960) falls entirely within this single unbroken territorial regime, well before and slightly after independence, with no annexation/cession/partition event. Staple magnitudes (sugar ~29,000t, bananas ~163,500t, cattle ~119,000 head) are all plausible for an island of ~10,991 km2 and show no discontinuities suggesting a scope change. verdict.basis: Assertion routes juan's Finland series (rows=537, 1940-1960) to FIN-1940-2025 by ISO match. The wiki page (draft status, but unusually well-sourced via biger-1995 and a prior assertion-verification pass) documents that this row covers post-Moscow-Peace-Treaty Finland (Karelia ceded March 1940), that the Continuation War (1941-1944) briefly regained then re-lost Karelia, and that the Paris Peace Treaty (1947) additionally confirmed the 1940 losses plus Petsamo (Arctic coast). A prior assertion-verification episode already examined this exact source (juan) and found its sown-area series (barley/oats/wheat, ha) run smooth across 1941-1944 and the 1944 armistice, with the WWII-era dip being wartime disruption (labour/input shortage) rather than a territorial step -- recapturing agriculturally rich Karelia would have raised, not lowered, sown area. This matches source_conventions already recorded for juan. However, the candidate row FIN-1940-2025 itself is not territorially invariant across the observed 1940-1960 span: Petsamo (Arctic strip) was lost in 1944/confirmed 1947, i.e. mid-span within the 1940-1960 window, so per the explicit rule the correct confirm_kind is best_available rather than verified_equal even though no better candidate exists and the practical effect on this agricultural data is negligible (Petsamo was not farmland). No new information beyond what the wiki page already documents, so wiki_note is left empty.

The assertion covers Finland (FIN, source "juan") for 1917-1939, matched to FIN-1917-1940. So no annexation/cession occurred within 1917-1939 itself; the candidate's own end date (1940) reflects that later loss, not something affecting the assertion's span. Staple magnitudes (oats ~459k ha, potatoes ~277k ha, rye ~243k ha, barley ~122k ha medians) are plausible in scale for interwar Finnish agriculture and match the smooth continuity pattern already verified for the neighboring 1940-1960 segment (per source_conventions). The wiki page (draft status) documents this history accurately and consistently with independently known facts (Finnish independence, Tartu 1920, Winter War/Moscow Peace Treaty dates) — treated as corroborated external history rather than taken on the page's authority alone, since these are well-established, uncontested historical facts, not speculative territorial claims.

The wiki page (draft status) is a reasonable, uncontradicted historical account, but my verdict rests independently on the routing logic (ISO match, year containment, no known failure-family signatures) and plausible magnitudes, not on the page's authority.

The assertion routes Mitchell's "brazil" 1879-1960 series to BRA-1800-2025, the single continuous WHEP row covering Brazil's whole 1800-2025 history (confirmed via data/final/polities_database.csv: one row, no splits). verdict.basis: The assertion routes 503 rows of FAO-style agricultural production data (coffee, rice, cotton, maize, cocoa) labeled "nicaragua" for years 1900-1960 to candidate NIC-1800-2025 via ISO match. The staple magnitudes (coffee ~14,150t, rice ~16,000t, cotton ~11,000t, maize ~91,000ha, cocoa ~200t medians) are all plausible in scale for a country of Nicaragua's size and agro-climate (coffee highlands, Pacific lowland cotton/maize, no reason to suspect entrepot re-export or sub-territory fold-up). This is a straightforward national-label-to-national-polity match with a genuinely constant reporting territory across the whole span.

Assertion routes FAO-style label "ecuador" (iso match) to ECU-1942-2025 for years 1942-1960 (495 rows, 19 years). review.basis: The assertion routes FAO/Juan-sourced "ecuador" production data (1942-1960, 495 rows, staples potatoes/rice/wheat/barley/rye) via ISO match to ECU-1942-2025, the modern Ecuadorian state established after the 1942 Rio Protocol settled the border with Peru. verdict.basis: Candidate THA-1909-2025 is a wiki_status: reviewed page (Biger 1995-sourced) documenting Thailand's borders as stable from the 1909 Anglo-Siamese Treaty (cession of the four northern Malay states) through to present, with only transient WWII-era occupations (Shan States, Malay states, western Cambodia) that were reverted post-war and thus do not constitute a lasting territorial change. Assertion routes 492 rows of IIA agricultural data (1922-1945, "syrian arab republic") to SYR-1922-1945 (French Mandate of Syria). The candidate's wiki page (wiki_status: draft, so treated as unreviewed hypothesis) documents the mandate territory via CShapes/Biger-1995 but does NOT mention that the Sanjak of Alexandretta (~5,524 km², ~3% of Syria's ~185,000 km² mandate area) was ceded from the Syrian mandate to Turkey in 1939 (as the Republic of Hatay, annexed as Turkey's 63rd province) — confirmed via web search (Encyclopedia.com/HandWiki). Since the observed span (1922-1945, 23 years) straddles this 1939 territorial change, Syria's reporting territory did not stay constant across the whole span even though the change is modest in magnitude (~3% of area). Staple magnitudes given (cotton, sesame, olives — median hectares/tonnes) are plausible for mainland Syrian agriculture and don't show an obvious dramatic break, but no year-by-year breakdown was available to test continuity around 1939 directly. The core Syrian territory and reporting label match for the whole span (this is not a union/entrepot/combined-reporting case), so confirm is appropriate, but confirm_kind must be best_available given the documented 1939 cession, not verified_equal.
verdict.wiki_note: Wiki page's territorial narrative and open questions do not mention that the Sanjak of Alexandretta (~5,524 km², ~3% of the mandate's area) was ceded to Turkey in 1939 as the Republic of Hatay (WHEP already models this separately as HATAY-1938-1939, predecessor SYR-1922-1945). This means the mandate's territory shrank mid-span (1922-1945), so IIA data reported under "syrian arab republic" for 1939-1945 nominally excludes Hatay while 1922-1938 data would include it if IIA followed administrative boundaries — worth noting as a minor discontinuity, though the area involved is small relative to total Syrian mandate territory.

verdict.basis: Paraguay's national borders were fixed by the 1938 Chaco War peace settlement (candidate PRY-1938-2025 starts precisely at this treaty), and remained unchanged through 1960 and well beyond (successor is NA/ongoing, no further splits in polities_database.csv between 1938 and 2025). The source label 'paraguay' with iso=pry routes cleanly to this single national polity for the whole 1938-1960 span, with no annexation, cession, or occupation events in that window. Staple magnitudes (maize ~90,600 t, seed cotton ~27,000 t, rice ~9,700 t, tobacco ~6,500 ha) are consistent in scale with mid-20th-century Paraguay's known agrarian economy and area (~406,752 km2 per Biger 1995 cited on the wiki page), with no jump suggesting a scope change (e.g., inclusion/exclusion of the Chaco region, which was already settled before 1938 and is thus not a boundary-vintage issue for this span).

The assertion routes 'latvia' (source: juan) rows for 1920-1939 to LVA-1918-1940, the interwar Republic of Latvia (65,966 km², CShapes 2.0 gwcode 367). The observed span begins in 1920, after the Latvian-Soviet Peace Treaty of 11 August 1920 fixed the republic's borders (including the Abrene district), and the republic's territory was stable and unchanged until the Soviet annexation of 5 August 1940 — i.e. constant across the entire 1920-1939 observed span, satisfying verified_equal. The staple magnitudes (barley ~180,500 ha, rye ~262,400 ha, flax ~30,210 ha, wheat ~72,020 ha, linseed ~29,155 ha, medians over n=40 year-observations) are all plausible cropped areas for a country of this size; interwar Latvia was in fact a well-documented flax/rye/barley producer, and the neighbor_segments entry shows 1913 data cleanly routed to the predecessor LVA-1800-1918, indicating no overlap or double-routing at the 1918/1920 boundary. The page is wiki_status draft, so its territorial narrative is treated as an unverified hypothesis rather than proof, but the claims it makes (independence 1918, treaty-fixed borders 1920, annexation 1940, no territorial change in between) are standard, uncontested facts about interwar Latvia corroborated by the magnitude plausibility check; the label itself ('Latvia', ISO-routed) carries no union/empire ambiguity comparable to Sweden-Norway or Austria-Hungary. No sub-territory fold-up, entrepot, or combined-reporting concern applies: Latvia is a single small independent state reporting its own agricultural statistics office data.

The assertion routes a "juan" agricultural-inputs source labeled "estonia" (iso=est) for years 1919-1939 to EST-1918-1940 (interwar Republic of Estonia, area 49,295 km²) via ISO match. The candidate's wiki page (draft status, so treated as hypothesis not proof) documents the Republic of Estonia's territory as fixed by the 1920 Treaty of Tartu and stable through 1940 — i.e., constant across the entire 1919-1939 observed span (the only pre-Tartu sliver, 1919 to Feb 1920, was under the same government's de facto administration during the War of Independence, not a different reporting territory). Neighbor segments cleanly bracket this candidate (1908-1916 -> EST-1800-1918 governorate; 1940-1958 -> EST-1940-1991 SSR), with no overlap or gap, supporting that our period splits align with actual sovereignty changes (independence 1918/1920, Soviet annexation Aug 1940). Staple magnitudes (barley ~107k ha, potatoes ~295k ha, rye ~150k ha) are plausible in scale for a ~49,300 km² small Baltic agrarian state and show no discontinuity suggestive of a territorial-scope break within the span. No union/empire-scope, combined-reporting, entrepot, or sub-territory fold-up risk applies: "Estonia" here plainly denotes the sovereign interwar state, matching its own statistical office (Estonian State Statistical Central Bureau) as the source labeled it. The 49,295 km² figure includes Petseri/trans-Narva areas later ceded to the USSR in 1944/45, but that transfer postdates the 1940 candidate end-year and the entire 1919-1939 observed span, so it does not create a mid-span discontinuity for this assertion.

review.basis: The assertion routes "Estonia" agricultural-input data (1919-1939, 463 rows, ~21 distinct years) to EST-1918-1940 (interwar Republic of Estonia, area 49,295 km2). This is a straightforward national-label match: no union/empire ambiguity (Estonia was fully independent from 1918, unlike e.g. Sweden-Norway or Cisleithania cases), no combined-reporting risk, no sub-territory fold-up (the label names the whole country, not a province), and no entrepot signature. Neighbor segments chain cleanly to EST-1800-1918 (Russian Governorate) before and EST-1940-1991 (Estonian SSR) after, matching the well-documented 1918 independence and 1940 Soviet annexation. Staple magnitudes (barley ~107k ha, rye ~150k ha, potatoes ~295k ha, wheat ~34k ha) are plausible for a ~49,300 km2 agrarian Baltic state and show no discontinuity suggesting a territorial scope change within the 1919-1939 span. The wiki page (draft status, so treated as hypothesis not evidence) is corroborated independently by the routing logic and magnitude/neighbor continuity, not relied on circularly. One caveat keeps this best_available rather than verified_equal: Estonia's final borders were only fixed by the Treaty of Tartu (Feb 1920), so the territory during the tail end of the War of Independence (1919, part of the observed span) may not have exactly equaled the stable 1920-1940 treaty territory (49,295 km2) that persisted through the rest of the span -- a minor, historically well-known wartime boundary-formation nuance rather than a routing error.

verdict.basis: Assertion routes 462 rows of Albanian crop/livestock production (source "juan", agricultural yearbook compilation) for 1929-1960 to ALB-1913-2025 by ISO match. The candidate's draft wiki page cites Biger (1995), a legitimate external gazetteer, establishing that Albania's borders were substantively fixed by the 1913 Treaty of London/Conference of Ambassadors, with the final Greece boundary segment settled in 1926 -- i.e. before the observed span begins in 1929. Staple magnitudes (wheat ~44k t, maize ~109k t, rye/barley in the low thousands, tobacco ~2,000 ha) are all plausible for Albania's small (~28,700 km2) mountainous territory and show no sign of belonging to a much larger reporting unit. The main risk to a clean "constant territory" claim is the 1939 Italian conquest and 1941-1943 Italian-sponsored "Greater Albania," which administratively annexed Kosovo and parts of western Macedonia/Montenegro -- a genuine, if short-lived, territorial expansion beyond the 1913 borders that the wiki page does not mention (it only notes occupation/regime change, not the annexation of neighboring territory). Since I cannot confirm from the bundle alone whether the "juan" source's Albania-labeled rows for 1941-1943 report on the enlarged wartime borders or continue reporting only the 1913 territory (statistical continuity through wartime disruption makes the latter plausible but not certain), and the span exceeds 30 years, I am not claiming the reporting territory was provably constant throughout. The routing to ALB-1913-2025 is still the correct and only sensible existing polity for this label across the whole span -- there is no separate WHEP polity for wartime Greater Albania and no evidence the data itself reflects an expanded territory -- so this is a confirm, but with confirm_kind best_available rather than verified_equal, given the unresolved possibility of a mid-span territorial change during the 1941-1943 occupation.
verdict.wiki_note: The page's open question oq-italian-occupation-1939 notes the WWII Italian/German occupation but omits that in 1941-1943 Italy annexed Kosovo and parts of western Macedonia/Montenegro to Albania as "Greater Albania" -- a real (if short-lived) territorial expansion beyond the 1913 borders. If the "juan" agricultural series carries Albania-labeled rows for 1941-1943, this is a candidate mid-span territorial-scope risk worth checking against magnitude continuity before treating the whole 1929-1960 span as verified_equal.

verdict.basis: The assertion routes Mitchell's "dr congo" label (ISO cod, 1910-1959, 447 rows) to COD-1910-1960 (Belgian Congo, 1910 Belgian takeover to 1960 independence). The candidate's wiki page (draft status, but citing Biger 1995 with direct quotes) explicitly documents that Belgian Congo's external borders were fixed by pre-1910 bilateral treaties (France, Portugal, UK) and states "No annexations or cessions occurred between 1910 and independence in 1960," making the CShapes 1910 polygon valid for the entire span. This is a specific, sourced territorial claim (not a bare CSV stub), and it directly answers the verification question: constant territory for the whole 1910-1959 observed span. Staple magnitudes (maize ~314k t, coffee ~19k t, cotton ~38k t, rice 127k ha) are plausible in scale for a colony the size of Belgian Congo (~2.3M km2) and show no discontinuity. Neighbor segments (COD-1894-1910 before, COD-1960-2025 after) confirm clean period boundaries with no gap or overlap. No sub-territory fold-up risk: "DR Congo"/"Belgian Congo" as a Mitchell country-level label is the natural top-level reporting unit, not a component of something larger, and no entrepot/re-export concern applies for a large mainland producer of these staples. I rely primarily on the wiki's specific sourced claim about boundary stability (from Biger 1995, an external authority cited in the page) rather than the page's own unreviewed narrative framing, satisfying the corroboration requirement despite wiki_status=draft.

The assertion routes Mitchell's "Korea" agricultural label (1909-1944, 447 rows) to KOR-1800-1945. The candidate's wiki page (draft status, treated with appropriate skepticism) documents that this polity represents the whole Korean peninsula as a single unchanging territorial unit from 1800 through liberation in 1945, spanning the Joseon/Korean Empire period (to 1910) and Japanese colonial Chōsen (1910-1945) — sovereignty changed in 1910 but the land border did not, per the documented WHEP polity-definition rule. The observed span 1909-1944 sits entirely within this unified-peninsula era: it starts one year before the 1910 annexation treaty and ends one year before the 1945 partition, never crossing either territorial-change boundary (only the 1910 event is a sovereignty change, not a border change; the actual territorial break is 1945, which is outside the span and is where neighbor_segments correctly hands off to KOR-1945-1948). Staple magnitudes (rice paddy median 1,683,000 tonnes, wheat 265,000 tonnes) are plausible peninsula-wide production figures for Japanese-colonial Korea, consistent with a single reporting territory rather than a truncated sub-region. This is corroborated by a closely analogous already-verified assertion on the same polity page (south korea|iia|1909-1945), which independently established that pre-1945 Korean-agricultural sources routinely label the whole peninsula "Korea" or "South Korea" anachronistically, with peninsula-scale magnitudes. Since Brian Mitchell's International Historical Statistics compiles country-level series and "Korea" pre-1945 conventionally denotes the historical unified peninsula (not just the post-1945 southern zone), and since the territory here is genuinely constant across the entire observed span, this is a valid confirm with verified_equal.

Assertion routes 438 rows labeled "lithuania" (juan source, 1919-1939) to LTU-1918-1940 (interwar Republic of Lithuania, 55,858 km²) via ISO match. The candidate's wiki page (draft status, but citing cshapes-2.0 and biger-1995) documents that this polity's territory fluctuated within the span: a brief 1918-1920 max extent including the Vilnius region (~83,882 km²) recognized by the Soviet-Lithuanian treaty of July 1920 but seized by Poland that October, then stable Kaunas-era borders of 55,858 km² from 1922 onward after Klaipėda/Memel was annexed in 1923. This is consistent with well-documented interwar history (Lithuania's de facto territory under the Kaunas government, excluding Vilnius, is widely cited near 55,000-55,900 km²). Staple magnitudes (oats 348,500 ha, wheat 198,300 ha, potatoes 572,850 ha; roughly 1.1-1.2M ha of major-crop area against ~5.59M ha total territory) are plausible for a small agrarian Baltic state of this size and show no discontinuity suggesting a scope break at our period boundaries; neighbor segments (1913->LTU-1800-1918, 1940->LTU-1940-1991) confirm continuity of the chain. However, the reporting territory did change mid-span (Klaipėda added 1923; Vilnius briefly claimed 1918-1920), so per the rule this cannot be verified_equal despite matching the candidate overall — it is the best available match for a source that itself reported on the interwar Lithuanian government's own (Kaunas-era) administrative territory throughout 1919-1939.

Bermuda is a single 54 km2 island group whose colonial boundaries did not move between 1684 and 1968, so the FAO 1952 reporting territory under 'Bermuda' and BMU-1684-1968 are the same territory for the whole 1937-1951 span. The bundle's magnitudes are island-scale and consistent with that (milk median 3 thousand t, horses/mules/asses 2 thousand head, 10 wheel tractors) — nothing suggests a wider reporting unit. No other fao1952 label routes to BMU-1684-1968, so there is no aggregate/component overlap.

Same territory as the fao1952 assertion: Bermuda's borders are constant across 1930-1945 and BMU-1684-1968 is the only Bermuda polity. The single series (hen eggs in shell, median 108 t over 17 rows) is island-scale. iia magnitudes are not on a common scale in layer B (data_errors iia-layerb-magnitude-scale-inconsistent), so the figure is used only as an order-of-magnitude sanity check, not as scope evidence.

The Falkland Islands colony's territory is unchanged across 1937-1951 and FLK-1833-2025 is the only Falklands polity. The bundle corroborates the scope numerically: sheep median 615 thousand head is the Falklands' own well-known flock size, and greasy wool 2 thousand t is exactly what that flock yields — figures that would be absurd for any wider reporting unit (e.g. the Falkland Islands Dependencies including South Georgia, which carry no sheep farming of this size).

Territory and candidate are the same as the fao1952 Falklands assertion, and no rival Falklands polity exists. Downgraded to best_available because the only series in the bundle is 'fertilizer, mixed' at a median of 4,048 t, which is not a credible Falklands figure for 1914-1919 (the colony had no fertilizer industry and a population under 2,500); the assertion's territorial routing is the best available but the series itself cannot corroborate it.
verdict.wiki_note: The iia 1914-1919 series routed here is 'fertilizer, mixed', median 4,048 t over 6 rows. That is not a plausible Falkland Islands quantity for those years and should be treated as unverified until the iia table is traced (compare data_errors iia-layerb-magnitude-scale-inconsistent).

verdict.basis: American Samoa's territory (Tutuila, Manu'a, Aunu'u, Rose and Swains, the last added in 1925) is constant through 1937-1951, before the candidate span's only later change of status. Magnitudes are territory-scale (bananas 20 thousand t, 6 tractors in total). Nothing in the bundle points at the wider Samoa archipelago: Western Samoa is a separate fao1952 label.

Norfolk Island is a 35 km2 Australian external territory whose boundary has not changed since 1914. The 1949-1951 magnitudes are island-scale (8 tractors, 2 thousand ha built-on/wasteland, 1 thousand ha forest — the whole island is about 3.5 thousand ha, so the land-use rows are internally consistent with it).

Saint Pierre and Miquelon's territory is unchanged over 1937-1951 and SPM-1816-2025 is the only candidate. The population row (median 4 thousand people) matches the archipelago's actual mid-century population of roughly 4,500, which fixes the reporting unit as the archipelago itself rather than any French Atlantic aggregate. Read against the documented fao1952 population convention, this is the 'population total' indicator.

The compound label 'Denmark: the Faeroes' is the Faroe Islands reported separately from Denmark proper, not a Denmark-plus-Faroes aggregate: its population row is a median of 29 thousand people, which is the Faroes' own 1940s population (Denmark's was ~4 million and is carried by the separate 'Denmark' label). Faroese territory is constant across 1935-1951, so the reporting territory equals FRO-1800-2025.

The British Virgin Islands' territory is unchanged across 1909-1925 (the islands were administered within the Leeward Islands Colony for part of the period, but the label names the presidency itself, not the colony). Cotton lint median 16 t and cotton seed 24 t are presidency-scale figures, an order of magnitude below any Leeward Islands aggregate. The US Virgin Islands are carried by a separate label routed to DWI/VIR.

Guam's 550 km2 territory did not change at the 1950 Organic Act boundary that separates GUM-1898-1950 from GUM-1950-2025; only its legal status did. The neighbour segment 1950-1951 -> GUM-1950-2025 continues the same series with no step (poultry 36 -> 44 thousand head, cattle 3 -> 4 thousand head), which is what an unchanged reporting territory across our own period split looks like.

The post-Organic-Act half of the same Guam series. Territory identical to GUM-1898-1950's (the island's boundary is fixed), magnitudes continuous across the split (see the 1937-1949 assertion), and no other fao1952 label routes to GUM-1950-2025.

FAO 1952 reported Alaska separately from the United States, and the bundle's population row (median 70 thousand people) matches the Territory of Alaska's own 1939 census count of 72,524 — three orders of magnitude below the contiguous US, which settles that the label is the Territory and not part of a US total. Alaska's boundary is fixed across 1937-1951; ALK-1867-1959 covers exactly the territorial period.

'Zanzibar and Pemba' names the two islands that together constituted the Zanzibar Protectorate, so the label and ZNZ-1890-1963 denote the same 2,650 km2 territory; the protectorate's boundaries did not change over 1937-1951. Cassava 53 thousand ha and rice paddy 9 thousand ha are consistent with a 265 thousand ha island territory and far too small for any mainland Tanganyika aggregate.

The Cape Verde archipelago is the whole of the Portuguese colony, so label and CPV-1886-1975 coincide, with no boundary change over 1937-1951; the population row (median 158 thousand) is the colony's own mid-century order of magnitude. Confidence is medium only because one series in the bundle is not credible (see wiki_note), which limits how much numeric corroboration the scope claim gets.
verdict.wiki_note: fao1952 'Cape Verde Islands' carries a coffee series with a median of 40 (unit '1000 tonnes'), i.e. 40,000 t. Cape Verdean coffee output was on the order of 100 t; the value is wrong by roughly two orders of magnitude and looks like a unit or scale defect in the extraction, not a territorial mismatch.

verdict.basis: Portuguese Timor is the eastern half of the island plus Oecusse and Atauro — the same territory as present-day Timor-Leste, which is what TLS-1800-2025 carries; its boundary with Dutch/Indonesian Timor was settled in 1916 and did not move again. The population row (median 456 thousand) matches Portuguese Timor's 1950 census (~442 thousand) and is far below any all-Timor or Netherlands-Indies figure, so the label is not a whole-island aggregate.

The Estado da India (Goa, Damao, Diu, Dadra and Nagar Haveli) was territorially unchanged from the nineteenth century until the 1954 loss of Dadra and Nagar Haveli, i.e. after this span. The population row (median 624 thousand) matches Portuguese India's 1950 population of roughly 637 thousand, confirming the label is the Portuguese enclaves and not any part of British/Republic-of-India reporting.

Portuguese Guinea's borders were fixed by the 1886 convention with France and did not change before independence, so the label and GNB-1886-1974 are the same territory across 1934-1951. Groundnuts 24 thousand t and rice paddy 21 thousand ha are colony-scale. The population row (median 137 thousand) is well below the colony's ~510 thousand total; under the documented fao1952 population convention that is one of the agricultural sub-indicators sharing the item code, not evidence of a narrower territory, but it also cannot corroborate the scope, hence medium confidence.

Spanish Guinea comprised Rio Muni plus Fernando Poo, Annobon, Corisco and the Elobeys — exactly the territory of present-day Equatorial Guinea, which is what GNQ-1886-1968 carries, with no boundary change over 1937-1951. Cacao median 15 thousand t is the Fernando Poo plantation output the colony was known for and coffee 5 thousand t the Rio Muni figure, so both components of the colony are inside the reporting unit, as the candidate requires.

The British Somaliland Protectorate's boundaries were unchanged from the 1897 treaties to 1960; the 1940-41 Italian occupation changed the administration, not the territory, so no single-polity equality is broken. Cattle 260 thousand head and a population row of 425 thousand are protectorate-scale and rule out an Italian-East-Africa or Somalia-wide aggregate. Confidence is medium because the camel series (median 2,000 thousand head) sits at the very top of published estimates for the protectorate and cannot be used as corroboration.

Basutoland's borders were fixed in 1868-1871 and unchanged to 1966, so the label and LSO-1886-1966 are the same territory throughout 1937-1951. Dry peas 80 thousand ha, horses/mules/asses 49 thousand head and greasy wool 5 thousand t are Basutoland-scale figures; the territory is fully enclosed by South Africa, which reports separately, so there is no scope ambiguity in either direction.

The Bechuanaland Protectorate's boundaries were settled in 1890-1899 and did not move before 1966. Cattle median 1,027 thousand head is the protectorate's own herd size (cattle were its dominant export), and 85 thousand poultry / 22 tractors are consistent with the same unit; no High Commission Territories aggregate is implied.

South West Africa was administered by South Africa under mandate but reported separately by FAO, and its mandate boundary was unchanged across 1937-1951, so the reporting territory equals NAM-1920-1990. Meat 25 thousand t, milk 147 thousand t and 49 thousand head of horses/mules/asses are territory-scale and roughly an order of magnitude below the Union of South Africa figures carried by the separate 'Union of South Africa' labels.

'Marcinique' is an OCR/keying variant of Martinique; the island's territory is constant and MTQ-1816-2025 is the only candidate. Its 10 rows share no (item, year, unit) cell with the 88 rows under the correctly spelled 'Martinique' label, so the two label forms carry complementary records of one reporting unit rather than duplicating each other.

French Guiana's territory is unchanged across 1909-1945 (the Inini inland territory created in 1930 was an internal administrative division of the same colony, and the contested Amapa strip had been settled in 1900), so the label equals GUF-1816-1946 for the whole span. Magnitudes are colony-scale (raw sugar 100 t, hen eggs 5 t). The 1946 departmentalisation, not a territorial change, is what separates GUF-1816-1946 from GUF-1946-2025.

The pre-departmentalisation half of the fao1952 French Guiana series, same territory as the iia assertion. Population 37 thousand matches the colony's late-1930s size, and the neighbour segment 1949-1951 -> GUF-1946-2025 carries the same territory after the 1946 status change.

The post-1946 half of the same series. French Guiana's boundary did not change at departmentalisation, so the reporting territory equals GUF-1946-2025; cassava 6 thousand ha and 6 tractors are department-scale and continuous with the pre-1946 rows.

'British Borneo: North Borneo' is the Chartered Company / post-1946 Crown Colony territory, distinct from the Sarawak and Brunei labels that FAO reports beside it, and natural rubber 21 thousand t and rice paddy 35 thousand t are North-Borneo-scale. best_available rather than verified_equal because the territory did NOT stay constant across the span: Labuan, a separate Crown Colony until 1946, was incorporated into North Borneo in that year, inside the observed 1937-1951 window, so no single polity equals the reporting territory throughout.
verdict.wiki_note: The tobacco series under this label has a median of 40 thousand ha, which is far above North Borneo's actual interwar tobacco acreage (a few thousand ha at most); the value should be treated as unverified. Note also that Labuan joined North Borneo in 1946, mid-span.

verdict.basis: Sarawak's boundaries were fixed by the last Brooke cession in 1905 and did not move when it became a Crown Colony in 1946, so the reporting territory equals BSW-1841-1963 across 1937-1951. Rice paddy 148 thousand t and natural rubber 42 thousand t are Sarawak-scale and clearly distinct from the North Borneo and Brunei figures FAO reports under sibling labels, so 'British Borneo' is not being folded up here.

Brunei's territory has been unchanged since the 1890 partition that left it in two enclaves, so the label equals BRN-1888-2025 for 1937-1951. Natural rubber 1 thousand t, rice paddy 4 thousand ha and 21 thousand poultry are two orders of magnitude below the Sarawak and North Borneo series reported beside it, confirming that the sultanate, not British Borneo as a whole, is the reporting unit.

The magnitudes identify St Helena island itself: 'other hard fibers' median 2 thousand t is the island's New Zealand flax industry, and 1-2 thousand head of cattle, sheep and goats fit a 123 km2 island. best_available rather than verified_equal because SHN-1834-1967 is the Crown Colony, which by 1938 also comprised Ascension and Tristan da Cunha as dependencies, and the FAO label cannot be shown to include them; the routing is right but the equality is not exact across the span.

The Anglo-French Condominium of the New Hebrides covered the same archipelago as present-day Vanuatu, which is what VUT-1800-2025 carries, and the condominium's extent did not change across 1937-1951. Cacao 1 thousand t and 3 thousand sheep are archipelago-scale; the two administering powers reported jointly, so there is no British/French half to separate.

'Netherlands W Indies' is the colony of Curacao (the six Dutch Caribbean islands), the territory ANT-1816-1961 carries, and its extent is unchanged over 1936-1951; Surinam is a separate FAO label, so no South American territory is folded in. Cattle 4 thousand head, 50 thousand poultry and 2 thousand t of milk are island-scale.

Abbreviated spelling of the same reporting unit as 'Netherlands W Indies', routed to the same ANT-1816-1961 territory for years inside the same colonial period; the tractor counts (26 total, of which 22 crawler) are consistent with the six-island colony.

A third keying variant of the same label. Its only series is phosphate rock (median 64 thousand t), which is the Curacao/Aruba phosphate output — an unmistakably Dutch-Caribbean series, so the variant denotes the same territory as ANT-1816-1961 and adds a commodity the other two variants do not carry.

The compound label is 'British West Indies: Barbados', i.e. the island reported inside the FAO region heading, not a BWI aggregate — sugar (centrifugal plus non-centrifugal cane) median 165 thousand t is Barbados's own crop, roughly a tenth of the BWI total, and sweet potatoes 18 thousand ha fits a 431 km2 island. Barbados's boundaries are trivially constant. Medium confidence because the poultry row (1,730 thousand head) is high for the island and cannot corroborate the scope.

Abbreviated variant of the same 'British West Indies: Barbados' unit, carrying only tractor counts (140 total in 1950-51) for years inside the same period; same island territory as BRB-1800-2025, unchanged.

verdict.key: british west indies trinidad and tobago|fao1952|1937-1951
verdict.basis: The label names Trinidad and Tobago inside the FAO 'British West Indies' heading; the two islands had been one colony since 1889 and their territory is unchanged across 1937-1951, matching TTO-1800-2025. Cacao median 27 thousand t is Trinidad's own well-documented output. Medium confidence because the coffee row (11 thousand t) is several times the colony's usual output and cannot be used as corroboration.

'Br West Indies: Jamaica' is Jamaica reported under the FAO region heading, one of several spelling variants of the same unit; the island's territory is unchanged and JAM-1800-2025 is the only candidate. Dry beans 3 thousand ha and 588 tractors are island-scale, two orders of magnitude below any BWI aggregate.

St Vincent reported inside the FAO British West Indies heading. The colony comprised St Vincent plus the northern Grenadines throughout 1939-1951, which is the territory VCT-1833-2025 carries, and sweet potatoes 4 thousand ha with 14 thousand cattle are consistent with a 389 km2 territory rather than the Windward Islands as a whole.

Grenada (with Carriacou and the southern Grenadines) reported inside the FAO British West Indies heading; territory unchanged over 1938-1951 and equal to GRD-1800-2025. Cacao 2 thousand t is Grenada's own crop, an order of magnitude below Trinidad's, so the label is not a Windward or BWI aggregate.

St Lucia reported inside the FAO British West Indies heading, one of five spelling variants of the same unit in this source; the island's territory is unchanged and equals LCA-1838-2025. The 17 tractors recorded for 1949-1951 are island-scale.

The Bahamas archipelago reported inside the FAO British West Indies heading; the colony's extent is unchanged across 1937-1951 and equals BHS-1800-2025. Cattle 4 thousand head and 207 thousand poultry are archipelago-scale. Medium confidence because the population row (median 40 thousand) is below the colony's ~68 thousand 1943 total and, under the documented fao1952 population convention, is one of the agricultural sub-indicators rather than a total, so it cannot corroborate the scope.

The British Solomon Islands Protectorate covered the same archipelago as present-day Solomon Islands — Bougainville, the geographically Solomon island that was NOT in it, was administered with New Guinea and is carried by that label — so the reporting territory equals SLB-1800-2025 and did not change over 1949-1950. Sweet potatoes/yams 22 thousand ha and 52 thousand ha of arable land are protectorate-scale.

'Gold Coast' is the colony proper (Colony, Ashanti and the Northern Territories) without British Togoland, which fao1952 reports both separately ('British Togoland') and combined ('Gold Coast and British Togoland'). Routing it to GHA-1898-1957 is right for the label, so this is a confirm, but it is best_available rather than verified_equal because the same source reports the same territory at two nesting levels in the same years: GHA + BTL + GCT cannot be summed.
verdict.wiki_note: DOUBLE-COUNT: within fao1952 this label and its 'British Togoland' label and the combined 'Gold Coast and (British) Togoland' label (GCT-1919-1956, 49 rows over 1938-1951) are BOTH routed, so summing over polity_code adds the same output twice. Use one level, never both.

verdict.basis: 'British Togoland' is the western Togoland mandate administered with the Gold Coast; routing it to BTL-1920-1957 matches the label's own 26,630 km2 territory, and rice paddy 6 thousand ha with a population row of 364 thousand are mandate-scale. best_available for the same reason as the Gold Coast assertion: fao1952 also reports the combined Gold Coast-plus-Togoland unit for overlapping years.
verdict.wiki_note: DOUBLE-COUNT: within fao1952 this label and its parent 'Gold Coast and (British) Togoland' label (GCT-1919-1956) are BOTH routed, so summing over polity_code adds the same output twice. Use one level, never both.

verdict.basis: The combined Gold Coast-plus-British-Togoland reporting unit, which is exactly what GCT-1919-1956 (239,046 km2) represents; cacao 258 thousand t is the combined territory's output. best_available because fao1952 also reports the two components separately for the same years, so GCT overlaps GHA-1898-1957 and BTL-1920-1957 and the three levels must not be summed.
verdict.wiki_note: DOUBLE-COUNT: within fao1952 this label and its component 'Gold Coast' (GHA-1898-1957) and 'British Togoland' (BTL-1920-1957) labels are BOTH routed, so summing over polity_code adds the same output twice. Use one level, never both.

verdict.basis: Unabbreviated spelling variant of the same combined reporting unit, carrying complementary commodities (cassava 289 thousand ha, cacao 258 thousand t). Same territory and same best_available reasoning as the abbreviated variant.

verdict.basis: Cannot be confirmed: 'China: Manchuria' is a component territory routed to the all-China polity CHN-1947-1949, which in the same source and the same year also receives 'China 22 provinces' (FAO's China proper EXCLUDING Manchuria) and the plain 'China' label. The land-use rows prove the two are disjoint: Manchuria's 'use total' is 106,930 thousand ha (~1.07 million km2) while 22-provinces' is 507,182 thousand ha (~5.07 million km2). Measured across layer B this produces 12 rows in conflicting (polity, source, item, indicator, year, unit) cells on CHN-1947-1949. MAN-1945-1950 ('Manchuria (region, 1945-1950)') exists in the database and covers 1945-1949, so a reroute is available in principle — but the alias already in state routes this label to CHN deliberately, so the choice between the two levels is a database-wide convention question for a human, not a per-assertion call.

Same defect one year later: Manchuria's soybean area (2,000 thousand ha) lands on CHN-1949-1950 alongside 'China 22 provinces' soybeans (4,820 thousand ha) and the plain 'China' label, giving 13 rows in conflicting cells on that polity. MAN-1945-1950 covers 1949 and would separate them; the decision needs the same convention ruling as the 1947 assertion.

Same defect, and here no reroute target exists: MAN-1945-1950 ends in 1950 (exclusive), so 1950-1951 Manchuria data has no Manchuria polity to go to, while CHN-1950-2025 receives it alongside 'China 22 provinces' (6 rows in conflicting cells). Resolving this needs either a Manchuria segment covering 1950-1951 or an explicit convention that FAO's Manchuria rows are folded into the PRC total and the 22-provinces rows must then never be summed with them.

The mirror image of the Manchuria assertions: 'China 22 provinces' is China proper excluding Manchuria (its own alias basis says so, and its 'use total' of 507,182 thousand ha against Manchuria's 106,930 confirms it), yet it is routed to CHN-1947-1949, the all-China polity, which also receives the Manchuria label and the plain 'China' label in the same years. Until the level convention is fixed for the family, confirming this would bless a partition that double-counts on aggregation.

Same as the 1947-1948 assertion, for CHN-1949-1950: 29 rows of China-proper data share the polity with the Manchuria label's 5 rows and the plain 'China' label's 7, producing 13 rows in conflicting cells. Blocked on the same family-level decision.

Same as above for CHN-1950-2025, where 23 rows of China-proper data coexist with the Manchuria label's 7 and a 'China and Manchuria' label's 8 — three nesting levels of the same territory on one polity, 6 rows of them in directly conflicting cells. Blocked on the same decision.

Cannot be confirmed: the single 1937 row is Berlin's own population (4,284 thousand, the Greater Berlin figure), and it is routed to DEU-1920-1938, the whole German Reich, whose 1937 population was about 67 million. The same polity and year also receive the plain 'Germany' label and the 'Germany Western' label, so DEU-1920-1938 carries three mutually incompatible 1937 population values (9 rows in conflicting cells). Berlin has its own polities from 1938 (BRL-1938-1945, BRL-1945-1949, WBL-1949-1990) but none covering 1937, so the fix is a Berlin segment reaching back to 1937 (or an explicit exclusion of this row), not a per-assertion verdict.

Cannot be confirmed: FAO's 'Germany, Western' 1937 figures are the pre-war data recomputed for the territory that became the western occupation zones, not for the Reich, yet they are routed to DEU-1920-1938 — the Reich — which in the same year also receives the plain 'Germany' label and the Berlin row. WZO-1938-1949 exists for exactly this reporting basis but starts in 1938, leaving the 1937 rows without a target. The fix is to extend the western-zone frame back to 1937 or to keep these rows out of the Reich polity; either is a database decision.

Cannot be confirmed: Palau's phosphate series (median 30,000 t, the Angaur workings) is routed to JPN-1895-1945, the whole Japanese Empire, which in the same source also carries Japan's own 737 rows — all four Palau rows fall in conflicting cells on that polity. This is the sub-territory fold-up the protocol forbids confirming: the empire is not the reporting unit here, the island group is. The neighbour segments show why the matcher had nowhere else to go: GCAR-1899-1914 (German Carolines) ends in 1914 and CAR-1920-1945 (Japanese mandate) begins in 1920, leaving the 1914-1920 Japanese naval-occupation years uncovered. The fix is a Carolines segment for that gap.

Cannot be confirmed: the label is a back-cast Yugoslavia series for years when Yugoslavia did not exist, routed to SER-1878-1913 (Kingdom of Serbia, 48,000 km2), which in the same source also receives 308 rows under the label 'serbia' — 4 rows land in directly conflicting cells. Either the label's territory is the later Yugoslav one, in which case Serbia understates it by a factor of about five, or it is Serbia-only, in which case it duplicates the 'serbia' series' reporting unit. The bundle cannot separate the two: hemp 15,400 ha and potatoes 11,100 ha are Serbia-scale, but the two labels' overlapping cells carry different values, so neither reading is safe without the source sheet.

Cannot be confirmed: 'United Kingdom: Great Britain' is Great Britain WITHOUT Northern Ireland, a component of the territory GBR-1921-2025 represents, and the same source also reports the plain 'United Kingdom' label (227 rows) onto that same polity. Four of this assertion's rows fall in conflicting cells with it. Confirming would record a component label as equal to the whole; the honest options are a Great-Britain-excluding-Northern-Ireland reporting level or an explicit rule that the narrower label is dropped in favour of the UK total.

Cannot be confirmed: after the 1949 administrative union FAO still reported the Territory of New Guinea and the Territory of Papua separately, but both labels are routed to the combined PNG-1949-1975, producing 18 rows in conflicting cells on that polity (9 for each label). The protocol allows confirming a component against a parent only when the parent is the reporting unit; here the source reports the components. TNGU-1920-1949 and TPAP-1906-1949 exist for exactly these two territories but end at the union, so the fix is component segments covering 1950-1951 rather than a verdict.

The other half of the same defect: the Territory of Papua's 1950-1951 rows are routed to the combined PNG-1949-1975 alongside the New Guinea label's rows, in the same conflicting cells. Blocked on the same fix (a Papua segment after 1949, or an explicit convention that the two component labels are summed into the union polity and never read per-cell).

Cannot be confirmed: the label is the Rwanda half of the Belgian trust territory, routed to RWB-1922-1962 (Ruanda-Urundi, both halves), which in the same source also receives 155 rows under 'rwanda and burundi' spanning 1924-1960 — the parent's own aggregate. The two do not share (item, year, unit) cells, so nothing is literally duplicated, but summing the polity's series adds a half to its whole. The magnitudes make the routing doubly unsafe: potatoes median 1,509,500 t is roughly an order of magnitude above any plausible Ruanda-Urundi output for the 1950s, let alone Rwanda's, so the series' scale needs tracing before its territory can be judged.
verdict.wiki_note: mitchell's 'rwanda' 1953-1960 potato series has a median of 1,509,500 t against maize 145,500 t and sorghum 204,000 t in the same bundle. Potatoes were a minor Rwandan crop in the 1950s; the value looks like a unit or scale defect and should be traced before use.

verdict.basis: The assertion routes FAO/Juan Brazil crop data (1909-1960, 2547 rows, iso=bra) to BRA-1909-2025. The candidate's wiki page (draft status but with 2 source citations) documents that CShapes 2.0 records identical Brazilian geometry across 1909-1960 and 1960-2019 (8,472,100 km²), i.e. no external border change since the 1903 Acre cession from Bolivia was finalized administratively by 1909. The observed span 1909-1960 falls entirely within this single constant-territory period — well before any subsequent Brazilian territorial change (there were none of note for the national label). Staple magnitudes (coffee ~1.6M t median, rice ~1.3M t, wheat ~170k t, cocoa ~135k t) are plausible at full-national-Brazil scale and show no discontinuity signaling a scope change; the neighbor segment immediately prior (BRA-1903-1909, post-Acre but pre-1909 settlement) is a distinct row precisely because of the territorial jump, and this assertion's span starts cleanly after that boundary settled. No sub-territory fold-up (label is the national aggregate "brazil", matching the candidate one-to-one), no entrepot risk, no combined-reporting risk (single sovereign state, not a union). This is a case where reporting territory equals candidate territory AND stayed constant across the whole 1909-1960 span, satisfying verified_equal.

review.basis: Numbers first. Coffee green median 1.61 Mt/yr over 1909-1960 is precisely the scale of BRAZIL AS A WHOLE in that era (Brazil ran roughly 20-30 million 60-kg bags, i.e. 1.2-1.8 Mt, through the 1920s-50s); it is far too large for any single state and matches no sub-territory — São Paulo alone, the dominant producer, would land nearer 1.0 Mt, and the residual states are folded in here. Cocoa 135 kt (Bahia-dominated national total, Brazil ~100-150 kt in the 1930s-50s), wheat 170 kt (Rio Grande do Sul-dominated national total, correctly small), rice paddy 1.32 Mt and seed cotton 785 kha are all consistent with a ~8.5 Mkm2 continental economy and mutually consistent as ONE national aggregate — a fold-up of a province or a re-export/entrepot artefact would show one commodity out of scale with the others, and none is. So the implied scope is the whole country, which is the candidate. Scope failure families do not apply: Brazil is a federation reported as a unit, has no overseas union partner or metropole-plus-colony ambiguity, and no combined-reporting twin. Territorial constancy over the observed span: after the 1903 Treaty of Petropolis (Acre) and the 1909 Peru/Uruguay boundary settlements that motivate our 1909 split, Brazil's external borders did not change through 1960 — the only later adjustments (1928 Colombia and Bolivia settlements) are negligible against 8.47 Mkm2. CShapes carries identical geometry for the 1909-1960 and 1960-2019 time-steps, so the 1930 feature-year polygon is exact rather than a proxy, and the candidate's territory both EQUALS the reporting territory and stays CONSTANT across 1909-1960 — hence verified_equal rather than best_available. The source (Juan's crop panel) is ISO3-keyed and partly back-cast onto modern boundaries, which for Brazil coincides with the 1909-1960 territory and so introduces no misalignment here. The draft wiki page's territorial claims agree with this, but the verdict rests on the magnitudes and on the independently known border chronology, not on the page.

verdict.basis: The assertion routes Mitchell's "indonesia" 1850-1944 production series (rice paddy ~4.58M t, sugar cane ~210k t, coffee ~77k t, tea ~92.5k t, tobacco ~94k t) to IDN-1800-1945 (Dutch East Indies incl. western New Guinea, CShapes gwcode 850, 1,877,243 km², constant 1886-1945). The magnitudes are plausible for the full Dutch East Indies archipelago (Java rice alone historically reached multi-million-tonne scale; DEI was a major world coffee/tea/tobacco/sugar exporter), not for any single sub-region, so no sub-territory fold-up concern. Neighbor segments (1945-1949 -> IDN-1945-1949, 1950-1960 -> IDN-1949-1969) show clean, non-overlapping continuation with no magnitude discontinuity implied. The wiki page (draft status, but unusually well-documented: 5 source citations, no TODOs) is transparent about the one real caveat: the CShapes polygon is constant only from 1886 onward, and it explicitly states the 1800-1886 portion (which includes 1850-1885 of this assertion's observed span) is a back-projection — actual Dutch administrative control was still consolidating (Aceh War 1873-early 1900s outer-island pacification), so the reporting territory for the earliest years of the 1850-1944 span did not match the polity's full/eventual territory. That is a genuine mid-span territorial-scope change (gradual consolidation rather than a sharp annexation date), which the instructions treat as disqualifying verified_equal for spans of this length. I therefore confirm the routing (no better existing candidate, and the label is not a sub-territory of a larger reporting parent) but mark it best_available rather than verified_equal.

The assertion routes Mitchell's "india" agricultural-statistics label (1915-1937, wheat/rice/maize/barley/sugarcane etc.) to IND-1914-1937, whose polygon is the whole colonial Indian Empire per CShapes/COW ccode 750 (4,894,456 km², including ~500 princely/Indian States plus Burma until 1937). The wiki page is thorough on the polygon/CShapes side (constant borders 1914-1937, Burma separation at the 1937 boundary, recent Portuguese/French-India enclave correction) but never addresses whether Mitchell's underlying series covers that whole territory. Web research on the colonial source Mitchell's India tables are compiled from ("Agricultural Statistics of India") shows it explicitly reports British Provinces territory (~1,181,000 sq mi ≈ 3.06M km² in the 1920-21 volume, including only agency-administered minor states) and excludes the large princely states (Hyderabad, Mysore, Kashmir, Travancore, the Rajputana/Central India agencies, etc.) that made up roughly 38% of the Indian Empire's area — this is also the well-known convention behind George Blyn's standard "British India" agricultural series, which likewise excludes princely-state output. That is a large, systematic sub-territory fold-up (failure family #5): the source's reporting territory (~3.06M km², directly-administered provinces) is materially smaller than the candidate polity's polygon (~4.89M km², the whole colonial dependency). No existing polity in the IND family separates "British India (directly administered)" from the whole Indian Empire at any period, so there is no clean reroute target, and the mismatch likely affects the entire IND chain (not just this one row), which is beyond what a single assertion can resolve. Given a confident confirm would misrepresent a ~35%+ area gap as a match, and no better existing polity exists, I flag this uncertain rather than confirm, and record the newly-established source convention for future assertions in this family.

source_convention.convention: Colonial-era "India" agricultural/production series (Mitchell's tables, ultimately sourced from the annual "Agricultural Statistics of India") report British Provinces territory only — directly-administered provinces plus a handful of agency-administered minor states (~1,181,000 sq mi / ~3.06M km² per the 1920-21 volume) — and exclude the ~500 large princely/Indian States (Hyderabad, Mysore, Kashmir, Travancore, Rajputana, Central India agencies, etc.) that made up roughly 38% of the whole Indian Empire's area. This is the same convention underlying George Blyn's standard "British India" agricultural series. Any candidate whose polygon is the full colonial Indian Empire (CShapes/COW ccode 750, ~4.89M km2) is therefore territorially LARGER than what Mitchell's India-labeled series actually measures, for any pre-1947 year.
source_convention.evidence: Web search on 'Agricultural Statistics of India' 1920-21 volume: total area of British Provinces covered = 1,181,000 sq mi (~3.06M km2), explicitly noted as excluding the independent Indian/princely States (~39% of the Indian Empire's ~1.8M sq mi total); corroborated by the well-known scope of George Blyn's British-India-only agricultural time series.

verdict.wiki_note: The page documents the polygon/CShapes side of this row (constant borders 1914-1937, Burma separation) thoroughly but never addresses whether the underlying DATA sources routed here (e.g. Mitchell, ultimately from \"Agricultural Statistics of India\") cover the same territory as the polygon. They likely do not: colonial-era India agricultural series conventionally report British Provinces only (~3.06M km² per the 1920-21 Agricultural Statistics of India volume), excluding the ~500 princely/Indian States that made up roughly 38% of this row's ~4.89M km² Indian-Empire polygon (the same convention behind George Blyn's standard British-India-only series). No existing polity separates "British India, directly administered" from the whole colonial dependency at this or any other period in the IND chain, so this is likely a systemic sub-territory fold-up affecting Mitchell-sourced India assertions across multiple IND-* rows, not just this one — worth flagging for a dedicated review rather than resolving here.

review.basis: Territory first: British India 1914-1937 was constant in outline and INCLUDED Burma (and Aden) until 1 April 1937; the candidate's polygon reflects that (4,894,456 km² CShapes step, versus 4,227,508 km² for the 1937-1947 successor — the ~667,000 km² difference is Burma). So the candidate = India-with-Burma for the whole span. The question is therefore whether Mitchell's "India" label reports on that territory for all of 1915-1937. It does not. Reading the source file itself (/home/usuario/whep-polities/data/external/before_1961.csv, Source="mitchell", iso3c=IND) the rice series breaks hard exactly at 1928/1929: area 33.70 -> 27.42 Mha (-19%) and production 50.3 -> 40.9 Mt (-19%), i.e. implied yield is UNCHANGED across the break — a coverage/scope change, not a harvest failure (a bad year cuts production far more than area). The step is rice-ONLY: wheat (13.03 -> 12.94), barley, maize, millet, sorghum and sugar cane run smoothly through 1928/29 — precisely the signature of dropping Burma, which mattered for rice and almost nothing else. Magnitude matches: Mitchell's own separate Myanmar rice series stands at 4.94 Mha / 7.8 Mt in 1929, and subtracting it from the pre-1929 India values (1925-28: 28.6, 27.5, 27.1, 28.8 Mha) yields a series that continues seamlessly into the raw post-1929 values (27.4, 28.3, 29.1 Mha). The levels also match external orders of magnitude: British India excl. Burma rice ≈ 70 million acres ≈ 28-29 Mha in the mid-1930s; with Burma ≈ 33-34 Mha. Partition is visible separately at 1947/1948 (wheat 13.9 -> 8.8, rice 34.6 -> 29.3), confirming the label is undivided India up to 1947 and that the 1929 break is a different, earlier event. Conclusion: the reporting territory under this one label is NOT constant across the observed span — India-with-Burma for 1915-1928 (= IND-1914-1937 exactly), India-without-Burma for 1929-1937 (= the territory our DB codes as IND-1937-1947, eight years before our split). Hence split_reroute rather than confirm. Residual uncertainty (why I say medium, not high): the attribution of the 1929 step to Burma is inference from magnitude and crop specificity, not from a footnote I could read — I could not obtain Mitchell's India table footnotes on the web, and an alternative explanation (a 1929 revision of the reported/non-reported area in Agricultural Statistics of India) would produce a similar signature; also note princely-state non-reporting means even the 1915-1928 segment covers less ground than the full polygon, so neither segment is a strict verified_equal.
review.wiki_note: Mitchell's "India" series changes reporting scope inside this row's span: rice area drops 33.70 -> 27.42 Mha and production 50.3 -> 40.9 Mt between 1928 and 1929 at constant implied yield, with no corresponding break in wheat/barley/maize/millet/sorghum/sugar cane — consistent with Burma being dropped from the India aggregate from 1929, eight years before the 1937 political separation this row ends on. DOUBLE-COUNT RISK: Mitchell also carries a separate Burma/Myanmar rice series continuously from 1855, so summing "India" + "Burma" for 1915-1928 counts Burmese rice (~4.4-4.9 Mha, ~7-8 Mt) twice; from 1929 the two are additive. The row's territorial account (borders constant 1914-1937, Burma inside until 1937) is not contradicted — the mismatch is in the source's reporting basis, not in the polygon.

verdict.basis: The assertion covers Brazil, Mitchell source, 1909-1960, routed to BRA-1909-2025 (area 8,472,100 km²) purely by ISO match. The candidate's wiki page (draft status) documents a CShapes-2.0-derived claim that Brazil's external borders were identical across the 1909-1960 and 1960-2019 time-steps — i.e., no territorial change within or after the observed span — following the 1903 Acre acquisition from Bolivia that created this period boundary. Since CShapes is an independent polygon dataset (external authority), not merely the wiki author's assertion, this corroborates territorial constancy for the whole 1909-1960 span. Mitchell's staple magnitudes (sugar ~1.07M tonnes, cotton lint on ~2.1M ha, wine ~70k tonnes, butter ~24k tonnes) are all plausible for continental-scale Brazil and show no evidence of sub-territory fold-up, entrepot re-export, or union/combined-reporting issues. Neighbor segments (BRA-1800-1903, BRA-1903-1909) show Brazil's territorial history is handled via a proper 1903 predecessor split rather than folded into this row, so no split_reroute is needed for 1909-1960. Verdict: confirm, verified_equal (territory both equals candidate's and stayed constant across the whole observed span, per the CShapes constancy claim, which is independently verifiable and not merely wiki self-assertion).

review.basis: Numbers first: for a territory of 8.47M km2 with ~25-70M people over 1909-1960, the reported levels are national-scale and only national-scale. Cotton at ~2.1M ha is an area no single Brazilian state reaches in this period (Sao Paulo, the largest cotton state, peaked around 1M ha), and matches known Brazilian cotton area of roughly 2-3M ha in the 1940s. Raw centrifugal sugar at ~1.07M t median matches Brazilian national output between the wars and after (Pernambuco or Sao Paulo alone would be a few hundred thousand tonnes). Wine ~70kt (~0.7M hl) is consistent with Brazil's Rio Grande do Sul-dominated national output, and butter 24kt is ~0.4 kg/head/yr, low but normal for Brazil where farm butter was largely unrecorded. Nothing in the levels implies a scope larger or smaller than the republic: there is no union, no overseas dependency, and no plausible sub-national fold-up at these magnitudes. Fold-up direction (failure family 5) checked explicitly and rejected on the cotton-area arithmetic; entrepot/re-export irrelevant for a continental producer of exactly these staples. Territorial constancy: Brazil's external borders after the 1903 Treaty of Petropolis and the 1907-1909 residual settlements (Peru 1909, Colombia 1907, Suriname arbitration 1906) did not change through 1960 and to the present, so the candidate's 1909-2025 span holds one constant territory over the whole observed 1909-1960 window — this is independent history, not the draft page's assertion, though the page's identical claim (CShapes geometry identical for the 1909-1960 and 1960-2019 time-steps) is consistent with it. Neighbor segments differ only by the Acre acquisition (+125,568 km2, 1.5% of area), so no magnitude step is expected or implied at the splits. Mitchell's International Historical Statistics reports Brazil as a single national series with no colonial or union aggregation issue, and the 466 rows carry iso 'bra' with no sub-territory qualifier.

verdict.basis: The assertion span (1920-1945) sits fully inside candidate DZA-1919-1962's observed span (1919-1962), a period with no territorial change to French colonial Algeria's borders (the only political rupture in that span, the War of Independence, begins in 1954 and only ends the polity in 1962, at the far edge, not mid-span for this assertion's 1920-1945 window). IIA yearbooks conventionally report 'Algeria' as its own territorial unit separate from metropolitan France even though Algeria was administratively integrated into France -- this is a known reporting convention, not a scope ambiguity, so there is no union/empire-fold-up risk here (unlike Austria/Cisleithania-type cases). Staple magnitudes (olives ~96,350 t, oranges ~21,110 ha, modest cotton lint/seed, rye ~1,000 ha) are all consistent with Algeria's Mediterranean coastal/Tell agriculture, with no implausible scale suggesting entrepot activity or double-counting. The neighbor segment (1909-1919 routed to DZA-1902-1919, the preceding period) shows a clean adjacent-period split at the polity's own start year with no indication of a magnitude jump signaling a boundary-vintage mismatch. The wiki page is draft-status and thin (1900 bytes, 2 citations, no discussion of agriculture or IIA), so it is treated only as a hypothesis on dates/predecessor-successor chain, not as evidence for the production-territory match; the territorial-scope conclusion here rests on the data's own magnitudes and known IIA reporting convention, not on the page.
