source_convention.convention: IIA/agricultural yearbooks report Algeria as its own territorial reporting unit, distinct from metropolitan France, despite Algeria's administrative integration into France during the colonial period -- unlike some empire-vs-metropole ambiguities (e.g. Austria/Cisleithania), there is no fold-up risk for this label.
source_convention.evidence: Staple magnitudes (olives, oranges, cotton) match Algeria's own Mediterranean-belt agricultural geography rather than combined France+Algeria totals, and IIA consistently tabulates Algeria separately across the observed span with no discontinuity at years when metropolitan-France reporting conventions might otherwise intrude.

verdict.basis: Assertion routes IIA "south korea" (iso KOR) rows for 1909-1944 to KOR-1800-1945 (Korea to 1945, i.e. Joseon/Korean Empire/Japanese Chōsen as one unbroken-border unit). The candidate's wiki page already documents and dates (2026-07-24) an established source_convention — corroborated in this bundle's own source_conventions field — that the IIA's "south korea" label is anachronistic and actually covers the whole peninsula under Japanese colonial administration, since no separate southern Korean entity existed before 1945. The observed span (1909-1944) falls entirely inside the Japanese Chōsen period (1910-1945), which the page states had unchanged borders from the preceding Korean Empire/Joseon dynasty — so the reporting territory is both equal to the candidate and constant across the whole observed span. Staple magnitudes (cotton lint ~49k ha, cotton seed ~95k ha, tobacco ~16k ha, silk cocoons ~7.6k tonnes) are consistent with peninsula-wide production scale, not a partial/southern subset. The 1945 neighbor_segment correctly routes to the successor KOR-1945-1948, confirming clean continuity at the boundary. Wiki is draft status but this specific claim is independently corroborated by the already-recorded source_convention (established via a prior, separately-verified assertion on the same label), not merely self-assertion.

The assertion routes Juan's "bulgaria" label (1890-1912, 426 rows) to BGR-1878-1913. The candidate's draft wiki page documents Bulgaria as an autonomous principality (1878) that unified with Eastern Rumelia in 1885 (~96,000 km²) and held that territory until the Second Balkan War/Treaty of Bucharest (Aug 1913) stripped Southern Dobruja and parts of Macedonia. The observed data span (1890-1912) falls entirely inside this stable post-1885/pre-1913 window, so the source's reporting territory did not change across the whole observed span. Staple magnitudes (wheat ~977,100 ha, oats ~162,260 ha) are plausible for a country of Bulgaria's size (~96,000 km²) and population (~3.7M c.1900), with no discontinuity suggesting a scope change. The neighbor_segments show a clean handoff to BGR-1913-1918 for 1913-1917, consistent with the Balkan Wars border change happening just after the observed span ends. The wiki page is draft (unreviewed) but reasonably substantive (6KB, 7 source citations, no TODOs), so its territorial narrative is treated as a hypothesis corroborated here by the magnitude/date reasoning above rather than accepted at face value.

review.basis: Numbers first: wheat median 977,100 ha over 1890-1912. Post-union Bulgaria is ~96,300 km2 (9.6 Mha total land, ~3-3.5 Mha arable), so wheat at ~1 Mha is ~10% of all land and ~30% of arable — exactly the profile of the Balkan wheat-exporting kingdom, and independently corroborated outside our wiki: the 1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica records "over a million hectares" under wheat in 1910 with a 1,148,000 t crop and ~300,000 t of grain/flour exports. That pins the reporting territory at unified Bulgaria (principality + Eastern Rumelia), not the pre-1885 principality alone (63,750 km2, where ~977k ha wheat would be an implausible 15% of total land and would exclude the Thracian plain that grew much of it), and rules out any Ottoman-suzerain fold-up (an Ottoman-scope series would be several times larger). The minor-crop levels point the same way: seed cotton 487 ha, linseed 150 ha, hempseed 1,709 ha are small-Balkan-state magnitudes, not empire ones; a fold-up of an Ottoman or a post-1913 Greater Bulgaria scope would not produce a cotton figure under 500 ha. Sub-territory fold-up in the other direction is not in play either — "bulgaria" with iso bgr is the national label, not a district. Vintage/boundary checks: the observed span 1890-1912 lies entirely between the two territorial events that bracket this row — the 1885 Eastern Rumelia union (before the first observed year) and the Balkan War changes of 1912-13 (the Treaty of London/Bucharest gains and the Southern Dobruja loss both fall in 1913, and 1912 crop statistics were compiled on pre-war borders). So the reporting territory was constant at the post-1885 ~96,300 km2 extent across the whole observed span, and that is the extent the candidate carries (polygon_feature_year 1886, i.e. post-union). The mid-row 1885 territorial change flagged on the wiki page therefore affects only 1878-1885, for which this source has no rows. Neighbour segments (BGR-1913-1918 onward) start after the data ends, so no split-basis misalignment and no combined-reporting risk. I used the draft wiki page only for the row's date logic, not for the territorial magnitude, which rests on the data and Britannica.
review.wiki_note: Quantified corroboration the page lacks: this source's 1890-1912 series gives wheat at a median 977,100 ha, matching the 1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica's "over a million hectares under wheat in 1910, crop 1,148,000 t" — independent confirmation that data labelled "Bulgaria" in this period is on the post-1885 unified ~96,300 km2 territory. Also answers oq-1885-eastern-rumelia from the data side: no observed rows fall before 1890, so a mid-row split at 1885 would not re-route any data. Separately, the page asserts "CShapes first records Bulgaria at 1908-10-05" while the CSV records polygon_feature_year 1886 for this row — one of the two is wrong and the page's own open question ("Check whether CShapes has Bulgaria before 1908") is still unresolved.

verdict.basis: The assertion routes IIA's "Russian Federation" 1922-1939 series (cotton, rye, flax, hempseed, etc.) to F228-1921-1940 ("RSFSR/USSR 1921-1940"). This is essentially a near-duplicate of the already-verified assertion "russian federation|iia|1922-1940" (435 rows) documented on the candidate's own wiki page: IIA's Soviet-era "Russian Federation" label is anachronistic and actually reports whole-USSR territory (cotton lint ~726k ha, cotton seed ~1.28M ha, rye ~22.4M ha medians are far too large for RSFSR alone — cotton was grown in Central Asia/Transcaucasia, outside the RSFSR proper). The candidate's neighbor_segments chain (F228-1920-1921 -> F228-1921-1940 -> F228-1940-1945) is smooth and the magnitudes match the union-scale convention already established. However, per the candidate's own "Territorial extent" section, the Soviet invasion of eastern Poland (Sept 1939, annexing western Ukraine/Belarus) falls within the observed span's final year (1939), meaning USSR territory was not perfectly constant across the whole 1922-1939 window even though it predates the formal 1940 CSV-split boundary. Given this documented mid/end-span territorial change, confirm_kind is best_available rather than verified_equal, despite no better candidate existing. The wiki page is a draft but is well-cited (5 source_citations) and its territorial narrative is corroborated by the bundle's own staple magnitudes, so I rely on the combination rather than the page alone.

Haiti's national territory (western third of Hispaniola, ~27,750 km²) has been constant since independence in 1804, including through the 1900-1960 span (which covers the 1915-1934 US occupation, an administrative arrangement that did not alter territorial boundaries). The FAO/Juan dataset's iso-based routing (hti) to HTI-1800-2025 is a direct national match with no union/empire scope issue, no sub-territory fold-up, and no entrepôt signal — the staple magnitudes (coffee ~33,500t median, cocoa ~1,800t, cotton, rice paddy ~30,000 ha) are consistent with Haiti's known agricultural profile and scale (coffee was historically Haiti's dominant export crop). The wiki page is thin (draft, no territorial-change discussion) but its core claim (constant western-Hispaniola territory since 1800) is externally well known and uncontested, so it serves as adequate corroboration alongside general historical knowledge of Haiti's stable borders.

The assertion covers "Finland" 1878-1916 (rows=405, iso=fin) routed to FIN-1809-1917 (Grand Duchy of Finland, autonomous within the Russian Empire 1809-1917). The Grand Duchy had its own Diet, customs, and currency (markka from 1860), making it a genuinely distinct statistical/administrative reporting unit from Russia proper — this is the classic union/empire-scope failure mode, and here the wiki's rationale for NOT folding this into F228 (Russian Empire) is sound and independently plausible (a component of an empire with its own fiscal/statistical apparatus is commonly reported separately, unlike e.g. Cisleithania-vs-Austria where the ambiguity runs the other way). The observed span 1878-1916 falls entirely inside 1809-1917 and does not cross the 1917 independence split or the 1940 Karelia/Petsamo territorial-change split (confirmed via neighbor_segments and the polities_database.csv family, which show FIN-1917-1940 and FIN-1940-2025 as the segments handling those later boundary changes). No known territorial change to the Grand Duchy's own borders occurred during 1878-1916 itself (Petsamo was gained in 1920, Karelia lost in 1940 — both outside this span). Staple magnitudes (oats ~271k t, potatoes ~384k t, rye ~261k t, barley ~110k t) are plausible for Finland's actual agricultural scale, not for all of Russia, corroborating that this is genuinely Finland-scale data rather than empire-scale data mislabeled. The wiki page is draft with only 1 source citation, so it is treated as a hypothesis, not evidence — but its core territorial claim (Finland as a distinct reporting unit from Russia, borders stable 1809-1917 aside from independence-era edge changes handled by neighbor segments) is corroborated independently by the source_conventions precedent, the magnitude plausibility check, and the clean alignment with the DB's period-split structure.

review.basis: Reasoned from magnitudes before prose. Medians 1878-1916: rye 260.5 kt, oats 271.3 kt, potatoes 383.5 kt, barley 110.3 kt, wheat only 3.6 kt. The vanishing wheat share with rye/oats dominance is the signature of a boreal territory north of ~60N (wheat only became meaningful in Finland in the 1920s-30s), and ~645 kt total grain for a 2.1-3.0M population (~230 kg/head, consistent with Finland's documented net rye imports from Russia) implies ~1.5-1.7 Mha sown, i.e. 4-5% of a ~360,000 km2 land area — exactly the Grand Duchy's scale. Two orders of magnitude below Russian Empire rye (~20 Mt), so the label is not an imperial aggregate; far too large for any single Finnish governorate, so no sub-territory fold-up. Scope check passes in the unusual direction: the Grand Duchy was itself the reporting unit — separate Diet, customs frontier and currency (markka 1860), with its own official statistical series reported separately from Russia, which is precisely why the data carries a distinct 'finland' label 1878-1916 in the first place. Constancy: Grand Duchy borders were unchanged from 1812 to 1917; no annexation or cession falls inside the observed span, and Petsamo (Tartu 1920) postdates it and is outside the 1917 CShapes polygon, so territory equals the candidate's and was constant throughout — the two conditions for verified_equal. Continuity into the neighbor FIN-1917-1940 is territorially exact (same borders, same polygon feature year 1917). Residual risk I could not fully exclude: whether juan's pre-1917 Finnish series sits on contemporaneous borders or a modern back-cast onto post-1940 borders (a ~11% difference, the agriculturally significant Karelian Isthmus/Viipuri); the bundle's verified source convention describes juan following contemporaneous territory rather than back-casting, and the magnitudes cannot arbitrate a 10% difference, so I take the contemporaneous reading. The candidate wiki page is a thin draft with a single Wikipedia citation and null area, but its territorial claims (borders essentially those of 1917 Finland, minus Petsamo plus later-ceded Karelia) match what I derived independently, so I record it only as corroborating, not load-bearing.

verdict.basis: Juan's "United States of America" label for 1900-1958 routes to USA-1867-1959. Both the Alaska Purchase (1867) and Hawaii's annexation (1898) predate the observed span, and no annexation, cession, or separation affecting the mainland/Alaska/Hawaii territory occurred between 1900 and 1958 (Alaska/Hawaii statehood in 1959, the row's own end-point, was an administrative status change only, not a territorial one, as the wiki page itself notes). Staple magnitudes (wheat median 23.3M ha, barley 4.2M ha, seed cotton 6.8M ha across n=118 country-years) are the right order of magnitude for continental-US harvested-area totals in this period, with no step change indicating a scope shift (e.g. Philippines inclusion, which would be agronomically and magnitude-wise a much smaller, tropical-crop-dominated addition, not reflected here). The neighbor segment cleanly hands off 1959-1960 to USA-1959-2025, consistent with our period split. The wiki page is draft (unreviewed) and its territorial narrative is self-referential to the CSV rather than externally sourced, but the specific claim needed here — territorial stability across 1900-1958 — is independently corroboratable from well-known US territorial history (no acquisitions/losses in this window) and is not contradicted by the data magnitudes, so I treat it as verified rather than merely asserted.

review.basis: Numbers first: the label carries 5,948 rows, 1900-1958, iso usa, with staple levels of wheat ~23.3M ha, seed cotton ~6.8M, barley ~4.2M, potatoes ~3.4M (n=118 = 2 series/year, so the pooled median mixes area and production, which explains potatoes/barley reading high for area alone). Those levels are exactly conterminous-United-States scale: US wheat harvested area ran ~17M ha (1900) to ~30M ha (1919, 1950s), cotton ~7-18M ha, barley ~1.2-5.3M ha over this span. Nothing in the magnitudes implies anything bigger (no Philippine/Puerto Rican sugar-cane- or coconut-scale signal) or smaller (no single-state or regional fraction). Scope checks: no union/empire issue (the US had no metropolitan-vs-colonial ambiguity of the Sweden-Norway or Austria kind; insular possessions -- Philippines 1898-1946, Puerto Rico, Hawaii Territory -- are separate rows and are reported separately in USDA/FAO-lineage crop statistics, which cover the states); no combined reporting; no sub-territory fold-up (the label is the national aggregate, not a state or district); no boundary-vintage problem, because the states' borders were literally unchanged 1900-1958. Year containment is clean: the observed span sits wholly inside USA-1867-1959 and the only neighbor segment begins at 1959, our statehood split, after the data end. So the routing to USA-1867-1959 is right. I mark it best_available rather than verified_equal because the source's reporting territory is the crop-reporting states (effectively the conterminous 48), whereas the candidate's documented territory is continental US plus Alaska (~9.4M km2, i.e. ~18% of the candidate's area is Alaska, which contributes essentially nothing to these series) and, within the span, the candidate nominally carries Hawaii Territory as well; the difference is agriculturally negligible but it is a real non-identity, and no more granular polity exists or should exist. The wiki page (draft, 5.2 KB, 1 citation) describes the territory consistently with this and I used it only as corroboration, not as the basis; the arithmetic alone settles the scope.
review.wiki_note: Data-scope point the page lacks: national US crop statistics of this era (USDA-lineage, which FAO/whep panels inherit) are compiled for the crop-reporting states -- effectively the conterminous 48 -- and exclude Alaska, and report Hawaii, Puerto Rico and the Philippines separately. So data routed to USA-1867-1959 covers ~7.7M km2 of the row's ~9.4M km2 footprint; the omitted Alaskan share is agriculturally negligible but the row's territory and the reporting territory are not identical.

verdict.basis: The assertion routes Juan's "italy" label (rows 1919-1960, iso=ITA) to candidate ITA-1919-2025, whose start (1919, Treaty of Saint-Germain gains of Trentino/South Tyrol/Trieste/Istria) matches the observed span's start and the neighbor_segments show a clean hand-off from ITA-1870-1919. Staple magnitudes (potatoes ~930k ha, olives ~1.17M ha, sugar beet ~344k ha medians) are plausible for peninsular Italy at national scale, not a sub-region or entrepot. However, Italy's territory did NOT stay constant across the observed 1919-1960 span: the Treaty of Paris (1947) transferred Istria and parts of Dalmatia to Yugoslavia and ~268 sq mi to France (a well-documented, historically established border change, also cited in the candidate's own page via biger-1995). The WHEP database does not split ITA at 1947, so there is no finer-grained existing polity to reroute the post-1947 portion to (the candidate's own open question 'oq-post-wwii-losses' flags this as a Tier-X unresolved split-policy question). Since a territorial change occurred mid-span and no better candidate exists, this is the best available match rather than a verified-constant equality.

The assertion routes Juan's Italy production data (1870-1918, 1739 rows, ~49 distinct years) to candidate ITA-1870-1919. The wiki page (wiki_status: draft, but well-documented with 4 source citations from Wikipedia and COW) explicitly describes this sub-period as the polygon-faithful mainland Italy period: from the capture of Rome (Sept 1870) to the Treaty of Saint-Germain (Sept 1919), with no territorial changes to the European mainland in between (colonial Libya, acquired 1911-12, is explicitly tracked separately and does not affect the European polygon). This matches the observed data span (1870-1918) entirely within the constant-territory window documented on the page. Staple magnitudes (wheat ~4.4M t, maize ~2.0M t, rice paddy ~396k t, oats ~389k t) are all plausible for mainland Kingdom of Italy (Po valley rice, well-established wheat/maize belt) and implausible for colonial Libya, so there is no entrepot/fold-up risk. Neighbor segments (1861-1865→ITA-1861-1866, 1866-1869→ITA-1866-1870, 1919-1960→ITA-1919-2025) show a continuous, non-overlapping period chain consistent with this candidate's start/end boundaries, supporting territorial continuity across splits. No annexation/cession/occupation affects the observed span itself (the 1919 change falls exactly at the candidate's own boundary, handled by the successor row). I therefore confirm with verified_equal: the reporting territory equals the candidate's and was constant throughout the observed 1870-1918 span.

The assertion routes Juan's Chilean crop-area/production series (barley, maize, wheat, oats, potatoes — median wheat area 730,000 ha, all plausible for continental Chile's agricultural belt) for 1902-1960 to CHL-1902-2025, whose predecessor chain (CHL-1899-1902 -> CHL-1902-2025) and neighbor segments show smooth continuity with no step-change in magnitude across the 1902 boundary, consistent with a single stable reporting territory for continental Chile. The candidate's wiki page is "reviewed" with 5 sourced citations (biger-1995) and itself documents that Chile's northern boundary with Peru was not finally settled until the 3 June 1929 Tacna-Arica treaty (Chile retaining Arica, ceding Tacna to Peru) — a genuine, if small, territorial change roughly midway through the 58-year observed span. Because the span exceeds 30 years and includes this documented boundary finalization, the territory did not stay perfectly constant, so confirm_kind is best_available rather than verified_equal even though no better-fitting existing polity exists and the affected area (a single northern province) is a negligible fraction of Chile's ~756,630 km2 whole, with no effect on the agricultural staples reported. No entrepot/re-export or combined-reporting concerns arise for continental Chilean crop data.

review.basis: Arithmetic first: the label carries national-scale staples — wheat median 730,000 ha, oats 77,820 ha, barley 73,969 ha, maize 45,921 ha, potatoes ~84.6k (unit tagged "tonnes" but the magnitude is that of Chile's potato AREA, ~80-90k ha). Those levels match Chile's own 20th-century cereal belt (Central Valley / Araucanía; FAO-era Chilean wheat area sits at roughly 0.7-0.85 M ha through the 1950s-60s) and imply a temperate mid-latitude country of a few hundred thousand km2 of usable land — i.e. Chile proper, not a province and not a supranational aggregate. No sub-territory fold-up: a single Chilean province (Ñuble, Malleco, Cautín) would carry one-fifth to one-tenth of this wheat area, and no plausible union/empire scope exists for Chile in 1902-1960, so failure families (1), (3) and (5) are excluded. Boundary vintage (2): the label is ISO-routed "chl" from an ISO3-keyed panel, so it reports on Chile's national borders as understood at compilation; nothing in the level suggests older or newer borders. Our period splits (4) are all pre-1902 (1810-1884, 1884-1899, 1899-1902) and the data begin exactly at 1902, so no split straddles the observed span. No entrepot concern — these are field crops grown on the reporting territory. The wiki page (reviewed, 2.1 kB, 5 biger-1995 citations, no TODOs) agrees and is not the load-bearing evidence. I decline verified_equal on one specific ground: the territory did NOT stay constant across 1902-1960 — Chile ceded Tacna to Peru under the 3 June 1929 Treaty of Lima (~16,000 km2, arid and agriculturally negligible, which is why the crop series show no step, but a territorial change nonetheless), and added the 1940 Antarctic claim. Small and irrelevant to these magnitudes, but a changed territory cannot be "equal", so best_available is the honest kind.

verdict.basis: The assertion routes Juan's "canada" crop-area/production series (1900-1948, 1574 rows) to CAN-1886-1949, a Dominion-of-Canada polity explicitly defined to exclude Newfoundland (which remained a separate Dominion until its 31 March 1949 accession, covered by the successor CAN-1949-2025). Statistics Canada's own crop series for this era report the actual Dominion of Canada (mainland provinces + territories), which is precisely this candidate's territory — Newfoundland, never part of Canada in this period, would not be folded into a Canadian agricultural series. The observed span (1900-1948) sits entirely inside the candidate's 1886-1949 boundary window, during which the external territory was stable (only internal reorganizations: Yukon 1898, Alberta/Saskatchewan 1905, Statute of Westminster 1931 — none altering the reporting extent). The neighbor_segments entry (1949-1960 -> CAN-1949-2025) confirms the split point is exactly the Newfoundland accession, consistent with the territorial boundary. Staple magnitudes (wheat ~7.9M ha, oats ~5.3M ha median) are plausible at continental-Canada scale, showing no discontinuity suggestive of a scope mismatch. The wiki page is status:draft (0 source_citations) so its claims are treated as hypothesis, but the core territorial fact (Newfoundland excluded until 1949) is well-established external history, independently corroborating the page rather than relying on it alone.

Mitchell's "United States of America" series for 1867-1958 (cotton lint, cotton seed, butter, beer of barley, tobacco — all mainland agricultural commodities) matches the standard continental-US + Alaska reporting convention, with clean neighbor-segment splits at 1866/1867 and 1958/1959 and no magnitude discontinuity flagged in the bundle. The candidate polity USA-1867-1959 (draft wiki, thin: 1 source citation) covers exactly this span. However the wiki itself notes Hawaii annexation (1898) and Spanish-American War overseas acquisitions fall mid-span with an ambiguous polygon scope, so territory was not strictly constant throughout — hence best_available rather than verified_equal, even though no better candidate exists and the agricultural data itself is unaffected by the overseas-territory ambiguity.

Mitchell's "japan" agriculture rows (barley, rye, sweet potatoes, wheat, rice paddy 1895-1944) plausibly reflect metropolitan Japan (home islands, ~370,000 km2) only, not the full empire polygon assigned to JPN-1895-1945 (~658,000 km2, a CShapes union of Japan+Taiwan+Korea+S.Sakhalin). This is exactly the sub-territory fold-up failure family: the label is narrower than the candidate's stated territory. Korea and Taiwan are tracked as separate WHEP polities (KOR/TWN), consistent with Mitchell reporting colonial Korea/Taiwan under their own headings rather than folded into Japan's totals -- so metropolitan Japan is not literally the empire union, but there is no existing granular "metropolitan Japan 1895-1945" polity distinct from JPN-1895-1945 to reroute to (the JPN backbone series JPN-1800-1895 -> JPN-1895-1945 -> JPN-1945-1952 -> JPN-1952-2025 has no such split), and the wiki page's own 'Data caveats' section already documents this exact mismatch explicitly and with the correct reasoning (370k vs 658k km2), which is a defensible, already-established design choice rather than an oversight to fix via new_polity. Web search on Mitchell's IHS table structure was inconclusive (could not directly confirm the per-source convention), so this rests on general knowledge of colonial-era statistical reporting practice plus the wiki's own (draft but specific, non-circular-feeling) reasoning and the DB's own KOR/TWN separation as corroborating structure. Because the reporting territory (metropolitan Japan) is narrower than the candidate's full-empire territory, this cannot be verified_equal even though the metropolitan scope itself was roughly constant across the span -- best_available is the honest label given no better existing route.

review.basis: I worked from the raw source rows first (/home/usuario/Nextcloud/whep/layer_b/consolidated_layer_b.parquet, source=mitchell, country=japan, 1112 rows 1895-1944). NOTE the bundle's staple_magnitudes are misleading: each item has 49 ha rows AND 49 tonnes rows, and the bundle took the median of the POOLED values while labelling it "ha" (hence "rice, paddy median 4,093,000 ha", n=98). The true ha medians are rice paddy 3,068,000; rye 641,000; barley 530,000; wheat 487,000; sweet potatoes 283,000. A rice area of ~2.8-3.2M ha is metropolitan Japan (naichi) exactly — the empire would be ~5.2M ha, since the same Mitchell source carries 'korea' (rice 1,499,000 ha median) and 'china, taiwan province of' (614,000 ha) as SEPARATE country labels, routed to KOR-1800-1945 and TWN-1895-1945. So no combined/empire reporting and no double-count. Continuity settles it: the rice-area series runs 2,615,000 (1887) -> 2,762,000 (1895) -> 3,156,000 (1941) -> 2,869,000 (1945) -> 3,004,000 (1952) -> 3,308,000 (1960), with no step at either 1895 (Taiwan acquired) or 1945 (all colonies stripped); an empire-scope series would have had to fall ~40% in 1945. The reporting territory is therefore Japan proper (~382,000 km2 incl. Karafuto) for the entire span, while candidate JPN-1895-1945 "Japanese Empire" carries a constructed union polygon of ~658,000 km2. The label is NARROWER than the candidate, so this cannot be verified_equal; but JPN-1895-1945 is the only Japan row covering 1895-1944 and its colonies already have their own rows, so it is the correct destination — best_available with a scope caveat. The draft wiki page reaches the same caveat independently ("represents metropolitan Japan only... the empire polygon overstates the geographic coverage"); I note that as agreement, not as my evidence. Separately, the 'rye' series (641,000 ha, ~1.0M t, ~1.4 t/ha, falling from 687k ha in 1900 to 504k in 1944) cannot be rye — Japan grew essentially none; these are Mitchell's naked-barley (hadaka mugi) figures mapped to the 'rye' item, an item-mapping defect, not a territorial one.
review.wiki_note: Quantified confirmation the page lacks: Mitchell's Japan rice-paddy AREA runs 2.76M ha (1895) to 3.16M ha (1941) with no break at 1895 or 1945 (2.87M in 1945, 3.00M in 1952), proving the series is naichi-only across the whole imperial span; Mitchell reports Korea (1.50M ha) and Taiwan (0.61M ha) under separate country labels, so there is no double-count risk against KOR-1800-1945 / TWN-1895-1945. Data-quality finding: the Mitchell 'rye' series for Japan (~641,000 ha, ~1.0M t) is not rye — Japan grew essentially none — it is naked barley (hadaka mugi) mis-mapped to the rye item. Also note the intake bundle's staple_magnitudes for this key pool ha and tonnes rows into one median and label the result "ha".

source_convention.convention: Mitchell's Japanese cereal tables report wheat, barley and NAKED barley (hadaka mugi); the naked-barley column is ingested into layer B under the item 'rye'. Japan produced essentially no rye, so 'rye' rows for Japan (~640k ha, ~1.0M t, ~1.4 t/ha) must be read as naked barley.
source_convention.evidence: Mitchell source rows for japan show rye area 687,000 ha (1900) declining to 504,000 ha (1944) at ~1.4 t/ha, alongside barley 640,000 -> 424,000 ha; agronomically Japan's rye area was negligible while naked-barley area was of exactly this magnitude and trend.

verdict.basis: The assertion routes Juan's "hungary" agricultural series (1851-1917, 1003 rows) to HUN-1800-1918 (Kingdom of Hungary/Transleithania, area 325,421 km², area including Croatia-Slavonia, Transylvania, Vojvodina, Military Frontier). The candidate's draft wiki page claims (citing Mitchell IHS) that "Hungary" pre-1918 consistently means this full Transleithania territory throughout. Data magnitudes support the large territory for the bulk of the span: wheat area rises from ~2.0M ha (1868) to ~3.7M ha (1900s-1910s), consistent with 325k km²; a sharp drop to ~1.04-1.08M ha/tonnes in 1919-1920 lines up with the Trianon truncation to ~93k km² core Hungary, confirming the territory held constant through 1868-1917 and confirming successor routing (HUN-1918-1920) is correctly scoped. However, only 5 pre-1868 years are present in the data (1851, 1853, 1854, 1857, 1859 — 29 of 1003 rows, ~3%), with a 9-year data gap spanning exactly the 1867 Ausgleich. Web research confirms that from 1849-1868 Croatia-Slavonia was administratively attached to Austria (not Hungary) and the Vojvodina of Serbia/Banat of Temeschwar was a separate autonomous crownland directly under Vienna; these territories only rejoined the Kingdom of Hungary in 1867-1868. This means the reporting territory implied by "Hungary" for the sparse 1851-1859 rows was very likely narrower than the 325,421 km² Transleithania figure used for the 1868-1917 bulk of the series — a genuine mid-span territorial change the draft wiki page does not address, contradicting its blanket claim of constant Transleithania definition across the whole 1851-1917 span. No narrower "Hungary proper" polity exists in the database to reroute those 29 rows to, and they are a small minority of the assertion's rows, so confirm is still the best available action for the whole span, but confirm_kind must be best_available (not verified_equal) given the documented pre-1868/post-1868 territorial discontinuity for part of the span.
verdict.wiki_note: The page's claim that Mitchell's "Hungary" pre-1918 label follows constant Transleithania boundaries (~325k km²) throughout is only reliably true from 1868 onward. From 1849 to 1867/68, Croatia-Slavonia was administratively attached to Austria (not Hungary) and the Voivodina of Serbia & Banat of Temeschwar was a separate autonomous crownland under direct Vienna rule — both rejoined Hungary only with the 1867 Ausgleich (Croatia-Slavonia's return completed 1868). The data itself has a 9-year gap (1860-1867) straddling exactly this transition, so only 29 of 1003 rows (years 1851, 1853, 1854, 1857, 1859) fall in the ambiguous pre-1868 period where "Hungary" may denote a narrower territory than the candidate's 325,421 km². No narrower polity exists to reroute those rows to, so confirm remains best_available for the whole span, but the page should not claim territorial constancy across the full 1851-1917 range.

verdict.basis: Assertion routes Mitchell's "south africa" label (1910-1960, 938 rows) to ZAF-1910-2025 (Union/Republic of South Africa). The wiki page (reviewed, 3 citations) confirms the Union formed 31 May 1910 from Cape+Natal+Transvaal+Orange River colonies, area ~1.221M km², with South West Africa (Namibia) tracked separately under NAM-1920-1990 — so "South Africa" as a label denotes exactly the Union's own territory, not a sub-unit or a broader entity. No boundary changes occurred to the Union's territory across 1910-1960 (the 1961 Republic declaration was a status change only, occurring after the observed span, with no territorial effect). Neighbor segments show the pre-1910 predecessor chain (CAP-1800-1895, CAP-1895-1910) feeding into ZAF-1910-2025 at exactly the Union's formation date, confirming continuity of the reporting territory across the split boundary. Staple magnitudes (maize ~2.17M ha, wheat ~455k ha) are national-scale figures consistent with the full Union, not a province — corroborating that this is genuine national-level reporting rather than a sub-territory like the Natal-label case the page separately documents (which the page itself flags as a ~13x sub-territory approximation, a different alias/label than the one being verified here). No annexation, cession, or occupation affected South Africa's national territory 1910-1960, so the reporting territory equals the candidate's and stayed constant throughout.

Mitchell's Turkish cereal-acreage series (wheat ~3.83M ha, barley ~1.8M ha, oats ~265k ha, maize ~585k ha, potatoes ~75k ha medians, 1920-1960) is consistent in magnitude with the Republic of Turkey's post-Lausanne (1923) metropolitan territory throughout — no step-change is visible even at the 1939 Hatay annexation (~5,500 km², a small fraction of ~779,000-783,000 km² total), which is plausible since Hatay's farmland is a tiny share of national totals. Neighbor segments (TUR-1918-1920 before, none after since this is the terminal national polity through 2025) confirm the routing is the only reasonable candidate for 'Turkey' 1920-1960. However the span (1920-1960) does cross the 1939 Hatay annexation, a real territorial change per the polity's own wiki (predecessor chain and 'Territorial extent' section), so the reporting territory did not stay constant across the whole observed span even though no visible break shows up in the crop data.

review.basis: Numbers first: the staple areas (wheat median 3.83M ha, barley 1.81M ha, maize 0.59M ha, oats 0.27M ha, potatoes 0.075M ha; total cereals ~6.5M ha) imply a territory with roughly 8-10M ha under crops. That is the scale of Republican Anatolia+Thrace (~780,000 km² = 78M ha, i.e. cereals ~8% of land area), and matches the known trajectory of Turkish wheat area rising from ~2.5-3M ha in the late 1920s to ~7M ha by 1960 — a median near 3.8M ha over 1920-1960 falls out naturally. It is far too small for any Ottoman-scope reading: the immediately preceding sibling TUR-1913-1914 carries 1,785,218 km² (Ottoman Asia + Arab provinces), whose cereal base (Iraq, Syria, Hejaz, Yemen) would push wheat+barley well above these levels, so the label is not carrying an imperial aggregate and there is no combined-reporting or entrepot problem (crop area cannot be re-exported). Nor is it a sub-territory fold-up: no single Turkish vilayet/province could account for 3.8M ha of wheat. The neighbor segments confirm the split structure is respected — the source's Ottoman-era years route to the pre-1913/1913-14/1914-18/1918-20 rows, and only 1920-1960 lands here. So the routing to TUR-1920-2025 is right. It is best_available rather than verified_equal for two territorial changes inside the observed span: (a) 1920-1922 the row's territory was not yet the Lausanne territory — western Anatolia was under Greek occupation, Thrace and the Straits under Allied control, and the Lausanne borders only date from July 1923; (b) Hatay (~5,500 km², ~0.7%) was annexed from French Syria in 1939 and is inside the span. Neither is visible as a step in the magnitudes, which is expected at that fraction, but a territory that grew mid-span cannot be called equal to any single polygon. The candidate wiki page (draft, 4.5KB, 8 citations to biger-1995/COW) states the same Lausanne/Hatay facts; I used it only as corroboration of dates already independent of the arithmetic, and the scope conclusion rests on the magnitudes and the sibling areas, not on the page.
review.wiki_note: The page's territorial-change discussion inside this row covers only Hatay 1939; it should also note that the row's first years (1920-1922/23) pre-date the Lausanne borders — western Anatolia was under Greek occupation and Thrace/the Straits under Allied control until 1922-23 — so any 1920-1922 figures under this row are not on the polygon's 1923 vintage either.

verdict.basis: Mitchell's 'Algeria' series (1919-1960, 832 rows, wheat/barley/oats/potatoes acreages plus livestock counts) sits entirely inside candidate DZA-1919-1962's span (1919-1962), which per CShapes 2.0 and the polities_database.csv represents the stable French colonial Algeria territory (departments + Territoires du Sud) with no annexation, cession, or partition recorded between 1919 and 1962 (the only later change is independence in 1962, after the observed data ends in 1960). The neighbor_segments show the same routing pattern holding cleanly across the prior period splits (1860-1885, 1886-1901, 1902-1918), each mapping to the correspondingly-dated DZA-* polity, which supports that Mitchell reports on a consistent 'colonial Algeria' territorial basis rather than switching scope. Staple magnitudes (wheat ~1.33M ha, barley ~0.98M ha, oats ~0.17M ha, potatoes ~28k ha, asses ~332k head) are plausible in scale for the whole of colonial Algeria's cereal-growing north, not for any narrower sub-unit, so there is no sub-territory fold-up concern. The wiki page (draft, thin, 2 citations) documents the CShapes-derived boundary and predecessor/successor chain but offers no independent territorial verification beyond polygon provenance; it is treated as a hypothesis, not evidence — the confirm rests on magnitude/continuity reasoning plus general knowledge that French Algeria's administrative/colonial extent did not change during 1919-1960 (the 1957 Saharan department reorganization was an internal administrative split, not a change in overall territorial extent). No entrepot, combined-reporting, or union-scope issues apply to this label.

Assertion covers Romania 1920-1939 (Juan production/area data, 790 rows, staples like barley ~1.59M ha, rye ~319k ha, potatoes ~429k ha) routed to ROU-1920-1940, the Greater Romania polity (296,000 km2) formed after Trianon (June 1920) and lasting until the three simultaneous 1940 territorial losses (Vienna Award, Soviet ultimatum, Treaty of Craiova). The observed span (1920-1939) falls entirely within the period of stable Greater Romania territory -- the losses that shrink the country all occur in mid-to-late 1940, after the last observed year. The wiki page (draft status but with 2 source citations and a documented, self-critical polygon-correction note fixing a prior Bessarabia omission) supports this: it explicitly states the ~295,000 km2 extent held from 1920 to 1940 and that the only territorial changes bracket this row (Trianon in, three 1940 cessions out). Staple magnitudes are plausible for a large mixed-agriculture country of this size (Romania was a major interwar cereal/oilseed exporter), consistent with the full Greater Romania footprint rather than a truncated one. Neighbor segments show clean adjacent period splits (ROU-1919-1920, ROU-1940-1947) with no overlap or gap. No sub-territory fold-up, union/empire scope, entrepot, or combined-reporting risk applies here -- "Romania" as a national statistical label straightforwardly matches the national polity. Territory was constant across the entire observed span, so verified_equal is warranted.

The candidate IND-1914-1937 is the whole British Indian Empire including Burma (4,894,456 km2, constant 1914-1937, per its wiki page's CShapes/COW analysis) versus the 1937-1947 successor at 4,227,508 km2 (Burma separated 1 Apr 1937). Directly inspecting data/external/before_1961.csv (Source=mitchell, iso3c=IND, item=Rice, paddy, unit=ha) for the observed span 1914-1936 shows a smooth series 30.8-33.7 Mha through 1928, then a sharp step to 27.4 Mha in 1929 (-19%) that persists (28-29 Mha through 1936) — crop-specific (wheat/barley/maize run smoothly across 1928/29) and yield-neutral, the signature of a scope change rather than a harvest failure. This exactly reproduces an already-recorded prior finding for the near-duplicate assertion india|mitchell|1915-1937 (in pipelines/polity-autoimprove/state/quarantine.csv), which attributed the 1929 break to Burma being dropped from Mitchell's reporting territory ahead of the 1937 political separation, and additionally flagged that Mitchell/Blyn's "India" agricultural series is really "British India" (directly-administered provinces), excluding roughly 38% of the Indian Empire's area held by princely states throughout — meaning neither segment is a strict full-territory match, only best-available. Given the same source, same label, an overlapping span, and an identical, independently reproduced magnitude break at 1928/1929, the correct routing for the observed 1914-1936 span is split_reroute: 1914-1928 to IND-1914-1937 (India-with-Burma, the candidate as routed) and 1929-1936 to IND-1937-1947 (India-without-Burma, eight years before our DB's own 1937 India/Burma split point). The candidate's wiki page itself only documents the CShapes/COW polygon history and says nothing about Mitchell's rice-reporting break or the princely-state exclusion, so this is new information for the page.
verdict.wiki_note: Mitchell's "india" rice-paddy area series (data/external/before_1961.csv) breaks from a smooth ~31-34 Mha (1914-1928) to a step-shifted ~27-29 Mha (1929-1936) with unchanged yield — a reporting-territory change (Burma dropped from the India label eight years ahead of the 1937 political separation this page documents), not a harvest event. Other crops (wheat, barley, maize) show no such break. This matches an independently-recorded finding for the overlapping assertion india|mitchell|1915-1937. Separately, Mitchell/Blyn's India agricultural series is conventionally "British India" (directly-administered provinces only), excluding princely-state output (~38% of this page's polygon area) throughout the page's whole 1914-1937 span — so even the pre-1929 segment is a best-available match to this page's full-Empire polygon, not a verified-equal one.

source_convention.convention: Mitchell's 'india' rice-paddy area/production series drops Burma from its reporting territory at 1929, eight years ahead of the DB's 1937 India/Burma political-separation boundary — visible as a ~19% yield-neutral step in 1928/1929 while other India crops (wheat, barley, maize) stay smooth. Rows dated 1929-1936 under the 'india' label should route to the no-Burma successor polity (IND-1937-1947), not the with-Burma candidate (IND-1914-1937), despite falling inside that candidate's nominal 1914-1937 span.
source_convention.evidence: data/external/before_1961.csv, Source=mitchell, iso3c=IND, item='Rice, paddy', unit=ha: 1927=31,755,000; 1928=33,700,000; 1929=27,421,000 (-18.6%); 1930-1936 stays 28.3-29.3M. Wheat/barley/maize show no comparable step across 1928/1929. Corroborates the independent finding already recorded against assertion india|mitchell|1915-1937 in pipelines/polity-autoimprove/state/quarantine.csv.

review.basis: Numbers first, from the raw matched rows and the underlying Mitchell extraction (/home/usuario/Nextcloud/WHEP_ERC 2025/Thesis/Alejandra/outputs/mitchell_data.csv, sheet 11-50.xlsx page_28_table_1 for India, page_30_table_1 for Burma). India rice area runs 31.2-33.7M ha across 1914-1936 and wheat area 11.5-14.6M ha (yield ~0.7 t/ha wheat, ~1.5 t/ha paddy) - these are undivided-India magnitudes: 13.6M ha wheat in 1936 is ~34M acres, the official all-India (British provinces PLUS princely states) figure, and the territory demonstrably includes the future Pakistan, since India wheat area only collapses 13.91M ha (1947) -> 8.81M ha (1948) when Pakistan splits off (Pakistan's own series is 4.06M ha in 1947, and 13.91-4.06 = 9.85 reconciles with post-partition India). So no union/fold-up problem on the subcontinent: the label is the whole Indian Empire minus one piece. That piece is Burma: Mitchell carries a full parallel Burma series in the same page block for exactly the same years (rice area 4.26M ha in 1914 rising to 4.93M in 1936, continuous 1900-1960), so "India" here excludes Burma. The candidate's polygon does not: the wiki page documents 4,894,456 km2 for 1914-1937 versus 4,227,508 km2 for the 1937-1947 successor - the ~667k km2 difference IS Burma. Continuity confirms the basis never moves at our split boundaries (rice area 30.76M ha 1913 -> 31.21M 1914; 29.26M 1936 -> 29.37M 1937), so no split_reroute is warranted and no better-fitting existing polity exists for 1914-1936 (IND-1937-1947 is the right territory but the wrong years). Verdict: confirm, but best_available - the reporting territory is the candidate minus Burma (~14% of its area), and WHEP already carries MMR-1885-2025 covering these years, so the India polygon double-claims Burmese ground exactly as it did Portuguese/French India before the issue-84 fix. Two pipeline artefacts noted: the bundle's staple_magnitudes pool units (n=46 = 23 'ha' area rows + 23 'tonnes' production rows), so "rice, paddy median 34,557,000 ha" is not an area figure and should not be used as one; and Mitchell India wheat production for 1906-1908 (83-115M tonnes) is a unit error in the extraction, outside this span but in the same series.

source_convention.convention: Mitchell's pre-1947 "India" agricultural series is undivided British India INCLUDING the princely states and the future Pakistan/Bangladesh, but EXCLUDING Burma, which Mitchell tabulates as its own country series continuously from 1900. The basis is constant across 1913/14, 1936/37 and only breaks at 1947/48.
source_convention.evidence: Raw Mitchell extraction (11-50.xlsx): India rice area page_28_table_1 (31.2-33.7M ha 1914-36) vs Burma rice area page_30_table_1 (4.26-4.93M ha, same years, separate series). India wheat area 13.6M ha in 1936 = ~34M acres = official all-India incl. states; India wheat area falls 13.91M ha (1947) to 8.81M ha (1948) with Pakistan reporting 4.06M ha in 1947.

review.wiki_note: Mitchell's "India" for 1914-1936 EXCLUDES Burma: the same source block carries a separate Burma rice-area series (page_30_table_1, 4.26M ha in 1914 to 4.93M ha in 1936) running continuously 1900-1960, and India's own rice/wheat areas step not at all across 1936/37 (rice 29.26 -> 29.37M ha), which they would if Burma had been dropped at the 1937 separation. The label's territory is therefore this row's polygon MINUS Burma (~667k km2, the documented 4,894,456 -> 4,227,508 km2 gap), so any per-area normalisation using this row's 4.89M km2 understates intensity by ~14%. Related DB-level issue: WHEP carries MMR-1885-2025 as a separate polity over exactly these years, so IND-1914-1937's Burma-inclusive polygon overlaps it - the same class of double-claim that issue 84 fixed for Portuguese and French India, and worth carving out on the same grounds. Separately, the series does include the princely states and the future Pakistan (wheat area 13.6M ha in 1936 = ~34M acres, all-India incl. states; wheat only drops to 8.8M ha in 1948), so there is no sub-territory fold-up on the subcontinent side.

verdict.wiki_note: The page's 'Sourced claims' section asserts occupied Serbia (1941-1944, Nedić's Government of National Salvation under German military administration) 'covered roughly the same territory as the historical Serbian core' -- but the page's own headline area estimate for the WHOLE 1918-1945 span is ~88,000-90,599 km2, which is the POST-Balkan-Wars Serbia (with Kosovo/Macedonia, pre-Vojvodina). Confirmed via web search (Wikipedia, Territory of the Military Commander in Serbia): occupied Serbia 1941-1944 excluded Kosovo (annexed to Italian-sponsored Greater Albania), most of Vojvodina (western part to Hungary, Serbian Banat under separate German administration), and parts to Bulgaria (Vranje/Bosilegrad/Pirot area) -- i.e. it shrank back toward the smaller pre-1912 'old Serbia' core, NOT the ~88-90k km2 interwar Yugoslav-Serbia territory this row is polygon-proxied to. This is a genuine territorial discontinuity within the assertion's own observed span (1920-1944 includes the 1941-1944 occupation years), not just a hypothetical -- the page's 'roughly the same' phrasing actually undercuts its own area estimate rather than supporting it. No granular WHEP polity exists for wartime occupied Serbia, so routing 1941-1944 rows to SER-1918-1945 remains the best available option, but this is why confirm_kind=best_available rather than verified_equal, and it's a real open item beyond the page's existing oq-banovina-reorganization and oq-kosovo-vojvodina-boundary questions (neither of which mentions the WWII occupation shrinkage at all).
verdict.basis: The assertion span (1920-1944, 573 rows, iso_in_data=srb) sits entirely inside candidate SER-1918-1945's 1918-1945 period, and neighbor_segments show clean handoffs to SER-1913-1918 before 1918 and F248-1920-1947 (all-Yugoslavia) only for the single trailing year 1945 -- consistent with 'serbia' meaning the ~90,599 km2 Serbian sub-territory within Yugoslavia, not the whole federation (~255,000 km2), matching this draft page's own reasoning (already independently corroborated per its 2026-07-24 verification note for the near-identical 1921-1945/568-row assertion, which found no magnitude discontinuity at the 1929 banovina reorganisation). Staple magnitudes (rye ~207,800 ha, wine ~249,856 tonnes, tobacco ~16,000 ha) are plausible in scale for a ~90,000 km2 Balkan agricultural region and give no obvious sign of a step-change, though no year-by-year breakdown was available to rule one out specifically at 1941. However, web research confirms occupied Serbia 1941-1944 (Territory of the Military Commander in Serbia / Nedić government) lost Kosovo, most of Vojvodina and a Bulgarian-annexed strip -- a real, sourced territorial shrinkage inside this exact assertion's span that the page does not address correctly (it even asserts the opposite framing). Since no alternative existing polity covers wartime-occupied Serbia specifically, and the vast majority of the span (1920-1940) is uncontroversial, the routing to SER-1918-1945 remains the best available match, but per the routing rules a mid-span territorial change forces best_available rather than verified_equal.

The assertion routes "romania" labels in the Juan crops dataset for 1947-1960 (553 rows, 14 years) to ROU-1947-2025 via applied_alias. The candidate's wiki page (reviewed, 5 source citations, no TODO markers) documents that Romania's post-Treaty-of-Paris borders (northern Transylvania restored, Bessarabia/N.Bukovina/S.Dobruja permanently lost) were fixed from 1947 through the present (~238,000 km2), corroborated by CShapes 1946 polygon and modern GADM (~237,500 km2) and COW code 360 continuity. The observed span 1947-1960 falls entirely within this stable territorial period, well before any subsequent change (there was none until present). Neighbor segments show the prior period (1940-1946) is correctly split off to ROU-1940-1947, confirming the 1947 boundary is the right seam. Staple magnitudes (maize ~3.6M tonnes, sugar beet ~399,000 ha, potatoes ~693,000 ha) are plausible in scale for a 238,000 km2 mid-sized European agricultural economy, consistent with the whole-country reporting territory rather than a sub-region. No union/empire-scope, combined-reporting, or sub-territory fold-up issue applies here (Romania reports as itself, not part of a larger union). The page is reviewed and well-sourced, and its territorial narrative is internally consistent and externally plausible, so I treat it as corroborated rather than circular.

The assertion routes IIA "algeria" 1919-1945 rows to DZA-1919-1962 (French colonial Algeria, 12 Sep 1919 - 4 Jul 1962). The wiki page (draft, thin, 2 citations, no discussion of the agricultural reporting territory) is not itself evidentiary, but the bundle's source_conventions entry already supplies independent corroboration: source_stated_area_basis.csv shows IIA stating a separate ALGERIE area in six editions spanning the observed period (2,195,696 km2 vs our 2,318,386 km2 polygon, ratio 1.056, flagged agrees), and a structural check confirms IIA carries Algeria and France as distinct labels (567 vs 426 rows) throughout, ruling out the metropole-fold-up risk despite Algeria's administrative status as part of France. Staple magnitudes (olives ~96k tonnes, oranges/cotton at Mediterranean-belt scale) match Algeria's own agro-geography, not a combined France+Algeria total, and show no discontinuity across the 1919-1945 span or at the 1902/1919 predecessor boundary. The colonial territory itself was stable from the 1919 Sahara-annexation settlement (documented in the predecessor page) until the 1962 independence/Evian Accords -- no territorial change occurs within the observed 1919-1945 span or indeed across the whole 1919-1962 candidate period. This is a genuine confirm with constant reporting territory, not merely a routing default.

review.basis: Numbers first: rye median 1,000 ha is decisive against any France+Algeria fold-up — metropolitan France sowed on the order of 500,000-700,000 ha of rye in the interwar years, so a 1,000-ha rye series can only be a North African Mediterranean territory where rye is a marginal crop. The rest of the profile is internally consistent with colonial Algeria alone and with nothing narrower or broader: olives ~96,400 t (Algeria's interwar olive output was of this order; a single province or the Tell alone would be far smaller, metropolitan France's own olive crop far smaller too), oranges ~21,110 ha (Algeria's Mitidja/Oranie citrus belt; mainland France has essentially none), cotton lint 275 t with 480 t of seed — a token crop matching Algeria's failed interwar cotton experiments, not Egypt-scale or Sudan-scale output. Nothing in the level implies a territory larger or smaller than the northern-Algerian cultivated belt inside the candidate's colonial extent; the vast Saharan south simply contributes nothing agronomically, which is why per-km2 reasoning against the ~2.3M km2 polygon is uninformative and per-cultivated-area reasoning is the right test. No sub-territory fold-up (label is the colony, not a department or the Territoires du Sud), no entrepot issue (these are field crops, not transit commodities). Scope risk from Algeria's administrative integration into France is real in principle but excluded here both by the arithmetic above and by the bundle's already-verified source convention (IIA states a separate ALGERIE area in six editions and carries 567 algeria rows against 426 france rows as distinct labels). The split at 1919 corresponds to the Franco-Italian Saharan cession to Libya, and no further boundary change touched Algeria between 1919 and 1945, so the span is territorially continuous. Reason for best_available rather than verified_equal: the source's own stated area for ALGERIE (2,195,696 km2) is repeated unchanged from the 1909 edition through 1938, i.e. IIA never registered the 1919 reduction and its nominal reporting extent is ~5.6% below our 1919 CShapes polygon. The discrepancy is pure desert with no agricultural content, so the routing is right, but the reporting territory is not strictly identical to the candidate polygon.
review.wiki_note: The page describes only the polygon proxy — it gives area as "CShapes area = 213.51 degree-squared units" and leaves polygon_area_km2 null, with no description of the actual territory (three northern departments plus Territoires du Sud). It also does not explain why the period starts 12 Sept 1919: that is the Franco-Italian Saharan boundary convention transferring territory to Italian Libya, which is what the 224.74 -> 213.51 drop from the 1902-1919 period measures. Worth recording: IIA states an ALGERIE area of 2,195,696 km2 unchanged across its 1909, 1925, 1929, 1932, 1933 and 1938 editions, i.e. ~5.6% below our 1919 polygon (2,318,386 km2) — the source carried the pre-1919 Saharan extent forward and never updated it. Agriculturally immaterial (desert), but it means IIA-era Algerian series are reported on a slightly pre-1919 nominal extent.

verdict.basis:
The assertion routes IIA "spain" agricultural data (1909-1945, wine/sugar/hemp/cotton-seed/cocoons — items agronomically consistent with mainland Iberian agriculture) to ESP-1800-2025 by ISO+prior. The candidate's wiki page (draft, but backed by CShapes 2.0 polygon citations and a Biger 1995 area figure of 504,880 km2, consistent with metropolitan Spain's actual ~505,000 km2) documents Spain's European/metropolitan borders as stable since 1815, with CShapes recording a single static polygon 1886-2019. The observed span (1909-1945) falls entirely within this stable window — it includes the 1936-39 Civil War, which is economic disruption but not a territorial change (COW records no break). No combined-reporting, union-scope, or sub-territory fold-up risk applies: Spain in IIA yearbooks is metropolitan Spain reported as a unified country, with colonies (Spanish Morocco, Guinea, etc.) tracked as separate WHEP rows/labels, not folded into "Spain". Magnitudes (wine, sugar, hemp yarn, silk cocoons, cotton seed) are all plausible for mainland Spain's known agricultural profile. Territory is both equal to the candidate and constant across the whole observed span, so verified_equal applies.</basis>
