The candidate MEX-1848-2025 covers post-Gadsden-Purchase Mexico, with its territory (~1.957M km2, per Biger 1995 sourced in the wiki page) stable from 1854 until the minor 1960s Chamizal adjustment (transferred 1967, outside this span). The observed assertion span (1877-1960) falls entirely within this stable-border period, so "Mexico" under Mitchell's reporting is the same territory throughout. Staple magnitudes (sugar ~167k t, cacao ~2k t, cotton lint ~321,500 ha, beer of barley ~207k t, cotton seed ~161k t) are all plausible for national-scale Mexican agricultural production across this era, with no discontinuity suggesting a scope change (no combined reporting, no entrepot anomaly, no sub-national fold-up). The wiki page, though wiki_status=draft, is well-sourced (8 citations, mostly Biger 1995, an external gazetteer) and its border-stability claims are independently corroborated by well-known history of the US-Mexico boundary (Guadalupe Hidalgo 1848, Gadsden Purchase 1853/1854, no further change until Chamizal in the 1960s).

The label 'czech republic' in IIA is this source's rendering of the official name of the First Czechoslovak Republic (adopted 1920), and the routing family across the whole IIA series (CZE-1804-1918 for 1910-1918, F51-1918-1938 for 1919-1937, F51-1938-1945 for 1938-1944, F51-1945-1947 for 1945) shows the same label being tracked continuously across the polity's successive territorial forms, per the 'prior' route tag confirming an earlier verification already established this convention. For the 1919-1937 span specifically: rye area (the dominant staple) runs at a median ~1.04M ha, which drops to ~864k ha in the post-Munich/protectorate 1938-1944 segment routed to F51-1938-1945 -- a magnitude step consistent with loss of Sudetenland and Slovak territory at the 1938 boundary, not a jump suggesting our 1919-1937 figure is itself only a sub-territory (Czech lands alone would be materially smaller, and would not produce this before/after contrast aligned exactly with Munich). The candidate's wiki page (draft status, but with 8 source citations, CShapes- and COW-backed) documents Czechoslovakia's territory as stable from formation (1918-10-28) through the whole First Republic until the Munich Agreement (1938-09-30) -- the observed span 1919-1937 falls entirely inside that stable window, with no annexation, cession, or occupation intervening, so the territory both matches the candidate and was constant throughout the whole observed span.

review.basis: Numbers first. The obvious failure mode for a label reading "czech republic" (iso cze) in 1919-1937 is sub-territory fold-up — i.e. the source reporting only the Czech lands (Bohemia/Moravia/Silesia) while we route to the whole First Republic, or a modern-Czechia back-cast. The magnitudes refute both. Median rye 1,042,636 ha: interwar Czech lands alone carried roughly 0.65-0.75 M ha of rye (Bohemia ~0.45, Moravia ~0.2, Silesia small), with Slovakia plus Subcarpathian Ruthenia adding ~0.25-0.3 M ha; ~1.04 M ha is the whole-state figure and is far too large for the Czech lands or for modern Czechia (which even in the 1930s never approached 1 M ha of rye). The decisive tell is tobacco, unmanufactured at a median 8,526 ha: tobacco in interwar Czechoslovakia was a state-monopoly crop grown almost entirely in western Slovakia and Ruthenia, with essentially nil area in Bohemia/Moravia — a Czech-lands-only reporting unit would show a few hundred hectares at most, not 8.5k. Hops ~9,964 ha (Žatec/Saaz, Bohemian) and flax ~12.4k ha are consistent with the same whole-state totals. So the reporting territory under this label is the full Czechoslovak state, matching the candidate's documented extent (Bohemia+Moravia+Silesia+Slovakia+Ruthenia), and "czech republic" is a modern country-name normalization of the source's "Tchécoslovaquie/Czechoslovakia", not a component label. Continuity: 15 distinct years, n=32-34 observations per staple, medians stable enough that no scope break is implied inside the span; neighbor segments (CZE-1804-1918 before, F51-1938-1945 after) sit outside it. Not verified_equal, however, because the territory did not stay constant across the whole observed span: 1919 data predate the border settlement (Trianon-era Slovak-Hungarian frontier, the July 1920 Teschen partition, Hlučín, Vitorazsko/Valticko), and the assigned CShapes polygon is pinned to feature_year 1918, before those adjustments. The differences are small (order 1,000 km² plus the disputed Teschen basin) but real, so best_available is the honest kind. The wiki page is a draft; I used it only for the candidate's territorial definition, which is standard textbook geography, and the verdict rests on the crop magnitudes, not on the page.
review.wiki_note: Quantified corroboration the page lacks: IIA agricultural data filed under the normalized label "czech republic" for 1919-1937 covers the WHOLE First Republic, not the Czech lands — median tobacco area ~8,526 ha can only come from Slovakia/Subcarpathian Ruthenia (the Czech lands grew essentially no tobacco), and median rye ~1.04 M ha exceeds any Czech-lands-only total. Caveat for users: the row's polygon is pinned to feature_year 1918, i.e. before the 1920 Teschen partition and the final Slovak-Hungarian frontier, so 1919-1920 figures sit on a slightly different territory than the polygon.

verdict.basis: The observed span 1909-1945 sits entirely inside candidate USA-1867-1959 (1867-1959), during which the continental-US-plus-Alaska territory was unchanged (overseas acquisitions of 1898 are tracked as separate WHEP rows). The main risk for a plain 'United States of America' label in this era is combined reporting with dependencies (Hawaii, Puerto Rico, Alaska pre-1959, Philippines, Virgin Islands). I inspected pipelines/polity-autoimprove/state/iia_territorial_notes.csv, which shows IIA itself distinguishing 'usa' from 'us hawaii', 'us puerto rico', 'us alaska', 'us philippines', and 'us virgin islands' as separate labels (used for bilateral trade entries), indicating the source's own convention keeps dependencies out of the bare 'usa' label rather than folding them in. This is corroborated by the review ledger: the same plain label 'united states of america' from two other sources (juan, mitchell) was already independently confirmed correct against this same continental-US polity family across overlapping spans (2026-07-24, 2026-08-18), while a distinct label 'united states and dependent territories' is tracked separately (ledger 'fixed'/'correct' entries) — showing the pipeline already treats the combined-territory case as a different label needing different routing. The wiki page (draft, only 1 source citation, but substantively covers territorial extent) documents the continental+Alaska scope and correctly separates overseas territories into their own rows (oq-1898-overseas-territories), consistent with this reading. Staple magnitudes (cotton seed ~11.1M ha, sugar ~749k t, wine/raisins) are plausible for continental US agriculture in this period; I could not fully rule out a small Puerto Rico contribution to the 'coffee, green' figure, but the source's own territorial-notes convention and the ledger's prior confirmations for the same bare label outweigh that residual uncertainty.

source_convention.convention: IIA reports the bare 'United States of America' label as continental US territory only (mainland + Alaska); dependencies (Hawaii, Puerto Rico, Alaska in some earlier series, Philippines, US Virgin Islands) appear under their own distinct 'US <territory>' labels rather than being folded into the parent USA figure.
source_convention.evidence: pipelines/polity-autoimprove/state/iia_territorial_notes.csv lists 'usa' as a label distinct from 'us hawaii', 'us puerto rico', 'us alaska', 'us philippines', 'us virgin islands' across 1909-1938; ledger separately tracks 'United States and dependent territories' as a different label from plain 'united states of america'.

verdict.basis: The assertion routes Mitchell's "guyana" rows (383 rows, 1850-1960) to GUY-1800-2025 via ISO match. The candidate wiki page (draft status, but substantively sourced from Biger 1995) documents British Guiana's territory: the three Dutch colonies (Berbice, Demerara, Essequibo) united in 1831, with a subsequent boundary shift on the western Venezuela frontier from the 1899 Paris Arbitration (roughly 30,000-50,000 km² of interior jungle/savanna added/confirmed relative to the earlier Schomburgk Line). This falls within the observed 1850-1960 span. The page itself argues the shift doesn't matter for agricultural data because all recorded commodities (sugar cane, rice paddy, cattle, sheep) were produced on the Atlantic coastal strip and lower river valleys, unaffected by the disputed uninhabited western interior. Staple magnitudes (sugar ~110,000 t, rice ~41,000 t, sugar cane area ~29,000 ha) are consistent with a stable coastal plantation economy and show no sign of a magnitude discontinuity that would indicate a territorial reporting break. No independence-boundary issue arises since the observed span (to 1960) ends before Guyana's 1966 independence, so no sovereignty-status crossing occurs within the span. Because the western boundary did shift mid-span (1899), even though the change had no bearing on the reporting territory for these commodities, the candidate's overall territory was not literally constant across the whole span, so confirm_kind is best_available rather than verified_equal per the routing rule. The page already documents this boundary issue thoroughly (including a planned future split at 1899), so there is nothing new to add in wiki_note.

The assertion routes IIA "italy" 1919-1945 (382 rows, wine/hemp/silk cocoons/cotton) to ITA-1919-2025. The candidate's (draft) wiki page documents that this row's territory is the post-Saint-Germain Kingdom of Italy (Trentino/South Tyrol/Trieste/Istria annexed from Austria in Sept 1919) and that it stayed unchanged until the Treaty of Paris (Feb 1947), when Istria/Dalmatia went to Yugoslavia and a strip to France — a territorial change the page itself flags as an unresolved split candidate (oq-post-wwii-losses), but one that falls entirely AFTER the observed span (1919-1945). Within 1919-1945 the only events noted (fascist takeover 1922, WWII, 1943 armistice/German occupation, 1946 referendum) are non-territorial per the WHEP rule, so the reporting territory is constant across the whole observed span. The neighbor_segment shows 1909-1918 correctly routed to the predecessor ITA-1870-1919, consistent with the Saint-Germain split at 1919, supporting that the candidate boundary is not itself in question. Staple magnitudes (wine ~3.2M t, hemp yarn 75k t, silk cocoons 31k t) are all plausible for metropolitan Italy's known interwar agricultural output and not swollen by colonial territory (Libya, Italian East Africa, Albania), consistent with "Italy" here meaning the metropole proper rather than the empire — no entrepot/scope-inflation red flag. No combined-reporting or vintage-mismatch signal found. Because the candidate's own valid life (1919-2025) does change territory in 1947, this is not an evergreen verified_equal claim about the whole polity-code, but it IS verified_equal for the actually observed 1919-1945 span, since territory was constant and equal to the candidate's territory throughout that window.

review.basis: Numbers first: the staple levels are those of metropolitan Kingdom of Italy (~310,000 km2, ~41m people) and of nothing else. Wine median 3.20 Mt ≈ 32 Mhl sits squarely in the interwar Italian range (roughly 30-45 Mhl/yr) — an order of magnitude too large for any single region (Sicily or Piedmont alone are ~4-6 Mhl) and with no room for a colonial add-on, since Libya/Eritrea/Somaliland produced essentially no wine. Silk-worm cocoons 31.4 kt matches Italy as the world's largest non-Asian sericulture producer (~45-50 kt in the early 1920s falling toward ~25-30 kt in the 1930s), hemp fibre/yarn 75 kt matches Italy's position as Europe's dominant hemp grower, and cotton lint at only ~3,500 ha is exactly the token Sicilian/Calabrian acreage — a scope that included Italian Africa or Aegean possessions would not look like this, and a sub-national label could not reach these totals. So the label is metropolitan Italy, neither folded up from a province nor an empire aggregate; IIA (Rome) in any case tabulated Libya, Eritrea, Somaliland and the Dodecanese as separate entries. Scope, combined-reporting and fold-up checks therefore all pass. Why best_available rather than verified_equal: the candidate is one row spanning 1919-2025 whose territory demonstrably did not stay constant — Istria/Zara and the Tenda-Briga strip were lost in 1947, Trieste settled only in 1954/1975 — while the observed 1919-1945 data sit entirely on the pre-1947 (post-Saint-Germain, plus Rapallo/Zara 1920 and Fiume 1924) borders that the CShapes 1919 polygon depicts. The reporting territory equals the polygon vintage but not the polity's whole span, and even inside the observed span the border moved slightly (Fiume 1924; and IIA series for 1919-1921 may still rest on "vecchie provincie" only, a ~2% effect). Those are small quantities against these magnitudes, so the routing is right; it is just not an exact-equality claim.
review.wiki_note: Partial answer to oq-post-wwii-losses from the data side: the IIA series routed here run 1919-1945 and therefore lie wholly on pre-Treaty-of-Paris borders (Trentino/South Tyrol/Trieste/Istria/Zara included, Fiume from 1924), so for economic series the 1947 losses are a genuine boundary-vintage break rather than a cosmetic one, and a 1947 split would leave this source's whole span cleanly inside the earlier segment. Note also that Italy's colonies (Libya, Eritrea, Somaliland, the Dodecanese) and Albania are reported separately by the IIA, so this row's totals are metropolitan only.

verdict.basis:
The assertion routes Mitchell's "tanzania" agricultural series (1922-1960, cattle/coffee/cotton/maize/rice) to TAN-1922-1964, the Tanganyika Territory polity (1922-1961, mainland only, pre-Zanzibar-union). The wiki (draft status, 7 source citations from Biger-1995) documents Tanganyika as the British League of Nations mandate then UN trust territory administered continuously by Britain from 1922 through independence on 9 Dec 1961, with no substantial mainland border changes across that span and area ~945,087 km2 matching Biger's cited 364,900 sq mi (944,726 km2) for Tanganyika. The observed data span (1922-1960) falls entirely within the candidate's span (1922-1961) and predates the 1964 union with Zanzibar, so there is no combined-reporting risk (Zanzibar is a separate polity in Biger's account, colony 1860-1963). Staple magnitudes (cattle ~5.6M head, cotton ~25k t, coffee ~14k t, maize ~375k ha, rice ~62.5k ha) are plausible in scale for mainland Tanganyika's size and known agro-economy (large pastoral cattle sector, coffee highlands, cotton belt), not indicative of a narrower sub-territory or an entrepot label. Neighbor segments (TAN-1891-1920, TAN-1920-1922) show continuous predecessor coverage with no scope discontinuity flagged. Since the mandate/trusteeship territory is documented as constant throughout the whole observed span with no annexation/cession/occupation, and the candidate equals the source's reporting territory, this supports verified_equal rather than best_available.</basis>
<parameter name="checks">["scope", "vintage", "combined_reporting", "magnitude_continuity", "wiki_territory"]

The assertion routes 379 rows of Juan-source agricultural production data (bananas, beans, cassava, cattle, chickens, coffee, rice, maize, etc.) labeled "panama" for years 1912-1960 to PAN-1903-1979 (Republic of Panama, 75,517 km², independent from Colombia in 1903). The wiki page (draft status, but with 4 source citations and a documented independent investigation) explicitly tested the label-mapping question: it compares the FAO 1952 area ratio of the "panama"/"panama canal zone" concurrent entries (51.8x) against the actual area ratio of Panama to the Canal Zone (75,517/1,432 = 52.7x), a strong external cross-check confirming the "panama" label maps to the sovereign Republic and not to the ~1,432 km2 US-administered Canal Zone enclave (tracked separately as CZN-1903-1979). The page also ran a dedicated entrepot-hypothesis test on the coffee series specifically (checking planted-area consistency and cross-polity intensity ratios) and rejected transit/re-export contamination, finding Panama's coffee production intensity (0.97x median) consistent with genuine domestic Chiriqui-highlands production rather than canal-transit re-labeling. The staple magnitudes in this bundle (rice paddy 67,500t, coffee 1,000t, maize/beans in the thousands of hectares) are unremarkable in scale for a country of this size and are consistent with the wiki's independently-verified series. Panama's sovereign territory did not change over 1903-1979 (no annexations/cessions), so the reporting territory (Republic of Panama, land only, Canal Zone excluded) matches the candidate polity's territory constantly across the whole 1912-1960 observed span.

The assertion routes IIA's "indonesia" label (1909-1944, 375 rows, 32 distinct years) to IDN-1800-1945 (Dutch East Indies), area 1,877,243 km². The wiki page, despite status:draft, is well-sourced (5 citations, no TODO markers) and its central territorial claim is independently verifiable: CShapes 2.0 gwcode 850 shows an identical 1,877,243 km² geometry across every time-step from 1886 through 1945 (the only later change being the 1949 loss of western New Guinea). Since the observed span (1909-1944) falls entirely within that constant-geometry window, there is no annexation/cession/separation event inside the span that would break territorial constancy. The staple magnitudes (sugar raw centrifugal median 1.4M tonnes, cacao, cotton, sesame) are plausible for colonial-era Java/Outer Islands sugar and plantation-crop output and show no entrepot or agronomic-impossibility red flags. "Indonesia" as an IIA yearbook label for the pre-1945 period is the natural retrospective name for the Dutch East Indies as a whole, not a sub-territory (no evidence of Java-only or other component-only reporting), and area 1.88M km2 matches the full archipelago under Dutch rule, consistent with candidate. No combined-reporting or union-scope issue applies (unlike Sweden-Norway type cases) since Dutch East Indies was a single colonial administrative unit. Neighbor segment (1945-1945 -> IDN-1945-1949) confirms the row boundary aligns with the source's own natural year cutoff. Overall: reporting territory equals candidate's, and stayed constant through the whole observed span, so verified_equal is appropriate. The page's territorial argumentation (CShapes step analysis, correction of the erroneous 1889 Anglo-Dutch treaty claim) is corroborated externally via the same CShapes documentation reasoning it cites and is plausible on its face, not merely self-referential circular reasoning, so this counts as independent corroboration of geometry constancy rather than blind reliance on the draft status.

review.basis: I worked from the numbers first and then traced them to the raw source, and the routing fails the sub-territory fold-up test. The assertion's headline staple — "sugar raw centrifugal, median 1,415,377 t (n=36)" — is not a Dutch East Indies series at all: in the IIA harmonized extract (/home/usuario/3itkt6h41pb7jdan/2025-10-06_iia-dataframe/outputs/processed data/harmonized_data.xlsx) the ONLY sugar-cane production series for the Dutch archipelago is under country "dutch java and madura", and it matches the routed values digit-for-digit across the whole span (1909 1,234,104.7; 1913 1,431,854.2; 1930 2,772,443.1; 1933 617,059; 1944 84,200; 1945 25,000). Java+Madura is ~132,000 km2, 7% of candidate_meta.area_km2 = 1,877,243. Same for soybeans (1930 127,700; 1933 181,500; 1937 268,900 = java-and-madura verbatim; 1939 332,500 = java-madura 317,600 + bali-and-lombok 14,900, i.e. a two-island partial sum) and groundnuts (only java-madura and bali-lombok series exist in the raw; no DEI-wide one). Rubber is the clearest quantified damage: routed area 1939 = 615,700 ha = java-madura estate 235,400 + outer-provinces estate 380,300, whereas the source's own "dutch east indies" total for 1939 is 1,329,500 ha — the routed figure understates the polity's rubber area by 54%; for 1941-42 the routed values (242,300 / 243,800 ha) are Java-and-Madura alone, a ~5x understatement. Meanwhile other items in the same assertion (cotton lint, cacao, sesame, tea, tobacco, coffee) DO have genuine "dutch east indies" series. So "indonesia" here is not one reporting territory: the upstream layer-B country harmonization collapsed at least six distinct IIA reporting units — "dutch east indies", "dutch java and madura", "dutch east indies: outer provinces", "dutch sumatra", "dutch bali and lombok", "dutch java, madura and outer provinces" — into the single string "indonesia", with the survivor varying by item and even by year. That cannot be confirmed (it would attribute Java's output to the whole archipelago), cannot be fixed by a single reroute (some rows really are whole-DEI), and cannot be expressed as a split_reroute because the split is by series, not by year. The candidate wiki page (draft, 3,772 bytes, 5 citations) is accurate about the DEI's territory and I found nothing wrong in it; the defect is upstream of the polity DB, in label harmonization, so this belongs in quarantine for a human to resolve by re-deriving the assertion from the raw IIA country strings.
review.wiki_note: IIA data routed to this polity is NOT whole-Dutch-East-Indies: the upstream layer-B harmonization collapsed six distinct IIA reporting units into the label "indonesia". Sugar (median 1.42 Mt), soybeans and groundnuts are "dutch java and madura" only (~132,000 km2, 7% of this row's 1,877,243 km2); rubber area is an estate-only partial sum (1939: 615,700 ha routed vs the source's own DEI total of 1,329,500 ha, -54%; 1941-42 values are Java-Madura alone, ~5x low), while cotton, cacao, sesame, tea and tobacco do come from genuine "dutch east indies" series. Any use of this source's series under IDN-1800-1945 must be checked per item against the raw country string.

verdict.basis: The assertion routes Mitchell's "india" agricultural-statistics label (1893-1913) to IND-1893-1914, a national British-India polity whose CShapes-derived polygon (~4.8M km²) covers the whole subcontinent under British paramountcy, including princely/native states. The wiki page (wiki_status: draft, so treated as hypothesis not evidence) makes a careful, well-cited argument that the *external political boundary* was constant across 1893-1914 (Durand Line 1893 and McMahon Line 1914 were frontier delimitations of territory already under British control, not sovereignty transfers) - this is corroborated independently by standard historical accounts of both events, which I accept. However, independent web research on the source side (official "Agricultural Statistics of India" series, which Mitchell's international historical statistics compiles from) turns up a genuine scope caveat the wiki page does not address: the official annual agricultural-statistics series was compiled primarily for directly-administered British Indian provinces, with princely-state acreage largely absent or only partially/inconsistently included, whereas the candidate's polygon area (~4.8M km²) represents the whole British-paramountcy territory including princely states (which held roughly 40% of the subcontinent's area). This is a potential sub-territory fold-up: the source's reporting territory may be narrower (British India proper) than the candidate polity's full territory. There is, however, no separate WHEP polity for "princely India" to reroute to, so IND-1893-1914 remains the only available and reasonable match - this is a best_available confirm, not a verified_equal one, both because of this coverage caveat and because a ~20-year span crossing two frontier-delimitation events (1893, 1913) is not automatically "constant" without independent corroboration beyond the draft page's own say-so. Staple magnitudes (rice 29.9M ha, wheat 9.9M ha) are plausible in scale for greater British India inclusive of Burma, not clearly pointing to either scope reading on their own.
verdict.wiki_note: Official "Agricultural Statistics of India," the primary source underlying Mitchell's India series in this period, was compiled mainly for directly-administered British Indian provinces; princely/native-state acreage was largely absent or only partially and inconsistently reported (per Blyn-type reconstructions vs. later broader compilations like Kurosaki's). The candidate's CShapes-derived polygon (~4.8M km²) covers the whole British-paramountcy territory including princely states (~40% of the subcontinent's area). This is a potential source-narrower-than-candidate scope gap the page does not discuss; no separate "princely India" polity exists to reroute to, so this remains the best available match, but the acreage/production totals may understate true full-territory magnitudes and should not be treated as complete British-India-plus-princely-states figures.

verdict.basis: The candidate's wiki page documents CShapes 2.0 recording Senegal as a constant-area colonial territory (~195,995.8 km²) from 1886-01-01 through the Mali Federation transition, with boundaries unchanged even through the 1959 Federation entry/exit and independence in 1960 — i.e. the reporting territory (French colonial Senegal) was geographically constant across the entire assertion's observed span (1886-1959). This is a component colony under French rule, not the wider AOF federation: the source's magnitudes (groundnuts ~487,500 t, cattle ~393,000 head, rice paddy 50,000 ha, maize 18,000 ha) are plausible for Senegal alone — Senegal was AOF's principal groundnut producer, and these figures are far too small to represent the whole multi-colony AOF federation (which would show cattle/livestock in the millions and groundnuts spread across several territories). No annexation, cession, or boundary change occurred within the observed span per CShapes, so the territory is both correct in scope (Senegal proper, not AOF or a sub-unit) and constant throughout.

The assertion routes FAO 1952 "Italy" (1937-1951) to candidate ITA-1919-2025, our single continuous Italy row (1919-2025, no internal split). The span 1937-1951 straddles a real territorial change: the Feb 1947 Treaty of Paris, under which Italy ceded Istria/parts of Dalmatia to Yugoslavia and ~268 sq mi to France. FAO's country-level series for Italy in a given year almost certainly reflects that year's actual borders (pre-1947 larger Italy including Istria for 1937-1946 rows, post-1947 smaller Italy for 1947-1951 rows), consistent with normal yearbook practice of reporting current-year national territory. Since WHEP's own database does not split Italy at 1947 (the wiki page itself raises this exact issue as an unresolved open question, oq-post-wwii-losses, and explicitly declines to split), there is no alternative existing polity to reroute or split-reroute to — ITA-1919-2025 is the only and best available match for the whole 1937-1951 span. Staple magnitudes (grapes ~2.87M ha, meat ~278k t, milk ~2.45M t) are all plausible in scale for interwar/postwar Italy (pop. ~42-47M), giving no sign of a scope mismatch (e.g., no evidence data includes colonies or excludes/includes Istria inconsistently with the label). Because the reporting territory did NOT stay constant across the observed span (1947 cession), this cannot be verified_equal even though no better candidate exists — it is best_available. The wiki page (draft status, but substantive: 5623 bytes, 12 source citations, no TODO markers) already documents this exact territorial-change issue in detail, so there is no new information to add via wiki_note.

review.basis: Numbers first. The FAO 1952 "Italy" levels are metropolitan-Italy scale, and they exclude both the colonial empire and any sub-national fold-up. Grapes ~2,868 kha of vine area only makes sense for the whole peninsula under Italy's characteristic promiscuous/mixed vine culture (contemporary Italian vine area, specialised plus mixed, ran ~3.0-3.6 Mha against ~12 Mha arable in a 310,000 km2 country); no single region or island could carry that, and no colony could add to it (Libya/Eritrea/Somalia grew negligible vine). Horses+mules+asses ~770k head, meat ~278 kt and milk ~2,450 kt are likewise per-capita and per-km2 plausible for a ~43M-person peninsular economy, an order of magnitude too large for a province and with no empire-sized surplus. The decisive independent check is the bundle's own verified source convention: FAO 1952 "population total" for Italy 1937 = 42,372k, which matches the 1936 census of the Kingdom of Italy proper (42.4M) and excludes the ~2.5M of Libya/AOI and the Dodecanese — so the label is metropolitan Italy, not the Italian Empire, and not a combined reporting unit. Fold-up in the other direction is ruled out by the same magnitudes. Hence the routing to ITA-1919-2025 is right, and no other existing polity fits (the Dodecanese is separately carried as ITAEG-1912-1947, consistent with FAO reporting it apart). It is best_available rather than verified_equal for one reason only: the reporting territory did not stay constant across 1937-1951. The 1937 figures are on pre-war borders including Venezia Giulia/Istria, Zara and Fiume (~8-9,000 km2, ~3% of area, plus disproportionate viticulture), while the 1951 figures are on post-Treaty-of-Paris (1947) borders after the cessions to Yugoslavia and France and the loss of Trieste's disputed zone. Our database does not split at 1947 (the candidate's own page raises this as open question oq-post-wwii-losses), so a single polity cannot equal the reporting territory over the whole span; the discrepancy is small but real and the honest label is best_available. The candidate page (draft, 5.6 kB, 12 citations) documents this territorial history and I used it only for corroboration of the 1947 losses, not for the scope verdict, which rests on the magnitudes and the population cross-check.
review.wiki_note: FAO 1952 reports "Italy" as metropolitan Italy only: its 1937 total population of 42,372k matches the 1936 census of the Kingdom proper and excludes Libya/AOI and the Dodecanese (carried separately here as ITAEG-1912-1947). This bears on oq-post-wwii-losses: within this row the 1937 series is on pre-war borders (incl. Venezia Giulia, Zara, Fiume) while the 1951 series is post-Treaty of Paris, so cross-period series on this row are not on a constant territory even though the step (~3% of area, more in vine area) is too small to show as a magnitude break.

verdict.basis: The IIA 'philippines' label for 1909-1945 reports on the Philippine archipelago as a single reporting territory (American colony through 1935, then Commonwealth, occupied by Japan 1942-1945, all on the same land area). The candidate PHL-1800-2025 covers the whole span as one row with CShapes feature 840 (1898 vintage) carried through unchanged; the wiki explicitly argues the 1898 and 1946 sovereignty transitions did not change the archipelago's extent. Staple magnitudes (abaca/manila fibre ~324k ha, tobacco ~69k ha, raw centrifugal sugar ~441k tonnes) are all plausible, well-attested Philippine export-crop scales under the same land base, with no sign of a step change indicating a territorial scope shift, and no sub-territory or entrepot signature (Philippines is itself the producing territory for these staples, not a transit point). No existing polity subdivides the Philippines for this period, so PHL-1800-2025 is the only candidate and it fits. However the observed span includes the Japanese occupation (1942-1945), which the routing instructions explicitly flag as an event that breaks constancy even when land extent is unchanged, so this is best_available rather than verified_equal despite territory itself never changing.

The assertion's observed span is 1949-1960, entirely inside the window between Indian independence/princely-state integration (completed 1947-1949) and the next two territorial changes documented on the candidate's own wiki page: Goa's annexation from Portugal (Dec 1961) and Sikkim's accession (1975). Both post-date the observed span, so they are irrelevant to this specific assertion even though the wiki page (thorough, well-cited, despite being labeled 'draft') treats them at length as caveats for the row's LATER years. Within 1949-1960 India's sovereign territory was stable and there is no combined-reporting, union-scope, or sub-territory fold-up concern (Mitchell's 'India' label at this date plainly means the Republic of India, not a colonial-era British India aggregate — partition was already complete in 1947). Staple magnitudes (millet ~15.8M ha, sorghum ~15.5M ha, barley ~3.1M ha) are large-country-scale figures consistent with subcontinental India and continuous with the neighbor segment IND-1947-1949 immediately preceding this row, supporting no scope discontinuity at the 1949 boundary. Given the reporting territory equals the candidate's territory and was constant across the whole observed 1949-1960 span, this is verified_equal rather than best_available.

The candidate NGA-1914-1960 is colonial Nigeria formed by amalgamation of Northern and Southern Nigeria protectorates on 1914-01-01, running unchanged (per CShapes area, constant at 71.1 sq deg) until the 1961 Northern Cameroons incorporation — which falls after the observed data span ends (1959). Mitchell's "Nigeria" label for 1914-1959 is the standard national aggregate for this exact same territory. Staple magnitudes (cacao ~84,000 t, groundnuts ~297,000 t, cotton lint ~34,000 t, cattle ~2.9M head) are all plausible national totals for Nigeria's known colonial-era export profile, with no signs of entrepot inflation or sub-territory fold-up. Neighbor segments (NNI/SNI predecessor pre-1914, NGA-1960-1961 successor at 1960) confirm clean chain boundaries. The wiki page is reviewed status with 4 source citations (Biger-1995) and its territorial narrative is internally consistent and externally plausible.

review.basis: Numbers first: for a territory of ~923,000 km2 with roughly 20-35M people, the staples read as whole-colony aggregates, not a province and not an empire. Cocoa median 84,000 t matches Nigeria's known trajectory (~50k t in the 1930s rising past 100k t in the 1950s, the world's 2nd-3rd producer) and is far too large for any single Nigerian province or for the small Southern Cameroons plantations; groundnuts 297,000 t is the Kano/Northern trade at its documented scale; cotton lint 34,000 t and wild/plantation rubber 2,250 t are of the right order for the whole colony; cattle 2.9M head fits the northern herd (Nigeria ~6M by 1960), and would be geologically/agronomically absurd for the southern colony alone. So the implied scope is "all of Nigeria" — the candidate's scope — with no sub-territory fold-up and no entrepot signature (all five staples are things Nigeria genuinely produced). Continuity supports the same reporting basis: the label runs unbroken 1889-1959 across our 1914 split into NGA-1886-1914, i.e. Mitchell already treats pre-amalgamation Northern+Southern+Lagos as one "Nigeria" series, so the 1914 amalgamation is a purely administrative event with no reporting-territory step, and 46 distinct years with n=45-46 on cocoa/cotton/rubber indicates a single continuous compilation. The reviewed wiki page (2.8KB, 4 citations to biger-1995, no TODOs) independently agrees on the territory and dates, and I did not need it to reach the verdict. Why best_available rather than verified_equal: the reporting territory did not stay constant across 1914-1959. British Cameroons (~87,500 km2, our own separate polity BCM-1916-1961) came under British administration in 1916 and under mandate from 1922, sat inside the Nigerian customs area, and its returns were routinely folded into Nigerian Blue Book/trade statistics, while the candidate's CShapes-475 1914 polygon excludes it. That is roughly a 9% area expansion mid-span, so no single polity equals the reporting territory; NGA-1914-1960 is nonetheless the best available routing and the distortion to these staples is small (Cameroons' cocoa/banana output was a minor fraction). I could not read Mitchell's own territorial footnotes, hence medium rather than high confidence.
review.wiki_note: Mitchell's "Nigeria" series for 1922-1959 very likely includes British Cameroons (Northern and Southern Cameroons, ~87,500 km2), which was administered with Nigeria and inside its customs area, and whose returns were folded into Nigerian colonial statistics; the CShapes-475 1914 polygon used here excludes it, so the reporting territory is ~9% larger than the polygon from 1922 on. Flag a double-count risk against any independent series routed to BCM-1916-1961.

verdict.basis: Uruguay is a small, long-stable South American republic whose borders have not changed since independence in 1828 (Treaty of Montevideo, buffer state between Argentina and Brazil) -- no annexations, cessions, unions, or occupations occurred in 1860-1960 that would alter its reporting territory. The wiki page (draft status, but citing Biger 1995 and COW state-system data, 3 citations) documents stable borders throughout the polity's 198-year span, consistent with COW ccode=165 continuity. Mitchell's 'Uruguay' label for 1860-1960 has no plausible sub-national or union-scope ambiguity (unlike Sweden-Norway, Austria-Hungary, etc.) since Uruguay was never part of a larger reporting union and has no internal component large enough to be separately reported by Mitchell's world tables. Staple magnitudes (wine ~17,000t, beer ~7,760t, meat ~289,000t, milk ~556,000t, flax ~183,500ha) are all plausible in scale for a small agricultural/pastoral nation of Uruguay's size (~176,000 km2, per Biger 1995) and show no discontinuous jumps suggesting a territorial scope change across the observed decades. No known failure family (union scope, boundary vintage, combined reporting, sub-territory fold-up, entrepot re-export) applies: Uruguay is not a component of a larger polity, was not combined with another state under this label, and its livestock/dairy/grain products are indigenous to its own pampas, not re-exports through a transit port.

The IIA label "China, Taiwan Province of" is a modern administrative label (post-1949 ISO convention) retroactively applied by IIA/FAO to Taiwan-island agricultural statistics for the observed years 1909-1944. The candidate TWN-1895-1945 (Formosa, Japanese Taiwan) covers exactly this island territory (~36,193 km²), stable from the 1895 Treaty of Shimonoseki cession through the 1945 retrocession, with no boundary change in that interval — a single colonial administration (Taiwan Governor-General's Office) that reported its own agricultural/trade statistics separately from the Japanese home islands. The draft wiki page is well-documented (6 source citations, Biger 1995 area figure of 35,987 km² closely matching CShapes' 36,193 km², explicit sub-territory note distinguishing TWN from the much larger JPN-1895-1945 empire aggregate) and its territorial claim is independently corroborated by staple magnitudes: sugar raw centrifugal median 500,724 tonnes and tea 40,832 ha are consistent with well-documented Japanese-era Taiwan being a major colonial sugar and tea producer at that scale, not plausible for a fractional sub-region or for the whole Japanese Empire. No evidence of a mid-span territorial change (island extent fixed 1895-1945), so the whole observed span (1909-1944) maps to one constant, correctly-scoped candidate polity.

The candidate MAR-1911-1958's own wiki page contains a "Scope correction" (2026-07-24) establishing, from a prior assertion review of a different source (Mitchell), that this row's attached polygon is French Morocco specifically (350,268 km²) and NOT the whole Sherifian Empire/Morocco proper (~446,000 km², which also includes Spanish Morocco tracked separately as SMO-1912-1956 plus Tangier and Ifni). The IIA assertion here (rows=338, years 1911-1945, agricultural items: flax, tobacco, grapes, cotton seed, linseed) matches that same known pattern for international statistical-yearbook sources of this era: French and Spanish protectorate administrations each ran their own statistical services and reported separately to international bodies like the IIA, so a bare "Morocco" label most plausibly denotes the French zone, consistent with the candidate's actual (French-zone) territory. Staple magnitudes (grapes 24,000 ha, flax 17,000 ha, cotton seed 385 ha, linseed 11,000 tonnes) are modest and plausible for the French zone's arable agricultural belt (Gharb, Chaouia, Doukkala), not inflated in a way suggesting the whole protectorate+Spanish zone was folded in. Web search could not directly confirm IIA's own French/Spanish Morocco reporting split (no digitized-yearbook-level detail surfaced), so this rests on analogy to the already-established convention for a comparable source (Mitchell) rather than direct external verification of IIA itself. One year (1911) predates the Treaty of Fez (1912) establishing the protectorates, meaning for that single year "Morocco" would have denoted the still-unified sovereign sultanate rather than the French zone alone — a minor territorial-scope wrinkle within the 35-year span that, combined with the reliance on an analogous-source convention rather than direct IIA-specific confirmation, keeps this at best_available rather than verified_equal.

review.basis: Numbers first: I pulled the 340 IIA rows for label "morocco" from the raw consolidated source (/home/usuario/Nextcloud/WHEP_ERC 2025/Sources/datasets/processed_datasets/consolidated_datasets/mitchell/mitchell_juan_iia.csv) and from the layer-B parquet. The slice is minor crops only (flax 5k->52k ha 1915-1945, linseed 3-24k t, grapes 5.6k->26k ha, olives 50-105k t, wine area 0.8k->23k ha, oats 35-53k ha, cotton a few hundred ha). Working blind from levels: a territory with ~7M people and a few hundred thousand km2 of which the plains (Gharb, Chaouia, Doukkala, Haouz) carry all commercial cropping — i.e. exactly French Morocco (candidate polygon measured 350,268 km2, cshapes feature 600 @1912). The settler-driven series (vineyards 0.8k ha in 1922 growing tenfold by 1937; wartime flax expansion to ~50k ha in 1940-45) are French-zone phenomena; the Rif/Spanish zone had negligible commercial viticulture or fibre flax. Scope check both directions: the label is not a sub-territory of the candidate (no province/district reading), and the upward risk (French+Spanish combined) is immaterial to the levels — fao1952 in the same DB reports French vs Spanish Morocco separately for 1939-51 and the Spanish zone runs ~5-12% of the French one (sheep 595k vs 9,149k; cattle 254k vs 1,762k; population 1937 6.8M French zone), and no "spanish morocco"/"tanger" label exists anywhere in the IIA source, so the Spanish zone was simply not an IIA reporting unit. No entrepot/re-export issue (all field crops), no boundary-vintage step, and no continuity break at any of our period splits (the label's own span 1909-1945 sits entirely inside the candidate's 1911-1958, and there is no rival Morocco row for these years; SMO-1912-1956 carries the Spanish zone's own 55 rows, so no double count). Why best_available rather than verified_equal: (a) I could not find external documentation of the IIA yearbook's Morocco footnote, so French-zone-only vs French-zone-in-practice remains an inference from magnitudes and from the source's own footnote table (state/iia_territorial_notes.csv carries "french morocco" tenure notes 1928-1945, indicating the yearbook's Moroccan unit is the French protectorate); (b) the reporting territory was not constant across 1911-1945 — French statistical coverage tracked pacification, expanding from the coastal plains in the 1910s to the full protectorate only after 1934, which is visible as the 1915-1921 series being an order of magnitude below the 1930s levels for flax and grapes. The routing is right; the equality is approximate.
review.wiki_note: Data-quality break in the IIA slice, not in the territory: tobacco is internally consistent 1930-33 (92-222 ha, 141-314 t, ~1.5 t/ha) but from 1934 the area column collapses to 0 or exactly 1,000 ha while production jumps to 17,600-103,400 "tonnes" (up to 100 t/ha, agronomically impossible) — a unit/scale misparse from 1934 onward (likely quintals and '000 ha), which also affects flax 1945 (41,000 ha, 4,100 t). Also worth recording: the IIA rows for this polity are minor crops only (fibres, oilseeds, fruit, tobacco); Morocco's cereals and livestock in the same consolidated file come from Mitchell, so the two sources are complementary rather than overlapping here.

verdict.basis: The assertion routes Mitchell's "zimbabwe" 1901-1952 series (cattle, maize, cotton, groundnuts, tobacco, goats, sheep) to ZWE-1900-1953 (Southern Rhodesia). The candidate's wiki page (draft, but backed by 4 citations to biger-1995, an external gazetteer) documents that Northern Rhodesia was separated from the Southern Rhodesia administrative unit by 1900 (CShapes cowcode=552 vs 551), and that CShapes records no territorial change for cowcode=552 across the entire 1900-1953 span (single polygon, area≈390,610 km2 per the polities_database.csv SRH-1953-1964 sibling row which shares the same cowcode/area). The 1923 shift to self-governing colony status was constitutional only, not territorial, per the page's own sourced claim. The neighbor_segments field shows the immediate post-span years (1953-1960) already route to SRH-1953-1964, the Federation-era Southern Rhodesia row with the identical cowcode 552 and area, confirming continuity of the same reporting territory across the WHEP row boundary rather than a change. Magnitudes (cattle ~2.3M head, maize ~110k t, tobacco ~3,550 t) are plausible for the settler-agriculture economy of colonial Southern Rhodesia alone (not requiring Northern Rhodesia's copper-belt territory to explain scale) and show no discontinuity pattern suggesting a scope change mid-span. Mitchell's African historical statistics conventionally report "Rhodesia/Zimbabwe" as Southern Rhodesia distinct from Northern Rhodesia for this period, consistent with the routing. No sub-territory fold-up or entrepot risk applies (this is the primary agricultural/pastoral producer territory itself, not a transit hub). Given both the polygon-family cross-check (same cowcode 552, same area 390,610 km2 recurring in SRH-1953-1964) and the external biger-1995 citations independently corroborate a constant Southern Rhodesia territory 1900-1953, this is a solid confirm with verified_equal.

Assertion routes FAO1952 "United States" 1931-1951 data to USA-1867-1959, whose territory (continental US + Alaska, ~9.4M km2) was stable across the entire 1867-1959 span with no territorial change occurring within the observed 1931-1951 window (Hawaii/Alaska statehood in 1959 is a status change, not territorial, and postdates the span; Philippines/Puerto Rico/Guam are tracked as separate WHEP rows and are not part of this reporting label). The bundle's source_conventions entry (independently verified 2026-08-14 against consolidated_layer_b.parquet) cross-checked FAO1952's "population total" indicator for the US at 128,961k in 1937 against the accepted continental US population (~128.8M), confirming the reporting territory is the mainland+Alaska US, not a broader or narrower unit. No magnitude discontinuity or scope ambiguity found for this label in this era (unlike Yemen/USSR-type combined-reporting cases). The wiki page is draft status with only 1 (self-referential, CSV-derived) source citation, so it is not itself treated as evidence, but its territorial narrative is independently corroborated by well-documented US history and the bundle's own population magnitude check.
